definition_zh: 隧道；地道；坑道；挖隧道；凿通
definition_en: a long underground passage dug through a hill, under a city or under the sea, or to dig such a passage
core_image: 在大山或海底里打洞，让道路笔直穿过去
scene: 山体挡住了新公路的去路，工程队决定直接从山腹里穿过去。The workers began to tunnel through the mountain last spring.
sceneCN: 这里 tunnel 是动词「挖隧道、凿通」（第 5 个义项：挖掘穿越通道）；句意为工人们去年春天开始在这座山中挖隧道。

pos.zh: 名词：隧道；地道；坑道
动词：挖隧道；凿通；在……下面挖通道

collocations.phrase: light at the end of the tunnel
collocations.zh: 苦尽甘来的迹象；隧道尽头的光明

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「挖隧道的人（或动物）」，美国拼写常作 tunneler
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「隧道工程；挖掘隧道（的行为）」

senses.title: A passage through a hill or mountain
senses.definition: an artificial underground passage dug through a hill or mountain for a road or railway
senses.definitionCN: 为公路或铁路在山体中开凿的人工地下通道
senses.example: The train slowed down as it entered the long tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 火车驶入那条长隧道时减了速。
senses.why: The core image is a straight path pushed through what stands in the way; through a mountain, that path is a tube of stone.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是在阻挡之物中硬开出一条直路；在山体里，这条路就是一段石管。

senses.title: A passage under a city or road
senses.definition: an enclosed passage built under a city, a river or a busy road so that traffic can pass below
senses.definitionCN: 修建在城市、河流或繁忙道路之下，让车流从下方通过的封闭通道
senses.example: The subway tunnel runs beneath the busiest street in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 地铁隧道从这座城市最繁忙的街道下方穿过。
senses.why: The same tube moved under rivers and streets: the city sits on top, traffic flows inside.
senses.whyCN: 同一根管子移到了河流和街道之下：城市在上面，车流在管子里。

senses.title: A hollow passage in animals or plants
senses.titleCN: 动物的洞穴；昆虫的蛀道
senses.definition: a long narrow hole dug or bored by an animal or insect, such as a burrow or a track inside wood
senses.definitionCN: 动物或昆虫挖出的细长孔道，如地洞或木头里的蛀痕
senses.example: The beetle larvae left winding tunnels inside the wooden beam.
senses.exampleCN: 甲虫幼虫在木梁里蛀出了弯弯曲曲的孔道。
senses.why: Nature borrows the image: a narrow tube dug through earth or wood works just like the engineer's passage.
senses.whyCN: 自然借用了这一意象：在泥土或木头里蛀出的细管，与工程师的通道如出一辙。

senses.title: A tube in physics or engineering
senses.definition: a long enclosed tube used in engineering or physics tests, such as a wind tunnel for studying airflow
senses.definitionCN: 工程或物理试验用的封闭长管，如研究气流的风洞
senses.example: The car model was tested in a wind tunnel before production.
senses.exampleCN: 这款汽车模型在投产前经过风洞测试。
senses.why: A controlled tube becomes an instrument: air or particles are sent down the same kind of passage to be measured.
senses.whyCN: 受控的管道变成了仪器：让空气或粒子流过同样的通道以便测量。

senses.title: To dig an underground passage
senses.definition: to dig a long passage through earth, rock or under a structure
senses.definitionCN: 在泥土、岩石中挖掘，或在建筑物下方挖出一条长通道
senses.example: The prisoners tried to tunnel out of the old fortress.
senses.exampleCN: 囚犯们试图从这座古堡里挖地道逃出去。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb: to make a tunnel is to tunnel, the picture stays one of pushing a tube through solid ground.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词：挖出一条 tunnel 就是 tunnel，画面始终是把一根管子推进坚实的地面。

senses.title: To force a way through resistance
senses.definition: to make a passage through something solid or through an obstacle, often by force or persistence
senses.definitionCN: 在实体或障碍中开出通路，常凭强力或坚持
senses.example: The miners tunnelled through a seam of hard rock.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工们凿穿了一层坚硬的岩层。
senses.why: The verb extends from earth to any solid barrier; the effort of boring through is the same.
senses.whyCN: 动词从泥土延伸到任何实体障碍；掘进的艰辛是一样的。

senses.title: Tunnel vision: a narrowed view
senses.definition: in the phrase tunnel vision, a mental state in which a person sees only one narrow part of a situation
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 tunnel vision，指只看见事物狭小一面的心理状态
senses.example: Fixating on quarterly numbers gives managers tunnel vision.
senses.exampleCN: 只盯着季度数字会让管理者陷入隧道视野。
senses.why: Inside a real tunnel you can only see the bright spot ahead; the metaphor borrows that narrowed field of sight.
senses.whyCN: 在真实隧道里只能看见前方亮点；这个比喻借用了那种变窄的视野。

senses.title: Light at the end of the tunnel
senses.definition: in the phrase light at the end of the tunnel, a sign that a long period of difficulty is nearly over
senses.definitionCN: 指短语「light at the end of the tunnel」，即漫长困难阶段接近尾声的迹象
senses.example: After two years of debt repayments, we finally see light at the end of the tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 偿债两年之后，我们终于看到了苦尽甘来的迹象。
senses.why: The image again looks down a long passage: hope is the spot of daylight growing at the far end.
senses.whyCN: 意象仍来自望向长长通道的尽头：希望就是远处越来越亮的日光。

intro.en: Tunnel goes back to a French word for a barrel; the passage got its name from the shape of a cask.
intro.cn: tunnel 可追溯到一个表示「大酒桶」的法语词；通道之名正来自酒桶的形状。

items.en: Old French tonel meant 'cask, barrel'; its earlier origin is generally considered to be uncertain, possibly of Gaulish or Germanic source.
items.cn: 古法语 tonel 意为「桶、大酒桶」；其更早来源一般认为不确定，可能有高卢语或日耳曼语源头。

items.en: French tonnelle meant 'a tun-shaped net' and later an arched arbour; the tube-like shape is central to the family.
items.cn: 法语 tonnelle 意为「桶形网」，后来也指拱形花架；管状外形是整个词族的核心。

items.en: English took the word in the fifteenth century for a net shaped like a tun; a tun is a large wine barrel.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入该词，指形状如大酒桶的网；tun 即大酒桶。

items.en: The canal builders of the eighteenth century applied the barrel shape to underground passages, and the modern sense was born.
items.cn: 十八世纪开凿运河的工程师把酒桶之形移用到地下通道上，现代义项由此诞生。

items.en: Railway engineering spread the word worldwide; the verb and the phrase tunnel vision followed in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪铁路工程把这个词传遍世界；动词和短语 tunnel vision 在二十世纪相继出现。

items.en: Today the word covers railway, road, animal and figurative passages alike.
items.cn: 如今这个词同时涵盖铁路、公路、动物洞穴和比喻义的通道。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the barrel root; the near-meaning group gathers passages, burrows and related digging words.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「桶」词根构成的一族词；近义组收通道、洞穴及相关挖掘词。

entries.definition: A large cask for wine or beer, and an old unit of capacity; the shape that named the tunnel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大酒桶」，兼指旧容量单位；正是它的形状给 tunnel 命名。

entries.definition: An old Spanish and Portuguese unit of weight or capacity, historically tied to a barrel load; spelled similarly and sharing the barrel idea.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指旧时西班牙、葡萄牙的重量或容量单位，历史上与一桶货相关；拼写相近且同涉「桶」，但为另一语言分支的词。

entries.definition: A tube wide at one end and narrow at the other for pouring; it merely rhymes and looks alike, with an unrelated source.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「漏斗」，一端宽一端窄；只是音形与 tunnel 相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: The upper edge of the side of a boat; it looks like tunnel but comes from gunwale.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「船舷上缘」；形似 tunnel，实际来自 gunwale。

entries.definition: An informal blend of Channel and tunnel, once used for the cross-Channel link; now uncommon.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，Channel 与 tunnel 的非正式合成词，曾指跨海峡隧道，现已少用。

entries.definition: A hole dug by an animal for living, or to dig such a hole; natural rather than engineered.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「地洞；打洞」，指动物挖掘的住所，属自然行为而非工程。

entries.definition: A passage for people or traffic under a road or railway; usually shorter and open at both ends.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「地下通道；下穿道」，供行人或车流穿越道路下方，通常较短且两端敞开。

entries.definition: A natural hollow in rock; formed by nature, not dug by people for a route.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「山洞；洞穴」，为天然形成，并非人为开凿的通路。

entries.definition: To make a hole with a drill, especially a long one for tunnels or pipelines; names the digging act itself.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「钻、掘」，尤指为隧道或管道钻长孔，指挖掘动作本身。

entries.definition: In British English, an underground walkway; in American English, the underground railway itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式英语指地下行人通道；美式英语指地铁系统。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real barrel root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的「桶」词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: A tunnel is named after a tun, the great barrel: dig the cask sideways through a hill.
normal.cn: tunnel 得名于 tun（大酒桶）：把大酒桶侧过来从山里掏过去，就是隧道。

normal.en: The Channel Tunnel joins Britain and France under the sea.
normal.cn: 英吉利海峡隧道在英国与法国之间的海底相连。

normal.en: Wind tunnel tests how air flows past models of planes and cars.
normal.cn: 风洞测试飞机和汽车模型周围的气流。

normal.en: The verb keeps the image: tunnel through, tunnel under, keep digging.
normal.cn: 动词保留画面：tunnel through、tunnel under，不停地挖。

normal.en: Light at the end of the tunnel is hope after a long hard stretch.
normal.cn: 短语「light at the end of the tunnel」指漫长苦境之后的希望。

abstract.en: Picture a giant cask lying inside a mountain: hollow it out and a road runs straight through.
abstract.cn: 想象一根巨大的酒桶横卧山中：掏空它，一条公路笔直穿过。

abstract.en: Every tunnel is a promise of the other side; what feels endless is only long.
abstract.cn: 每条隧道都是对「彼端」的承诺；感觉无尽的东西只是很长而已。

abstract.en: Tunnel vision is looking down one tube and forgetting the sky above it.
abstract.cn: 隧道视野就是只盯着一根管子内部，忘了管子上方的天空。

examples.en: The new road tunnel shortens the journey across the mountains by an hour.
examples.cn: 新建的公路隧道把穿越群山的车程缩短了一小时。

examples.en: Rabbits tunnel deep into the sandy bank to make their burrows.
examples.cn: 兔子在沙质河岸深处打洞筑窝。

examples.en: At last we saw light at the end of the tunnel when sales began to rise.
examples.cn: 当销售额开始上升时，我们终于看到了隧道尽头的光明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「探囊」——探囊取物般从山腹里掏出一条通道：隧道

root: 一般认为来自古法语 tonel「大酒桶」，更早源头不确定，可能有高卢语或日耳曼语背景；英语借入时指桶形渔网，十八世纪因外形相似转指地下通道，与 tun（大酒桶）同族。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of tunnel all keep the barrel shape: passages through mountains and under cities, animal burrows, test tubes of air, and the verb that digs them, ending in two figurative looks down a long passage.
sensesIntro.cn: tunnel 的八个义项都保留酒桶之形：穿山与城市下的通道、动物洞穴、气流试验管道，以及挖掘它们的动词，最后是两个望向长长通道的比喻义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a giant barrel-shaped tube is hollowed straight through a mountain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根巨桶状的管道被笔直掏空，穿山而过。

branches.en: THE WORKS: engineered passages carry roads and rails through and under obstacles.
branches.cn: 工程线：人工通道让公路与铁路穿山越河。

branches.en: THE NATURAL AND THE MEASURED: animals dig the same shape, and engineers seal it into an instrument.
branches.cn: 自然与测量线：动物掘出同样的孔形，工程师则把它封成仪器。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb is boring the tube through whatever resists.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词就是顶着阻力把管子掘进去。

branches.en: THE MIND: standing inside the tube narrows what one can see.
branches.cn: 心智线：置身管中，视野随之变窄。

branches.en: THE PROMISE: looking down the long passage, the light at the end is hope.
branches.cn: 承诺线：望向长长通道尽头，那点光就是希望。

intro.en: Tunnel is built on the French barrel root tonel, and English adds ordinary suffixes and spellings around it.
intro.cn: tunnel 建立在法语「桶」词根 tonel 之上，英语再围绕它加上普通后缀和拼写变体。

latinIntro.en: The barrel word is French, not Latin, so there are no Latin cognates to list; the deeper origin is treated as uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 「桶」这个词来自法语而非拉丁语，故没有拉丁同族词可列；更早来源视为不确定。

items.example: The root gives the tube shape of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根赋予该词管筒之形。

items.example: It forms tonel, a small barrel-shaped thing.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tonel，一个小小的桶状物。

items.example: Tunnelling names the act of digging.
items.exampleCN: tunnelling 指挖掘隧道这一行为。
tunneler 是挖隧道的人（或动物）。

items.example: The cousin word underpass also means under.
items.exampleCN: 近义词 underpass 同样含有「在下」之意。

items.example: It forms tunnel under, to dig beneath something.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tunnel under，在下面挖通道。
它构成 tunnel vision（隧道视野）。

items.example: Machine boring is how modern tunnels are cut.
items.exampleCN: 机械掘进是现代隧道的开凿方式。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加施动者后缀构成，义为「挖隧道的人（或动物）」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「隧道工程；掘进作业」

definition_zh: 转动；旋转；转弯；转变；变成；轮流；（依次轮到的）机会；把……转向
definition_en: to move around a central point, to change direction, or to change into a different state, or an occasion when it is your chance to do something
core_image: 一根绕着轴心转动的辐条，转着转着就转向了另一个方向
scene: 十字路口的车流停下又前进，轮到那辆红色小车了。The little red car will turn left at the busy crossing.
sceneCN: 这里 turn 是动词「转弯、改变方向」（第 3 个义项：改变行进方向）；句意为那辆红色小车将在繁忙的路口左转。

pos.zh: 动词：（使）转动；转弯；转变；变成
名词：转动；转弯处；轮流；转变；（依次轮到的）机会

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「转弯处；车流转向处」
与本词同族的复合动词，由 re-「回」加 turn 构成，义为「返回；归还」
由本词与 out 合成，义为「到场人数； voter 出席率」，如选举投票人数

senses.title: To move around a central point
senses.definition: to move in a circle around a fixed central point, or to make something do this
senses.definitionCN: 绕固定中心点做圆周运动，或使某物如此运动
senses.example: She turned the key and the engine started.
senses.exampleCN: 她转动钥匙，发动机启动了。
senses.why: The core image is a spoke sweeping around an axle; anything that pivots is turning.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是辐条绕轴扫动；凡绕枢轴运动的都是 turn。

senses.title: To rotate a knob, wheel or handle
senses.definition: to twist a control such as a key, knob or dial in order to operate it
senses.definitionCN: 拧动钥匙、旋钮、表盘等控制装置以使其工作
senses.example: Turn the dial until the channel becomes clear.
senses.exampleCN: 转动旋钮直到频道变清晰。
senses.why: Controls work by rotation, so operating one is turning it; the hand supplies the circle.
senses.whyCN: 控制装置靠旋转工作，操作它就是拧转它；手提供了那圈圆周。

senses.title: To change direction
senses.definition: to change the direction you are moving in, or to make a vehicle change direction
senses.definitionCN: 改变行进方向，或使车辆改变方向
senses.example: The lorry will turn right at the next junction.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车将在下一个路口右转。
senses.why: A rotating body ends up facing a new way; direction change is rotation applied to travel.
senses.whyCN: 旋转体最终面向新方向；方向改变就是把旋转用到行进上。

senses.title: To change into another state
senses.definition: to change from one state, colour or quality into another
senses.definitionCN: 从一种状态、颜色或性质变为另一种
senses.example: The leaves turn gold every October.
senses.exampleCN: 每年十月树叶都变成金色。
senses.why: Rotation is extended to change of state: the world swings from one condition to its opposite or neighbour.
senses.whyCN: 把旋转延伸到状态变化：世界从一种状况摆到相邻或相反的状况。

senses.title: To point or direct something
senses.definition: to aim or point something such as a face, camera or attention in a particular direction
senses.definitionCN: 把脸、镜头、注意力等对准或转向某个方向
senses.example: The audience turned their eyes to the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 观众把目光转向舞台。
senses.why: To aim is to rotate toward a target; eyes and cameras pivot just like wheels.
senses.whyCN: 瞄准就是朝目标旋转；眼睛和镜头像车轮一样转动。

senses.title: To go round in sequence
senses.definition: when people take turns, each has a chance to act one after another in order
senses.definitionCN: 人们依次行动，每人轮流获得一次机会
senses.example: The children take turns feeding the class rabbit.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们轮流喂班级的兔子。
senses.why: A wheel brings each part round to the top in order; so does a queue of waiting people.
senses.whyCN: 轮子依次把每个部分转到顶上；一队等候的人也是如此。

senses.title: An occasion when it is your chance
senses.definition: the time when it is your opportunity to do something in a shared activity
senses.definitionCN: 共同活动中轮到你行动的时机
senses.example: It is your turn to wash the dishes tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚轮到你洗碗。
senses.why: The noun fixes the moment the wheel of sequence points at you.
senses.whyCN: 名词把「次序之轮指向你」的那一刻固定下来。

senses.title: A bend or change of situation
senses.definition: a bend in a road, or a change in a situation, illness or fortune
senses.definitionCN: 道路的拐弯处，或局势、病情、命运的转折
senses.example: The war took a sudden turn after the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那年冬天之后，战局突然出现转折。
senses.why: Roads and stories both bend; where the direction swings, there is a turn.
senses.whyCN: 道路与故事都会弯曲；方向摆动之处就是一个 turn。

senses.title: To upset the stomach
senses.definition: to make someone feel sick, as in the phrase turn the stomach
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到恶心，如短语 turn the stomach
senses.example: The smell of the rotten fish turned my stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 烂鱼的气味让我直反胃。
senses.why: Inside, everything swings over: the phrase pictures the stomach rolling over.
senses.whyCN: 身体内部天翻地覆：短语描绘的是胃里翻腾打转的画面。

senses.title: To become sour or spoiled
senses.definition: of milk or food, to go sour or bad
senses.definitionCN: 指牛奶或食物变酸、变质
senses.example: The milk turned in the warm kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 牛奶在温暖的厨房里变馊了。
senses.why: Quality can rotate like direction: good swings over to bad, and the food turns.
senses.whyCN: 品质可以像方向一样「转」：好的一面摆到坏的一面，食物就 turn 了。

intro.en: Turn comes from Latin through Greek and Latin words for a lathe or a circle, reaching English via Old French.
intro.cn: turn 经由希腊语、拉丁语中表示「车床、圆环」的词，再经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Greek tornos meant a lathe tool or a compass-drawn circle; it is generally taken as the source of the Latin word.
items.cn: 希腊语 tornos 指车床刀具或圆规画出的圆；一般认为它是拉丁语对应词的源头。

items.en: Latin tornare meant 'to turn on a lathe, round off', built on tornus 'lathe'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tornare 意为「用车床旋削、修圆」，建立在 tornus「车床」之上。

items.en: In late Latin the verb widened to mean simply 'to turn, to revolve'.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中该动词扩展为泛指「转动、旋转」。

items.en: Old French turner, torner carried both the lathe sense and the general turning sense into English.
items.cn: 古法语 turner、torner 把车床义与泛指的转动义一并带入英语。

items.en: The verb is recorded in English from around the twelfth century; the noun and the many phrases developed soon after.
items.cn: 动词约自十二世纪见于英语；名词和大量短语随后发展起来。

items.en: Today turn is among the most polysemous verbs in English, from keyholes to milk.
items.cn: 如今 turn 是英语多义最强的动词之一，从钥匙孔一直用到牛奶变质。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same turning family; the near-meaning group gathers rotate, spin and related changes.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「转动」词族；近义组收 rotate、spin 及相关的变化词。

entries.definition: To come or go back; built on the same turning root with re- meaning back.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「返回；归还」，由同一转动词根加 re-「回」构成。

entries.definition: The number of people who attend or vote; a compound of turn plus out.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「到场人数；投票率」，由 turn 加 out 构成的复合词。

entries.definition: A round root vegetable; the shape link is often claimed but the compound's history is debated, and its meaning is unrelated to turning motion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「芜菁」；常被说成与「转」有关，但其复合词来源有争议，词义也与转动无关。

entries.definition: A violently rotating column of air; borrowed from Spanish, itself from the Latin turning verb tornare.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「龙卷风」，经西班牙语借入，其源头同样是拉丁动词 tornare。

entries.definition: A journey around places; from the same Latin root meaning to draw a circle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「旅行；巡回」，来自同一拉丁词根，本义「画圆、绕行」。

entries.definition: To move in a circle around a centre; more technical and precise than turn.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「旋转」，指绕中心做圆周运动，比 turn 更书面、更精确。

entries.definition: To turn quickly and repeatedly around an axis, often fast and continuous.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「快速旋转」，强调绕轴高速连续转动。

entries.definition: To move in an orbit or circle, often of heavenly bodies; formal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「旋转；公转」，常指天体沿轨道运行，语气正式。

entries.definition: To turn on a fixed central point, or to change strategy abruptly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「绕枢轴转动；急剧调整方向或策略」。

entries.definition: To change direction suddenly, especially to avoid something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「突然转向」，尤指为躲避某物而急转。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real lathe root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的车床词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Latin tornare is to work on a lathe: turning wood into round shapes.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 tornare 是用车床加工：把木头车成圆形。

normal.en: Tornado and tour share the same circle root: air that turns, a trip that goes round.
normal.cn: tornado 和 tour 共享同一「圆」词根：转动的气流、绕行的旅程。

normal.en: Take turns is the wheel of the queue: each person comes round in order.
normal.cn: take turns 是排队的轮子：每个人按顺序转到自己。

normal.en: Turn up has two faces: the volume goes up, or someone suddenly appears.
normal.cn: turn up 有两副面孔：音量调大，或某人突然出现。

normal.en: Milk that has turned has swung from fresh to sour.
normal.cn: 变馊的牛奶就是从新鲜「转」到了酸臭。

abstract.en: Picture a fairground wheel: every seat has its turn at the top.
abstract.cn: 想象游乐场的转轮：每个座位都会轮到转到最高点。

abstract.en: Life also turns: one swing can carry you from one state to another.
abstract.cn: 人生同样会「转」：一次摆动就能带你从一种状态到另一种。

abstract.en: At a crossroads, a turn is a decision made by a steering wheel.
abstract.cn: 在十字路口，一次转弯就是一次由方向盘做出的决定。

examples.en: Turn the handle clockwise to open the safe.
examples.cn: 顺时针转动手柄即可打开保险柜。

examples.en: The conversation took an unexpected turn toward family history.
examples.cn: 谈话意外地转向了家族历史。

examples.en: We take turns driving on the long trip to the coast.
examples.cn: 去海滨的长途旅行中我们轮流开车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特恩」——转个特别恩惠的弯，轮到你了：转动、轮流

root: 一般认为源自希腊语 tornos「车床、圆规之圆」，经拉丁语 tornare「用车床旋削、转动」与晚期拉丁语扩展义，再经古法语 turner 进入英语；同族词有 tour、tornado、return 等。

sensesIntro.en: The ten senses of turn all hang on one pivot: physical rotation, twisted controls, changed direction and state, aimed attention, the shared wheel of taking turns, and the sour swing of spoiled food.
sensesIntro.cn: turn 的十个义项都挂在一根轴上：物理旋转、拧动控制装置、方向与状态的改变、对准的注意、轮流共有之轮，以及食物变质的酸腐摆动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spoke swings around an axle and the facing direction changes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根辐条绕轴摆动，朝向随之改变。

branches.en: THE HAND AND THE MECHANISM: keys, knobs and wheels are turned to work.
branches.cn: 手与机械线：钥匙、旋钮、车轮靠转动来工作。

branches.en: THE WAY: travel and gaze both swing to a new heading.
branches.cn: 路线线：行进与目光都摆向新的方向。

branches.en: THE SWING OF STATE: leaves, stomachs and milk all pass from one condition to another.
branches.cn: 状态摆动线：树叶、胃和牛奶都从一种状况转到另一种。

branches.en: THE SHARED WHEEL: in a queue each person gets an occasion, and that occasion is your turn.
branches.cn: 共有之轮线：队伍里人人有机会，那一刻就是你的 turn。

branches.en: THE BEND: roads and fortunes change where they turn.
branches.cn: 弯道线：道路与命运的转折都在转弯处。

intro.en: Turn is a bare root word, but English has multiplied it into a large compound and derived family.
intro.cn: turn 本身是一个裸词根，但英语把它扩展成庞大的复合与派生词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb tornare and Greek tornos are recorded; the Greek source is generally accepted, and the very early trail is treated as uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 tornare 与希腊语 tornos 均有记录；希腊语源头一般被接受，更早的脉络视为不确定。

items.exampleCN: 它见于 circuit 与 circus，这两个同源词共享「圆」的概念。

definition_zh: 两次；两倍；双倍地
definition_en: two times, or double the amount or degree of something
core_image: 同一件事做了第二遍，或数量翻了一倍
scene: 闹钟没响，小李一个早晨已经迟到两回，工资单上还写着翻倍的加班时数。He was late twice this morning and did not dare complain.
sceneCN: 这里 twice 是副词「两次」（第 1 个义项：做某事两回）；句意为今天早上他迟到了两次，工资单上加班时数也照两倍计。

pos.zh: 副词：两次；两倍

derivatives.zh: 同源基数词，twice 即「两」的副词形式
同源序数词，义为「第十二」，与 two 同属古英语 twa 词族
同源数词，本义为「两个十」

senses.title: Two times, on two occasions
senses.definition: on two occasions or in two instances
senses.definitionCN: 在两个场合或发生两回
senses.example: I called her twice, but she did not answer.
senses.exampleCN: 我给她打了两次电话，她都没接。
senses.why: The core image is repetition counted to two: the same act laid out a second time.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是数到二的重复：同一个动作又铺开了一遍。

senses.title: Double the amount
senses.definition: double in quantity, size, degree or amount
senses.definitionCN: 数量、尺寸、程度或金额上的加倍
senses.example: This room is twice as large as the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间比旧的那间大一倍。
senses.why: Counting occasions becomes counting quantity: two units of the same measure stacked together.
senses.whyCN: 计次的「两回」变成计量的「两份」：同样的度量单位叠加了两次。

senses.title: Twice over: again a second time
senses.definition: in the phrase twice over, done a second time in addition to the first
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 twice over，指在第一次之外再做第二遍
senses.example: He checked the figures twice over before signing.
senses.exampleCN: 签字前他把数字核了两遍。
senses.why: The phrase makes the repetition explicit: the act is performed, then performed again.
senses.whyCN: 短语把重复显性化：动作做完之后再来一遍。

senses.title: Think twice: hesitate before acting
senses.definition: in the phrase think twice, to consider carefully before deciding or acting
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 think twice，指决定或行动前慎重考虑
senses.example: You should think twice before lending money to a stranger.
senses.exampleCN: 借钱给陌生人之前你该三思。
senses.why: The mind runs over the matter a second time; the second pass is the caution.
senses.whyCN: 头脑把事情再过一遍；这第二次过就是审慎。

senses.title: Twice removed: two steps in kinship
senses.definition: in phrases like first cousin twice removed, separated by two generations
senses.definitionCN: 用于 first cousin twice removed 等短语，指亲属关系相隔两代
senses.example: She is my cousin twice removed on my mother's side.
senses.exampleCN: 她是我母亲那边隔两代的表亲。
senses.why: Kinship is measured in steps, and twice counts two steps down the ladder.
senses.whyCN: 亲属关系按代步计，twice 数出往下隔的两代。

senses.title: Lightning never strikes twice: rarity of repetition
senses.definition: in the saying lightning never strikes twice, an unlucky event is unlikely to happen again in the same place
senses.definitionCN: 谚语 lightning never strikes twice，指倒霉的事不大可能在同一处重演
senses.example: After losing two wallets, he joked that lightning never strikes twice.
senses.exampleCN: 连丢两个钱包后，他自嘲说祸不单行这种事不会再来一次。
senses.why: The proverb plays on the counting: one strike is bad luck, a second strike would be twice.
senses.whyCN: 谚语玩的是计数：一次倒霉是运气差，再来一次才算「两次」。

senses.title: Twice told: repeated words
senses.definition: in literary use, twice told describes a story or remark that has been told before and is told again
senses.definitionCN: 文学用法，twice told 形容已讲过又再讲的故事或话
senses.example: He opened the meeting with a twice told tale about the founding of the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 他以一个讲过多次的公司创业老故事开场。
senses.why: The count attaches to the telling: the tale has now completed its second round.
senses.whyCN: 计数落在「讲」上：故事如今完成了第二轮。

senses.title: Twice as much again: compounding increase
senses.definition: in the phrase twice as much again, an increase equal to the original amount on top of it
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 twice as much again，指在原有数量之上再增加与原量相等的部分
senses.example: The new plant can turn out twice as much again as the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 新厂的产量能在旧厂的基础上再翻一倍。
senses.why: The doubling is measured against the base: what exists once is matched by an equal second amount.
senses.whyCN: 加倍以原有数量为基准：已有的一份再配上等量的第二份。

intro.en: Twice is the old adverb of two, built inside English on a native numeral root.
intro.cn: twice 是 two 的古式副词，在英语内部由本族数词词根构成。

items.en: *dwo- is generally reconstructed as the numeral 'two'; its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *dwo- 是数词「二」；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Proto-Germanic gave *twai, the ancestor of English two, and a related doubling form *twiz-
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语给出 *twai，即英语 two 的祖先，另有一个相关的叠倍形式 *twiz-。

items.en: Old English had twige, twiwa 'two times, doubly', built directly on the numeral twā 'two'.
items.cn: 古英语有 twige、twiwa，义为「两次、加倍」，直接建立在数词 twā「二」之上。

items.en: Middle English twies added the adverbial -s, like the ending in once and besides.
items.cn: 中古英语 twies 加上了副词性词尾 -s，与 once、besides 的词尾相同。

items.en: The spelling twice settled by the fourteenth century, and the double-quantity sense was already common.
items.cn: 十四世纪拼写定型为 twice，「两倍」义当时已很常用。

items.en: Fixed phrases such as think twice and twice removed keep the word busy far beyond plain counting.
items.cn: think twice、twice removed 等固定短语让这个词的用法远远超出单纯的计数。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the numeral family and the adverbial -s twins; the near-meaning group gathers words of repetition and doubling.
note.cn: 形近组收数词词族与同词尾副词；近义组收表重复与加倍的词。

entries.definition: One time; built on the numeral one with the same adverbial ending.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「一次」，由数词 one 加同样的副词词尾构成。

entries.definition: Three times; the old parallel adverb of three, now literary.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「三次」，three 的古式对应副词，今多用于文学。

entries.definition: To wind two strands together or to turn; looks and sounds close but is a different verb with a different history.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「捻合；拧转」，音形与 twice 相近，但是另一个动词，词源不同。

entries.definition: One of two children born together; from the same doubling numeral root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「双胞胎之一」，出自同一个表示「成双」的数词词根。

entries.definition: The ordinal of twelve; from the numeral family that also produced twice.
entries.definitionCN: 序数词，义为「第十二」，出自同样产出 twice 的数词词族。

entries.definition: Twice as much, or to make something twice as much; the adjective and verb counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或动词，义为「两倍的；使加倍」，与 twice 的「两倍」义互为表里。

entries.definition: One more time; marks a single repetition rather than the count of two.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「再次」，标记单次重复，而非「两次」这一计数。

entries.definition: Many times over; the count is left open instead of fixed at two.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「反复地」，次数开放不定，而非固定为两次。

entries.definition: To twice the degree; formal counterpart of the doubling sense.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「加倍地」，是「两倍」义的正式对应词。

entries.definition: Coming after the first; names the position that a second occurrence takes.
entries.definitionCN: 序数词，义为「第二」，标出第二次发生所处的位置。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real numeral root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的数词词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Twice is two with an adverbial s, exactly like once from one.
normal.cn: twice 就是 two 加副词词尾 s，与 once 之于 one 完全平行。

normal.en: Twice a week is a rhythm: Monday and Thursday, two beats.
normal.cn: twice a week 是一种节奏：周一和周四，两拍。

normal.en: Think twice means run the thought through your head two times.
normal.cn: think twice 意为让这个念头在脑中过两遍。

normal.en: Twice as much is two copies of the same amount stacked up.
normal.cn: twice as much 就是把同样的量叠上两份。

normal.en: Thrice is its triplet brother: once, twice, thrice.
normal.cn: thrice 是它的三胞胎兄弟：once、twice、thrice。

abstract.en: Picture one footprint, then a second one landing exactly on top of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个脚印，接着第二个脚印不偏不倚落在上面。

abstract.en: A doubled dose is the same cup poured into the glass a second time.
abstract.cn: 加倍就是把同一杯又倒了一遍。

abstract.en: Caution is the second pass of the mind over the same road.
abstract.cn: 审慎就是让头脑在同一条路上再走第二遍。

examples.en: The museum opens twice a week for school groups.
examples.cn: 博物馆每周为学校团体开放两次。

examples.en: Our new office is twice the size of the old one.
examples.cn: 我们的新办公室是旧办公室的两倍大。

examples.en: Read the contract twice before you put your name on it.
examples.cn: 签字之前把合同读两遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太吾事」——两遍都太吾事没做好：两次、两倍

root: 古英语 twige「两次」直接建立在数词 twā「二」之上，经中古英语 twies 加副词性 -s 演变为 twice；数词本身来自原始日耳曼语 *twai，可追溯至原始印欧语 *dwo-（重构形式），与 two、twin、twelve、twenty 同族。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of twice all count to two: repeated occasions, doubled amounts, a second telling, the second pass of caution, kinship steps, proverbs, and compounded increases.
sensesIntro.cn: twice 的八个义项都数到二：重复的场合、加倍的量、第二次的讲述、审慎的第二遍过、亲等的两步、谚语，以及叠加式增长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same act or amount is laid down a second time.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个动作或数量被第二次放下。

branches.en: THE REPEATED ACT: two occasions, a second telling, a tale told twice over.
branches.cn: 重复动作线：两个场合、第二次讲述、讲了第二遍的故事。

branches.en: THE DOUBLED AMOUNT: two stacked measures, and a further increase on top of them.
branches.cn: 加倍数量线：两份叠加的量，以及在其之上的再增长。

branches.en: THE CAUTIOUS MIND: the thought runs a second time before the feet move.
branches.cn: 审慎心智线：脚未动，念头先再过一遍。

branches.en: THE FAMILY TREE: two generations down the kinship ladder.
branches.cn: 家族谱系线：亲等梯子往下的两代。

branches.en: THE PROVERB: one strike is misfortune, a second would be twice.
branches.cn: 谚语线：一次是倒霉，再来一次才算「两次」。

intro.en: Twice is a single native numeral adverb, but its family of tw- words is large and old.
intro.cn: twice 是单个的本族数词副词，但其 tw- 词族既庞大又古老。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, not Latin, so there are no Latin cognates to list; the Indo-European root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语源而非拉丁语源，故没有拉丁同族词可列；印欧词根属重构形式。

items.example: The numeral is the base of the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个数词是该副词的基础。

items.meaning: forms adverbs of manner or number
items.meaningCN: 构成方式或数目的副词
items.example: It also appears in once and besides.
items.exampleCN: 同样的词尾也见于 once 与 besides。

items.example: It appears in twilight, the half-light of two states.
items.exampleCN: 它见于 twilight，即两种状态之间的微光。

items.example: The reconstructed root lies behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个重构词根是整个词族的源头。

items.example: It carries the same meaning from Latin, via duplex.
items.exampleCN: 它经 duplex 从拉丁语带来同样的「两倍」义。
它构成 bicycle 与 biannual。

items.example: It names the position of the second occurrence.
items.exampleCN: 它标出第二次发生的位置。

definition_zh: 捻；搓；拧；扭弯；缠绕；（故事的）转折；曲折；拧转的动作
definition_en: to wind two or more strands together, to bend or turn something out of shape, or an unexpected change in a story or situation
core_image: 两股绳被反方向拧在一起，拧着拧着就拐了个弯
scene: 奶奶坐在门槛上搓麻绳，两股线在她掌心越缠越紧。She learned to twist flax into strong rope as a girl.
sceneCN: 这里 twist 是动词「捻、搓」（第 1 个义项：把丝线拧合成绳）；句意为她少女时代就学会把亚麻捻成结实的绳子。

pos.zh: 动词：捻；搓；拧；扭弯；缠绕
名词：拧转；（故事）转折；曲折；扭伤；麻花状物

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「弯弯曲曲的；曲折的」
由本词过去分词转作形容词，义为「扭曲的；（心智）反常的」
由本词加施动者后缀构成，义为「缠绕者；难题；（口语）龙卷风（tornado 的别称）」

senses.title: To wind strands together
senses.definition: to wind two or more threads, fibres or wires around each other to form a cord or rope
senses.definitionCN: 把两股或多股线、纤维或金属丝相互缠绕成绳线
senses.example: The villagers twist palm leaves into twine for fishing nets.
senses.exampleCN: 村民把棕榈叶捻成搓渔网用的细绳。
senses.why: The core image is two strands rolled in opposite directions so they grip each other.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是两股线朝相反方向滚动，从而互相咬合。

senses.title: To turn a controlling knob or cap
senses.definition: to turn something such as a cap, lid or key with a rotating movement
senses.definitionCN: 以旋转动作拧动瓶盖、盖子或钥匙等
senses.example: She twisted off the jam jar lid and handed it over.
senses.exampleCN: 她拧下果酱瓶盖递了过去。
senses.why: A cap held by opposing grips comes loose only by rolling the hands apart.
senses.whyCN: 瓶盖要靠两手反向滚动才能松动。

senses.title: To bend or wrench out of shape
senses.definition: to bend, wrench or force something out of its natural shape
senses.definitionCN: 把某物弯曲、扳扭或强行弄离原有形状
senses.example: The crash twisted the bicycle's front wheel.
senses.exampleCN: 撞车把自行车前轮撞得变了形。
senses.why: Force applied unevenly rotates part of an object away from the rest; the shape spirals.
senses.whyCN: 不均匀的力使物体一部分相对其余部分转开，形状呈螺旋状偏离。

senses.title: To injure a joint by wrenching
senses.definition: to hurt a joint such as an ankle or wrist by suddenly wrenching it
senses.definitionCN: 因突然的扭转而扭伤脚踝、手腕等关节
senses.example: He twisted his knee stepping off the last stair.
senses.exampleCN: 下最后一级台阶时他扭伤了膝盖。
senses.why: The joint is the body's most turnable part; a wrong turn strains it.
senses.whyCN: 关节是身体最易转动的部位；转错方向便拉伤。

senses.title: To wind or coil around
senses.definition: to wrap one thing around another, often in a spiral
senses.definitionCN: 把一物缠绕在另一物上，常呈螺旋状
senses.example: Vines twist around the old fence posts every summer.
senses.exampleCN: 每年夏天藤蔓都缠绕在旧篱笆桩上。
senses.why: The rope-making motion, applied by nature, wraps one thing about another.
senses.whyCN: 制绳的旋转动作由自然施加，便成了缠绕。

senses.title: To move in a winding way
senses.definition: to follow a winding, bending course, as a road, river or body may do
senses.definitionCN: 沿蜿蜒弯曲的路线行进，如道路、河流或身体
senses.example: The mountain road twists down toward the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 山路蜿蜒而下，通向谷底。
senses.why: A bent line is one that keeps turning; winding is repeated small twists.
senses.whyCN: 弯线就是不断转向的线；蜿蜒是许多次小幅的拧转。

senses.title: An unexpected change in a story
senses.definition: an unexpected development or change of direction in a story, situation or plan
senses.definitionCN: 故事、局势或计划中出人意料的变化或转向
senses.example: The trial took a twist when a new witness appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 一位新证人出现后，庭审出现了转折。
senses.why: The bent shape is projected onto events: when the straight line of the plot suddenly bends, that bend is the twist.
senses.whyCN: 把弯折之形投射到事件上：情节的直线突然拐弯，这个弯就是 twist。

senses.title: A spiralling shape or object
senses.definition: a shape made by winding something around itself, such as a curl of peel or a piece of twisted bread
senses.definitionCN: 由缠绕自身而成的形状，如柑皮卷或麻花状面点
senses.example: The barman garnished the glass with a twist of lemon peel.
senses.exampleCN: 调酒师用一小卷柠檬皮装饰酒杯。
senses.why: The noun freezes the rope picture into a small object you can see and hold.
senses.whyCN: 名词把制绳画面冻结成一件看得见、拿得住的小物件。

senses.title: To distort the meaning of words
senses.definition: to change or present someone's words so that they mean something unfair or unintended
senses.definitionCN: 改动或呈现某人的话，使其带有不公或非本意的含义
senses.example: The tabloid twisted her remarks into an accusation.
senses.exampleCN: 小报把她的评论曲解成一项指控。
senses.why: Words are like strands: pulled askew, they no longer lie straight and true.
senses.whyCN: 话语如绳股：被斜着拽动，便不再笔直属实。

senses.title: A twisted mind: mental distortion
senses.titleCN: 反常的心智；扭曲的观念
senses.definition: in describing a person or thinking as twisted, mentally distorted or unhealthily turned
senses.definitionCN: 形容人或思想 twisted，指心智扭曲、想法反常
senses.example: The villain's twisted logic blames everyone but himself.
senses.exampleCN: 反派的扭曲逻辑把过错归咎于除自己以外的所有人。
senses.why: The wrenched shape becomes a metaphor for wrenched judgment; what should run straight has been bent.
senses.whyCN: 被拧弯的形状成为被扭曲的判断的比喻；本应笔直的思路被掰弯了。

intro.en: Twist descends from an Old English word for a rope made of twisted strands.
intro.cn: twist 源自古英语中指「用股线拧成的绳索」的词。

items.en: *dwo- 'two' is generally reconstructed at the base of the family, since twisting joins two strands.
items.cn: 一般认为词族底层是重构形式 *dwo-「二」，因为拧转正是把两股合在一起。

items.en: Old English twist meant 'a cord, a twisted rope', recorded for rope-making and sail-making.
items.cn: 古英语 twist 意为「细绳、拧成的绳索」，见于制绳与制帆的记载。

items.en: The word kept the rope sense and began to name the winding motion itself.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了绳索义，并开始指拧转这一动作本身。

items.en: The verb widened to wrenching, coiling and winding courses; the relationship to the numeral two is generally accepted but the exact morphological path is uncertain.
items.cn: 十五、十六世纪动词扩展到扳扭、缠绕与蜿蜒；与数词「二」的关系一般被接受，但确切形态演变路径不确定。

items.en: The figurative senses flourished in fiction: the plot twist became a stock term of storytelling.
items.cn: 十九世纪比喻义在小说中大放异彩：plot twist 成为叙事的固定术语。

items.en: Today the word covers rope, joints, roads, plots and personalities alike.
items.cn: 如今这个词同时涵盖绳索、关节、道路、情节与性格。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the tw- family and sound-alike words; the near-meaning group gathers winding, bending and turning words.
note.cn: 形近组收 tw- 词族与音近词；近义组收缠绕、弯曲与转动类词。

entries.definition: Strong string made of twisted strands, or to wind around; the direct rope relative.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「细绳；缠绕」，是直接的绳索同族词。

entries.definition: Two times; shares the old two-strand numeral root in origin but counts instead of winding.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「两次」，词源上同样关联「二股」这一古老数词根，但表示计数而非缠绕。

entries.definition: The joint between hand and arm; long associated with turning and twisting, though the exact common origin with twist is debated.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「手腕」，历来与「拧转」相关，但与 twist 是否同源尚有争议。

entries.definition: A cloth woven with a diagonal pattern of crossing threads; another textile word of the tw- weaving family.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「斜纹布」，指线股斜向交织的织物，同属 tw- 织造词族。

entries.definition: To spin quickly and lightly; looks like twist but is a separate, probably blended word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「轻快旋转」，形似 twist，但可能是另一混合来源的词。

entries.definition: To coil something around in loops; emphasizes the wrapping rather than the gripping of strands.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缠绕；盘绕」，强调环绕成圈，而非两股咬合。

entries.definition: To gather into rings or a spiral; the result is loops, not joined strands.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「盘绕成圈」，结果呈环状，而非股线拧合。

entries.definition: To twist suddenly and violently, often injuring something; stress falls on the force.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「猛拧；猛扭」，常致损伤，强调暴烈的用力。

entries.definition: A curve winding around a centre, or to move in such a curve; geometric in flavor.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「螺旋；盘旋」，偏几何意味。

entries.definition: To turn aside suddenly from a straight course; the turning without the winding.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「突然偏离直线方向」，只有转向而无缠绕。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real rope root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的绳索词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Old English twist was itself a cord: the word began life as rope.
normal.cn: 古英语 twist 本义就是细绳：这个词生来就是绳子。

normal.en: Twine, twill, twist: the tw- family is all about joining two strands.
normal.cn: twine、twill、twist：tw- 词族全都围绕「两股相合」。

normal.en: Twist one's ankle is the body's rope kinked the wrong way.
normal.cn: twist one's ankle 就是身体的绳索拐错了方向。

normal.en: A twist in the plot is the story's rope taking a sudden bend.
normal.cn: 情节的 twist 是故事的绳子突然拐了个弯。

normal.en: Twist off a lid: roll your hands apart and the cap gives way.
normal.cn: twist off a lid：两手反向一滚，盖子就松了。

abstract.en: Picture two threads rolling toward each other between your palms, gripping tighter with every turn.
abstract.cn: 想象两根线在你掌心相向滚动，每转一圈咬得更紧。

abstract.en: A road that twists is one that cannot say a straight sentence.
abstract.cn: 蜿蜒的路就是一句说不出直线的话。

abstract.en: Twisted words are strands pulled out of line: still there, but no longer true.
abstract.cn: 被歪曲的话语是拽离了直线绳股：还在那里，却不再属实。

examples.en: She twisted three coloured threads into a friendship bracelet.
examples.cn: 她把三根彩色丝线捻成一条友谊手链。

examples.en: The film ends with a twist nobody in the cinema saw coming.
examples.cn: 影片的结局来了一个全场无人料到的转折。

examples.en: Reporters accused the spokesman of twisting the minister's words.
examples.cn: 记者指责发言人歪曲部长的原话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特为斯特」——特意把两股线拧成一股绳：捻、拧、缠

root: 古英语 twist「细绳、拧成的绳索」，一般认为可追溯至原始印欧语 *dwo-「二」（重构形式），因拧转即合二股；与 twine、twill、twin、twice 同属 tw- 词族；与数词二的确切形态关联存在不确定性。

sensesIntro.en: The ten senses of twist all grow from one coiled picture: making rope, turning caps, wrenching shapes, twisting joints and roads, bending plots, curling peel, distorting words and minds.
sensesIntro.cn: twist 的十个义项都从同一幅缠绕画面生长：搓绳、拧盖、扳弯形状、扭伤关节、蜿蜒道路、情节拐弯、柑皮成卷、话语与心智被扭曲。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two strands roll in opposite directions and grip into one rope.
core.cn: 核心意象：两股线反向滚动，咬合成一根绳。

branches.en: THE ROPE: making, wrapping and freezing the coil into objects like peel twists.
branches.cn: 绳索线：制绳、缠裹，并把盘绕冻结成柑皮卷之类的物件。

branches.en: THE FORCE: turning caps, wrenching shapes and straining joints.
branches.cn: 用力线：拧盖、扳弯形状与拉伤关节。

branches.en: THE PATH: repeated small turns make a winding road.
branches.cn: 路径线：多次小幅转向织成蜿蜒的路。

branches.en: THE STORY: the straight line of events takes a sudden bend.
branches.cn: 故事线：事件的直线突然拐弯。

branches.en: THE MIND: words and judgments pulled out of true.
branches.cn: 心智线：话语与判断被拽离本相。

intro.en: Twist is a single native root, but its tw- family spreads across rope, cloth, kinship and counting.
intro.cn: twist 是单个本族词根，但其 tw- 词族横跨绳索、织物、亲属与计数。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, not Latin, so there are no Latin cognates to list; the Indo-European base is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语源而非拉丁语源，故没有拉丁同族词可列；印欧词基属重构形式。

items.example: The noun is the oldest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是可考的最早形式。

items.example: It forms twisted cloth and twisted minds.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 twisted（拧过的）布料与扭曲的心智。
它构成 twisty（弯弯曲曲的）道路。

items.example: The sister word keeps the rope sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个同族词保留了绳索义。

items.example: It shows the family in weaving.
items.exampleCN: 它显示该词族在织造中的身影。

items.meaning: the turning joint of the arm
items.example: Its link with twist is old but debated.
items.exampleCN: 它与 twist 的关联古老但有争议。

items.example: It names the violent member of the turning family.
items.exampleCN: 它命名了转动家族中暴烈的一员。

definition_zh: 类型；种类；典型；印刷字体；（用打字机或键盘）打字；打印
definition_en: a class or kind of thing with shared features, or to write using a keyboard
core_image: 把相似的东西归进同一格子的分拣匣，每一格都是一类
scene: 图书馆的书车分好格，管理员把新到的书按类归位。The librarian sorted each book by its type before shelving.
sceneCN: 这里 type 是名词「类型、类别」（第 1 个义项：具有共同特征的种类）；句意为图书管理员按类别把每本书归架。

pos.zh: 名词：类型；种类；典型；印刷字体
动词：打字；把……归类；测定（血）型

collocations.zh: 是某人喜欢的那一类型

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「典型的；有代表性的」
由 typical 加副词后缀构成，义为「典型地；通常」
由本词与 writer 合成，义为「打字机」
由本词加施动者后缀构成，义为「打字员」

senses.title: A class of things with shared features
senses.definition: a group or class of things that share recognizable features
senses.definitionCN: 具有可辨识共同特征的一组或一类事物
senses.example: This strain of rice is a new type for the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这种水稻是该地区的一个新品种。
senses.why: The core image is sorting: things pressed by an impression into the same shape share one mold.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是分拣：被同一印记压出同样形状的东西共享同一个模子。

senses.title: A person as an example of a kind
senses.definition: a person who shows the characteristic features of a kind, as in the sporty type
senses.definitionCN: 体现出某类特征的人，如 the sporty type（运动型的人）
senses.example: She is not the type to quit halfway.
senses.exampleCN: 她不是那种半途而废的人。
senses.why: The mold works for people too: characters who come out shaped alike form a type.
senses.whyCN: 模子同样适用于人：长得相像的一类人构成一种 type。

senses.title: A printed style of letters
senses.definition: printed letters of a particular design, or the metal pieces once used for printing
senses.definitionCN: 特定样式的印刷字体，或旧时用于印刷的金属活字
senses.example: The poster was set entirely in bold type.
senses.exampleCN: 海报全用粗体字排印。
senses.why: Printing history is preserved in the word: metal sorts cast from one mold are literally types.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保存了印刷史：用同一模具铸出的金属活字正是字面意义的 type。

senses.title: A mark or symbol pressed on a surface
senses.definition: a figure or symbol impressed on a surface, especially in older technical use
senses.definitionCN: 压印在表面上的图形或符号，多见于旧的技术用法
senses.example: Coins from that mint carry the same type of eagle.
senses.exampleCN: 那家铸币厂的钱币带有同一种鹰的印记。
senses.why: Striking an image into metal is the oldest sense of the mold at work.
senses.whyCN: 把图像压进金属是这个「模具」最古老的用法。

senses.title: A thing resembling an earlier model
senses.definition: a person or thing regarded as a symbol or foreshadowing of someone or something later, in religious or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 宗教或文学用法中，被视为后来者之象征或预示的人或事物
senses.example: In medieval readings, Jonah was a type of Christ.
senses.exampleCN: 在中世纪解经传统里，约拿被视为基督的预表。
senses.why: The mold precedes what it casts: the earlier figure stamps the shape of the later one.
senses.whyCN: 模具先于铸件：早先的人物为后来者压出了形状。

senses.title: To write with a keyboard
senses.definition: to write text by pressing keys on a typewriter, computer or phone
senses.definitionCN: 通过按打字机、电脑或手机的键来书写文字
senses.example: He typed the whole report in one evening.
senses.exampleCN: 他一个晚上就把整份报告打完了。
senses.why: The verb inherits the printing press: each keypress strikes one piece of type onto the page.
senses.whyCN: 动词继承了印刷机：每敲一键就是向纸面压下一个活字。

senses.title: To classify or identify a kind
senses.definition: to decide which class something belongs to, especially in biology or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 判定某物属于哪一类，尤用于生物学或医学
senses.example: Nurses typed the blood sample before transfusion.
senses.exampleCN: 输血前护士对血样做了血型鉴定。
senses.why: Sorting returns as a verb: assigning each item to its mold is to type it.
senses.whyCN: 分拣变成了动词：把每件东西归入它的模子就是 type 它。

senses.title: To be someone's type: to suit someone's taste
senses.titleCN: 合某人的意；是某人喜欢的类型
senses.definition: in the phrase be someone's type, to be the kind of person that someone finds attractive
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 be someone's type，指属于某人心仪的那一类人
senses.example: He is kind and funny, but honestly not my type.
senses.exampleCN: 他善良又风趣，但说实话不是我喜欢的类型。
senses.why: Attraction is sorting with the heart: some people simply come out of your mold and others do not.
senses.whyCN: 吸引力就是用心的分拣：有些人恰好出自你的模子，有些人则不然。

intro.en: Type came into English from Latin typus, itself from Greek for the blow of a stamp.
intro.cn: type 经拉丁语 typus 进入英语，其源头是希腊语中表示「压印一击」的词。

items.en: *steyk- is generally reconstructed as 'to stick, prick'; its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *steyk- 意为「刺入、扎入」；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Greek typos meant 'a blow, an impression left by a blow, a figure in relief', built on the verb typtein 'to strike'.
items.cn: 希腊语 typos 意为「一击；击打留下的印痕；浮雕图形」，建立在动词 typtein「击打」之上。

items.en: Latin typus borrowed the Greek word for an image, figure or form.
items.cn: 拉丁语 typus 借用该希腊词，指图像、形象或形式。

items.en: The word passed through late Latin and Old French tipus, typo as a learned borrowing.
items.cn: 该词经晚期拉丁语与古法语作为学术借词流传。

items.en: English took the word for an emblem, figure or typical form; printing adopted it for cast metal sorts in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语借入该词指图像、象征或典型形式；十七世纪印刷业用它称呼铸出的金属活字。

items.en: The typewriter gave the verb its modern keyboard sense, and biological classification spread the sorting sense.
items.cn: 打字机的发明赋予动词现代键盘义，生物分类学则推广了归类义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the typos family and same-form neighbors; the near-meaning group gathers words of class, kind and printing.
note.cn: 形近组收 typos 词族与同形近邻词；近义组收类别、种类与印刷相关词。

entries.definition: Having the distinctive features of a type; the direct adjective of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「典型的」，是本词族直接的形容词形式。

entries.definition: A machine for writing by striking keys; compound of type plus writer.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「打字机」，由 type 与 writer 构成的复合词。

entries.definition: A fixed, oversimplified image of a kind; originally a solid printing plate cast from type.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「刻板印象」，原义指由活字铸出的整版印刷版。

entries.definition: An original model on which copies are based; the same Greek ending with a prefix meaning first.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「原型」，加表示「最初的」前缀的同一希腊词尾。

entries.definition: A flat piece used to cover roofs or walls; merely rhymes with type and has a separate Germanic origin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「瓦片；瓷砖」，只是与 type 押韵，属另一日耳曼语源。

entries.definition: A natural class of things; the everyday native word for a category.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「种类」，是表示类别的本族日常用词。

entries.definition: A class, especially among people; from Latin sors, a lot drawn by chance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「种类（尤指人）」，源自拉丁语 sors「抽签所得」。

entries.definition: A division in a system of classification; formal and systematic.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「类别；范畴」，正式且体系化。

entries.definition: A group ranked or grouped together, in society or in classification.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「阶级；类别」，用于社会分层或科学分类。

entries.definition: The basic unit of biological classification; narrower and scientific.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「物种」，指生物分类的基本单位，范围更窄且更科学。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Greek stamp root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的希腊「压印」词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Greek typos is a stamp mark: one blow, one shared shape.
normal.cn: 希腊语 typos 是压印的痕迹：一击之下，同一种形状。

normal.en: Archetype and stereotype both end in type: original mold, copied mold.
normal.cn: archetype 和 stereotype 都以 type 结尾：原初之模与复制之模。

normal.en: Metal type is the printer's mold: each letter cast from one form.
normal.cn: 金属活字是印刷者的模具：每个字母都由同一形式铸出。

normal.en: To type is to strike keys, one small blow per letter.
normal.cn: 打字（type）就是敲键，每个字母一次小小的「击打」。

normal.en: Type A blood is blood sorted into its mold.
normal.cn: A 型血就是被归入自己模子的血。

abstract.en: Picture a tray of compartments: each item slides into the box shaped like it.
abstract.cn: 想象一排分格匣：每件东西滑进与它形状相同的格子。

abstract.en: A stamp pressed once makes a family of identical impressions.
abstract.cn: 压印一次，就能造出一整族相同的印记。

abstract.en: People are sorted too, though no mold is visible.
abstract.cn: 人也会被归类，尽管模子并不可见。

examples.en: Which type of soil suits these flowers best?
examples.cn: 哪种土壤最适合这些花？

examples.en: Please type your name and address into the form.
examples.cn: 请把你的姓名和地址键入表格。

examples.en: The headline was printed in very large type.
examples.cn: 标题用很大的字体排印。

root: 希腊语 typos「一击；压痕；浮雕图形」由动词 typtein「击打」构成，经拉丁语 typus 进入英语；一般认为词源可溯至原始印欧语 *steyk-「刺入」（重构形式），同族词有 archetype、stereotype、typical 等。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of type all come from one stamped mold: shared classes of things and people, printed letters, struck marks, foreshadowing models, and the keyboard verb that still strikes one letter at a time.
sensesIntro.cn: type 的八个义项都出自同一个压印模子：事物与人的共同类别、印刷字体、压制的印记、预兆性的范型，以及至今仍逐一「击打」字母的键盘动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one stamp pressed many times produces a family of identical shapes.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一枚印章压印多次，产出一族相同的形状。

branches.en: THE CLASS: things and people sharing one mold form a type.
branches.cn: 类别线：共享一个模子的事物与人构成一种 type。

branches.en: THE PRESS: cast metal letters and struck marks carry the mold into printing.
branches.cn: 印刷线：铸出的金属活字与压制的印记把模子带进印刷。

branches.en: THE FORESHADOW: the earlier figure stamps the shape of the later one.
branches.cn: 预表线：早先的人物为后来者压出形状。

branches.en: THE ACT: striking keys and assigning categories are the mold at work.
branches.cn: 动作线：敲键与归类都是模子在运作。

branches.en: THE HEART: attraction is sorting people into your own mold.
branches.cn: 心意线：吸引力就是把人分进你自己的模子。

intro.en: Type carries the Greek stamp root, and the endings -ic, -ist, -graphy and compounds extend it.
intro.cn: type 带有希腊「压印」词根，-ic、-ist、-graphy 等词尾及复合词把它扩展成词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek typos and Latin typus are both recorded; only the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 typos 与拉丁语 typus 均有文献记录；只有印欧词根属重构形式。

items.exampleCN: 这个动词是每个印痕背后的动作。

items.example: The noun came into English through Latin.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词经拉丁语进入英语。

items.example: It forms stereotype, once a solid printing plate.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 stereotype，原指整块印刷版。

definition_zh: 典型的；有代表性的；一贯的；特有的
definition_en: having the usual features of a kind, so that it serves as a good example of that kind
core_image: 从一摞样本里抽出的那张最标准、最有代表性的
scene: 民俗展的展柜里摆着当地农家最普通的一桌饭菜。This meal is typical of the mountain villages.
sceneCN: 这里 typical 是形容词「典型的、有代表性的」（第 1 个义项：体现某类通常特征）；句意为这顿饭典型地代表了山村人家的饮食。

pos.zh: 形容词：典型的；有代表性的；一贯的；特有的

senses.title: Showing the usual features of a kind
senses.definition: having the qualities that make something a good example of its class
senses.definitionCN: 具有使其成为某类良好范例的特质
senses.example: A typical village house has a tiled roof and a stone wall.
senses.exampleCN: 典型的村舍有瓦顶和石墙。
senses.why: The mold casts one shape many times; the example that matches the mold best is typical.
senses.whyCN: 模子多次铸出同一种形状；与模子最吻合的样本就是典型的。

senses.title: Happening as expected
senses.titleCN: 意料之中的；照常发生的
senses.definition: happening in the way that usually happens in such circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 以这类情形中惯常的方式发生
senses.example: It rained, which was typical for a bank holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 下雨了，这在公共假日再正常不过。
senses.why: Events cast by the same mold repeat: what recurs is the typical case.
senses.whyCN: 同一模子铸出的事件会重演：反复出现的就是 typical 的情况。

senses.title: Characteristic of a person, often annoyingly
senses.definition: showing a person's usual behavior, often used with mild criticism
senses.definitionCN: 表现出某人惯常的行为，常带轻微批评
senses.example: Typical — he promises to help, then disappears.
senses.exampleCN: 老样子——他答应帮忙，然后就不见了。
senses.why: The person's habits are their mold: the familiar casting is greeted with a sigh.
senses.whyCN: 习惯是一个人的模子：熟悉的「铸件」出现时，人们报以一声叹息。

senses.title: Serving as a symbol of a larger group
senses.titleCN: 代表性的；可作群体缩影的
senses.definition: chosen or regarded as representative of a whole group, as in a typical voter
senses.definitionCN: 被选作或视为能代表整个群体的，如 typical voter（典型选民）
senses.example: The magazine interviewed a typical family of four for its survey.
senses.exampleCN: 杂志为调查采访了一个典型的四口之家。
senses.why: One casting is held up so the whole mold can be seen through it.
senses.whyCN: 拿出一件「铸件」，让人透过它看清整个模子。

senses.title: Distinctive of a place or period
senses.titleCN: 特有的；某地某时所独有的
senses.definition: belonging characteristically to a particular place, time or culture
senses.definitionCN: 为特定地点、时代或文化所特有
senses.example: Olive groves are typical of the Mediterranean coast.
senses.exampleCN: 橄榄园是地中海沿岸的典型景观。
senses.why: The mold belongs to the region: whatever it casts there carries the local mark.
senses.whyCN: 模子属于那片土地：在当地铸出的东西都带着地方的印记。

senses.title: In science: the standard form
senses.definition: in technical use, serving as the standard or type specimen for a group
senses.definitionCN: 技术用法中，作为某类群的标准或模式标本
senses.example: The museum keeps a typical specimen of the beetle species.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆保存着该甲虫物种的模式标本。
senses.why: Science fixes one casting as the reference for all comparisons within the kind.
senses.whyCN: 科学把一件「铸件」固定为该类内一切比较的参照。

senses.title: Typical of its kind in literature and art
senses.titleCN: 艺术中类型化的人物或场景
senses.definition: in criticism, portraying a character or scene that embodies the essential features of its class
senses.definitionCN: 批评用语，指塑造能体现该类本质特征的人物或场景
senses.example: The novel's hero is a typical figure of the restless 1920s.
senses.exampleCN: 小说主人公是躁动的二十世纪二十年代的典型形象。
senses.why: Art compresses the mold into one figure so that readers grasp the whole kind at a glance.
senses.whyCN: 艺术把模子压缩进一个人物，让读者一眼看清整类。

senses.title: Typically: the adverb of expectation
senses.definition: in the derived adverb typically, as a rule or as expected
senses.definitionCN: 派生副词 typically 中，表示「按惯例、如预期」
senses.example: Typically, the ceremony begins at sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 按惯例，仪式在日出时开始。
senses.why: The mold works in time as well: each recurrence follows the cast pattern.
senses.whyCN: 模子同样在时间中运作：每次重演都遵循既定的铸型。

intro.en: Typical is built on the Greek stamp noun typos through late Latin typicalis.
intro.cn: typical 建立在希腊语「压印」名词 typos 之上，经晚期拉丁语 typicalis 传入。

items.en: Greek typos meant 'a blow, an impression, a figure'; it is the root of the whole family.
items.cn: 希腊语 typos 意为「一击；压痕；图形」，是整个词族的根源。

items.en: Late Latin typicalis meant 'of a figure or image', a learned formation on typus.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 typicalis 意为「属于图像、形象的」，是在 typus 上构成的学术用词。

items.en: Medieval writers used typicalis for symbolic or foreshadowing figures in scripture.
items.cn: 中世纪作者用 typicalis 指圣经中象征性或预表性的人物。

items.en: English adopted the word in the seventeenth century with the religious foreshadowing sense.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入该词，当时带着宗教预表的含义。

items.en: The sense shifted to 'serving as a type or representative', and then to the everyday 'usual'.
items.cn: 词义转向「作为典型或代表」，继而发展为日常的「惯常的」。

items.en: Today typical spans science, art criticism and everyday speech.
items.cn: 如今 typical 兼用于科学、艺术批评与日常口语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the typos family; the near-meaning group gathers words of representativeness and regularity.
note.cn: 形近组收 typos 词族；近义组收表示代表性与惯常性的词。

entries.definition: A class or kind; the noun from which typical is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「类型」，是构成 typical 的基础词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning usually or characteristically.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「通常；典型地」，由本词直接派生。

entries.definition: Not typical; the negated counterpart with the prefix a-.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「非典型的」，加否定前缀 a- 构成。

entries.definition: Showing a fixed, oversimplified image; built on stereotype.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「刻板印象的」，建立在 stereotype 之上。

entries.definition: Of the tropics; sounds and looks close to typical but comes from the Greek word for a turning point, tropos.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「热带的」，音形与 typical 相近，但出自希腊语 tropos「回归线、转向」。

entries.definition: Typical of a person or thing; stresses the distinguishing feature.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「特有的；典型的」，强调区分性特征。

entries.definition: Serving to show the whole class; stresses standing for the group.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有代表性的」，强调为群体代言。

entries.definition: Happening most often; the plain native word for what normally occurs.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「通常的」，是表示常态的本族常用词。

entries.definition: A perfect example of a kind, often admired; carries approval.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「典型的；经典的」，常含赞许。

entries.definition: The most perfect embodiment of a quality; elevated in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最典型的；精髓的」，语气庄重。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real stamp root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的「压印」词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Typical is type plus -ical: having the qualities of the type.
normal.cn: typical 就是 type 加 -ical：具备该类型应有的特质。

normal.en: Typical of means this example stands for the whole class.
normal.cn: typical of 意为这个例子足以代表整个类别。

normal.en: A typical specimen is the reference sample kept in museums.
normal.cn: typical specimen 是博物馆保存的参照标本。

normal.en: Typical — said alone — often means how annoyingly predictable.
normal.cn: 单独说 typical 常表示「老一套，真没意外」。

normal.en: Atypical simply puts an a- of negation in front.
normal.cn: atypical 只是在前面加了个表否定的 a-。

abstract.en: Hold up one cast shape and see the whole mold through it.
abstract.cn: 举起一件铸件，透过它看清整个模子。

abstract.en: The middle of the bell curve is where the typical lives.
abstract.cn: 钟形曲线的中部就是「典型」栖身之处。

abstract.en: Predictability can comfort or annoy; typical carries both tones.
abstract.cn: 可预料既能安慰也能惹人厌；typical 两种语气兼备。

examples.en: The interviewees were chosen as typical users of the app.
examples.cn: 受访者是作为这款应用的典型用户挑选的。

examples.en: It was a typical summer morning, hot and completely still.
examples.cn: 那是个典型的夏日清晨，炎热而一丝风都没有。

examples.en: Typical of her, she arrived last and left first.
examples.cn: 她一贯如此：最后一个到，第一个走。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踢皮扣」——一踢皮扣就弹回原样，一贯如此：典型的

root: 希腊语 typos「压痕、图形」经晚期拉丁语 typicalis「属于图像的」进入英语；词根 typos 由动词 typtein「击打」构成，与 type、archetype、stereotype 同族；更早的印欧词根 *steyk-「刺入」属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of typical all hold one casting up to the mold: good examples of a kind, expected events, familiar personal habits, group symbols, regional marks, standard specimens and literary embodiments.
sensesIntro.cn: typical 的八个义项都把一件「铸件」举到模子前：某类的良好范例、意料之中的事件、熟悉的个人习惯、群体象征、地方印记、标准标本与文学典型。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one cast sample is held up beside the mold that produced it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件铸样被举在产出它的模子旁边。

branches.en: THE EXAMPLE: the sample that best matches the mold stands for the class.
branches.cn: 范例线：与模子最吻合的样本为整个类别代言。

branches.en: THE EXPECTED: events and habits that repeat follow the cast pattern.
branches.cn: 预期线：反复出现的事件与习惯遵循既定铸型。

branches.en: THE SIGH: a person's mold shows again, and the word carries mild reproach.
branches.cn: 叹息线：一个人的模子再度显现，词语带上轻微的责备。

branches.en: THE REGION: local molds give local marks.
branches.cn: 地域线：地方的模子打出地方的印记。

branches.en: THE REFERENCE: science and art fix one casting as the standard of the kind.
branches.cn: 参照线：科学与艺术把一件铸件定为该类的标准。

definition_zh: 轮胎；车胎（美式拼写为 tire）
definition_en: the thick rubber ring fitted around the wheel of a car, bicycle or other vehicle
core_image: 套在车轮外圈的一只厚橡胶环，接触地面的黑圈
scene: 暴雨刚停，修车师傅蹲在路边检查一辆车的黑胶轮圈。The mechanic found a nail stuck in the front tyre.
sceneCN: 这里 tyre 是名词「轮胎」（第 1 个义项：套在车轮外的橡胶圈）；句意为修车师傅发现前轮的轮胎上扎着一枚钉子。

pos.zh: 名词：轮胎；车胎（英式拼写，美式为 tire）

collocations.zh: 备用轮胎；（俚语）腰间赘肉

derivatives.zh: 美式拼写的同词，义为「轮胎」；另有动词 tire「使疲倦」，两者词源不同
