senses.title: The rubber ring on a wheel
senses.definition: the thick rubber band fitted around the rim of a vehicle wheel, filled with air or solid
senses.definitionCN: 套在车轮轮辋外的厚橡胶圈，可为充气式或实心
senses.example: Check the tyre pressure before a long drive.
senses.exampleCN: 长途驾驶前先检查胎压。
senses.why: The core image is the band that meets the road: everything the wheel feels passes through it.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是接触路面的那圈橡胶：车轮感受的一切都要经过它。

senses.title: A punctured or worn tyre
senses.definition: a tyre that has lost air or whose surface has worn out, needing repair or replacement
senses.definitionCN: 漏气或胎面磨耗到需修补更换的轮胎
senses.example: The flat tyre forced them to stop at the roadside.
senses.exampleCN: 瘪胎迫使他们停在路边。
senses.why: The band can fail: air escapes or the surface wears, and the wheel loses its cushion.
senses.whyCN: 这圈橡胶会失效：气跑了或胎面磨光，车轮失去缓冲。

senses.title: Spare tyre as the extra wheel
senses.definition: the extra tyre carried in a vehicle for use when one fails
senses.definitionCN: 车辆随车携带、供轮胎失效时替换的备用轮胎
senses.example: The spare tyre is under the boot floor.
senses.exampleCN: 备胎在行李箱底板下面。
senses.why: A copy of the band travels with the car, ready to take over the road contact.
senses.whyCN: 汽车的随行「替补圈」，随时准备接手与路面的接触。

senses.title: Spare tyre as waist fat
senses.definition: in informal British use, a roll of fat around a person's waist
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中，指绕在腰间的一圈肥肉
senses.example: Years of desk work gave him a spare tyre.
senses.exampleCN: 多年伏案工作让他腰间长了一圈赘肉。
senses.why: The round band is imagined strapped around the middle of the body.
senses.whyCN: 把那只环状的圈想象成套在身体中段的带子。

senses.title: Tyre tracks as evidence of passage
senses.definition: the marks left on a surface by tyres, used to trace where a vehicle went
senses.definitionCN: 轮胎在地面留下的痕迹，用于追查车辆去向
senses.example: Fresh tyre tracks led down the muddy lane.
senses.exampleCN: 新鲜的轮胎印一直延伸到泥泞的小路深处。
senses.why: The band writes its pattern on the ground; the mark names the wheel that made it.
senses.whyCN: 橡胶圈在大地上印出花纹；痕迹替那只车轮署名。

senses.title: Racing tyre types
senses.definition: specially designed tyres for racing, weather or terrain, such as slicks or snow tyres
senses.definitionCN: 为竞速、气候或地形特制的轮胎，如光头胎或雪地胎
senses.example: The team switched to wet tyres as the rain began.
senses.exampleCN: 开始下雨后，车队换上了雨胎。
senses.why: The same band is engineered differently for each road condition.
senses.whyCN: 同一只圈针对不同路况被设计成不同形态。

senses.title: To tyre a vehicle (technical)
senses.titleCN: 给车辆装配轮胎（技术用法）
senses.definition: in technical or commercial use, to fit tyres to a vehicle or wheel
senses.definitionCN: 技术或商业用法，指为车辆或车轮装配轮胎
senses.example: The fleet was tyred with winter rubber before November.
senses.exampleCN: 十一月前整个车队都换装了冬季胎。
senses.why: The noun turns into a rare verb: putting the band onto the rim.
senses.whyCN: 名词转出少见的动词：把橡胶圈装上轮辋。

senses.title: Tyre as a cushion between vehicle and road
senses.definition: in engineering discussion, the tyre regarded as the layer that absorbs shocks and grips the road
senses.definitionCN: 工程讨论中，把轮胎视为吸收震动、抓附路面的功能层
senses.example: Modern tyres grip the wet road far better than old designs.
senses.exampleCN: 现代轮胎在湿滑路面上的抓地力远胜旧设计。
senses.why: Beyond being a ring, the band is the only contact point, so it carries grip and comfort.
senses.whyCN: 不只是个环，它是唯一的接地点，因此承担抓地与舒适。

intro.en: Tyre (British) and tire (American) share one history, but that history is genuinely tangled.
intro.cn: 英式 tyre 与美式 tire 共享同一段历史，而这段历史确实纠缠不清。

items.en: The verb tire is generally linked to Old French tirer 'to draw, pull'; the noun's earliest English sense was the iron hoop around a cart wheel.
items.cn: 动词 tire 一般与古法语 tirer「拉、拽」相关；该名词在英语中最早指套在车轮外的铁箍。

items.en: The wheel tire began as the metal band that 'dressed' or bound the wooden wheel.
items.cn: 车轮的 tire 起初是「束缚」或包箍木轮的金属圈。

items.en: When rubber replaced iron, the word transferred to the rubber band; both spellings tyre and tire were used.
items.cn: 橡胶取代铁箍后，词义转指橡胶圈；tyre 与 tire 两种拼法并行。

items.en: In the nineteenth century, British usage settled on tyre and American usage on tire; the split is conventional, not etymological.
items.cn: 十九世纪英式拼法定为 tyre，美式为 tire；这一分裂是约定俗成，并非词源差异。

items.en: The unrelated verb tire 'to fatigue' comes from Old English tēorian and is a different word altogether.
items.cn: 表示「使疲倦」的美式动词 tire 来自古英语 tēorian，完全是另一个词。

items.en: Today the hoop word is tyre in Britain and most Commonwealth countries, tire in North America.
items.cn: 如今「轮箍」一词在英国及多数英联邦国家拼作 tyre，在北美拼作 tire。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the spellings and the fatigue word; the near-meaning group gathers wheel and ring words.
note.cn: 形近组收各拼写变体与「疲倦」同形词；近义组收车轮与环状物词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the wheel band; also a different verb meaning to fatigue.
entries.definitionCN: 美式拼法的「轮胎」；另有一个不相干的动词义「使疲倦」。

entries.definition: Fitted with a specified kind of tyre, as in wide-tyred; distinct from tired meaning sleepy.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指装有某种轮胎的，如 wide-tyred；与表示困倦的 tired 不同。

entries.definition: Sleepy or fatigued, from the Old English verb tēorian; merely shares the sound with tyre.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「疲倦的」，出自古英语动词 tēorian，与 tyre 仅同音。

entries.definition: A row or level in a structure; spelled one letter differently and pronounced almost the same, but a different word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一排；一层」，拼写仅差一个字母、读音几乎相同，但属另一个词。

entries.definition: Formal clothing; built on the Old French tirer family that also gave the wheel band its name.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「服装、盛装」，与「轮箍」同出古法语 tirer 词族。

entries.definition: The whole rotating device; the tyre is only its outer band.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「车轮」，指整体；轮胎只是其外圈。

entries.definition: The metal circle the tyre fits onto; the tyre's partner part.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「轮辋」，是轮胎安装其上的金属圈。

entries.definition: A circular band; the historical ancestor's own family word for a binding ring.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「箍环」，正是历史前身「铁箍」的同族词。

entries.definition: The patterned surface of a tyre that grips the road.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「胎面花纹」，是轮胎上抓地的那层。

entries.definition: The air-filled tube inside older tyre designs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指旧式轮胎内部充气的内胎。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real drawing root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的「拉拽」词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: The old wheel tire was a metal hoop drawn tight around the wheel.
normal.cn: 旧时的车轮 tire 是紧紧箍住轮子的金属圈。

normal.en: British tyre, American tire: same band, two spellings.
normal.cn: 英式 tyre、美式 tire：同一只圈，两种拼法。

normal.en: Tired drivers check tyres: the two words only sound alike.
normal.cn: 疲倦的司机也要检查轮胎：这两个词只是听起来像。

normal.en: Tyre pressure is checked with a gauge before every long trip.
normal.cn: 每次长途前都用胎压表检查胎压。

normal.en: Spare tyre means either the backup wheel or, as a joke, waist fat.
normal.cn: spare tyre 既指备胎，也是腰间赘肉的玩笑话。

abstract.en: Picture a black rubber bracelet gripping the road at one thin patch.
abstract.cn: 想象一只黑色橡胶手镯，以薄薄一小块紧贴路面。

abstract.en: The car never touches the earth directly; only the band does.
abstract.cn: 汽车从不直接触地；接触大地的只有那圈橡胶。

abstract.en: A worn band is a conversation with the road that has run out of words.
abstract.cn: 磨光的胎面就是一场与路面无话可说的对话。

examples.en: A nail in the left rear tyre left the car leaning to one side.
examples.cn: 左后轮扎了钉子，车身向一侧倾斜。

examples.en: Racing teams choose their tyres carefully for each track surface.
examples.cn: 赛车队针对每条赛道的路面仔细选择轮胎。

examples.en: He jacked up the car and changed the flat tyre in ten minutes.
examples.cn: 他架起千斤顶，十分钟就换好了瘪胎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太耳」——轮胎贴地，路面声音太吵到耳朵：轮胎

root: 轮箍义一般认为源自古法语 tirer「拉、拽」相关词形，最早指束缚木轮的金属箍；十九世纪橡胶取代铁箍后转指橡胶圈；英式拼法 tyre 与美式 tire 的分化属约定俗成；表示「疲倦」的动词 tire 出自古英语 tēorian，与轮箍义词源不同。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of tyre all belong to one road-going band: the ring itself, its failures, its spare, its comic double at the waist, the tracks it leaves, its racing variants, the act of fitting it, and its role as the car's only grip.
sensesIntro.cn: tyre 的八个义项都属于同一只行路之圈：圈本身、它的失效、备胎、腰间的滑稽翻版、它留下的车辙、竞速变体、装配动作，以及它作为车辆唯一抓地层的角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black rubber band is the only part of the car that touches the road.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑色橡胶圈是全车唯一触地的部分。

branches.en: THE GRIP: the band engineered for the road, from everyday to racing rubber.
branches.cn: 抓地线：为路面而设计的橡胶圈，从日常到竞速。

branches.en: THE FAILURE: air lost or surface worn, the wheel loses its cushion.
branches.cn: 失效线：漏气或磨耗，车轮失去缓冲。

branches.en: THE DOUBLE: a spare band on board, and the joke copy around the waist.
branches.cn: 替补线：随车的备胎，以及腰间的滑稽翻版。

branches.en: THE SIGN: the ground remembers which band passed.
branches.cn: 痕迹线：大地记得哪只圈经过。

branches.en: THE FITTING: putting the band onto the rim.
branches.cn: 装配线：把橡胶圈装上轮辋。

intro.en: Tyre is a bare root word; its family lives in compounds and spellings rather than suffixes.
intro.cn: tyre 是一个裸词根；其词族主要体现在复合词与拼写变体上，而非后缀。

latinIntro.en: The word is French and Germanic in origin, so there are no Latin cognates to list; the Old French link is the generally accepted account.
latinIntro.cn: 该词源于法语与日耳曼语，故没有拉丁同族词可列；与古法语的关联是公认的说法。

items.example: The verb is the accepted starting point for the band word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是「轮箍」一词公认的起点。

items.example: It shares the Old French family.
items.exampleCN: 它与「轮箍」同出古法语词族。

items.example: It gives the unrelated tired and tire.
items.exampleCN: 它给出不相干的 tired 与动词 tire。

items.example: It names the part of the band that meets the road.
items.exampleCN: 它命名橡胶圈触地的那一面。

derivatives.zh: 美式拼写的同词，义为「轮胎」；另有动词 tire「使疲倦」，词源不同
由本词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「装了某种轮胎的」

definition_zh: 丑陋的；难看的；令人不快的；丑恶的；有威胁性的
definition_en: unpleasant to look at, or unpleasant, threatening or morally bad in a situation or behavior
core_image: 让人移不开眼又不敢多看的脸或场面
scene: 地窖的旧镜子上蒙着灰，镜面裂纹交错，映出的脸都变了形。The cracked mirror made every face look ugly.
sceneCN: 这里 ugly 是形容词「难看的」（第 1 个义项：外观令人不快）；句意为裂了的镜子让每张脸都显得难看。

pos.zh: 形容词：丑陋的；难看的；令人不快的；丑恶的
名词（the ugly）：丑陋的事物（如 the good, the bad and the ugly）

collocations.zh: 恶劣的情绪；不妙的气氛
场面变得难看；冲突升级

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「丑陋；丑恶；恶劣（的局势）」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「弄丑；丑化」（罕用，见于游戏化语源传统）

senses.title: Unpleasant to look at
senses.definition: offensive or unpleasant to the eye, as of faces, buildings or objects
senses.definitionCN: 就面孔、建筑或物品而言，外观令人不快或反感
senses.example: The factory chimney is the ugliest building in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 那座工厂烟囱是山谷里最丑的建筑。
senses.why: The core image is the eye turning away: what we see repels instead of invites.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是目光躲开：所见之物排斥而非吸引视线。

senses.title: Unpleasant to hear
senses.definition: harsh or unpleasant to the ear, as of sounds or voices
senses.definitionCN: 就声音或嗓音而言，刺耳或令人不适
senses.example: The machinery gave off an ugly grinding noise.
senses.exampleCN: 机器发出难听的摩擦声。
senses.why: The turning-away of the eye is shared by the ear: harsh sound repels hearing too.
senses.whyCN: 耳朵与眼睛一样会「躲开」：刺耳之声同样排斥听觉。

senses.title: Threatening, likely to turn violent
senses.titleCN: 有威胁性的；可能失控的
senses.definition: likely to become violent or unpleasant, as of crowds, weather or moods
senses.definitionCN: 就人群、天气或情绪而言，可能走向暴力或恶化
senses.example: The crowd grew ugly when the gates failed to open.
senses.exampleCN: 大门迟迟不开，人群的情绪开始不妙。
senses.why: The repelling surface becomes a sign of danger: what looks wrong is about to turn worse.
senses.whyCN: 排斥性的外表成了危险的信号：看起来不对劲，就快要更糟了。

senses.title: Morally bad, shameful
senses.definition: morally offensive or shameful, as of deeds, lies or prejudices
senses.definitionCN: 就行为、谎言或偏见而言，道德上令人反感、可耻
senses.example: The trial exposed the ugly prejudice behind the policy.
senses.exampleCN: 庭审揭露了政策背后丑恶的偏见。
senses.why: The inner eye recoils just as the outer eye did; bad character is unpleasant to behold.
senses.whyCN: 内心的目光像外在的眼睛一样后缩；恶劣的品性同样令人不忍直视。

senses.title: Unpleasant or difficult in a situation
senses.definition: unpleasant, awkward or hard to settle, as of situations, truths or scenes
senses.definitionCN: 就局面、真相或场景而言，令人难堪、尴尬或难以收拾
senses.example: The merger negotiations turned ugly over money.
senses.exampleCN: 并购谈判因钱的问题变得难堪。
senses.why: A scene can repel as a face does; the unpleasant whole inherits the word of the unpleasant look.
senses.whyCN: 场面会像面孔一样令人排斥；令人不快的整体承袭了令人不快的外表之名。

senses.title: Ugly weather or conditions
senses.definition: severe, threatening or unpleasant, as of weather, seas or driving conditions
senses.definitionCN: 就天气、海况或路况而言，严峻、险恶或恶劣
senses.example: Ugly clouds were building over the ridge by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 到中午，山脊上空已聚起险恶的乌云。
senses.why: The sky wears a face too, and this one repels: dark, low and about to break.
senses.whyCN: 天空也有「脸色」，这一副令人回避：阴沉、低垂、即将变天。

senses.title: The ugly as a class of things
senses.definition: in phrases like the good, the bad and the ugly, ugliness treated as a category alongside good and bad
senses.definitionCN: 在 the good, the bad and the ugly 等短语中，与「好」「坏」并列的一类——丑
senses.example: Every project review has the good, the bad and the ugly.
senses.exampleCN: 每次项目复盘都有好的一面、坏的一面和难堪的一面。
senses.why: The adjective is turned into a noun: ugliness takes its seat beside good and bad.
senses.whyCN: 形容词升格为名词：丑在好坏之侧占了一席。

senses.title: The ugly duckling: late bloomer
senses.titleCN: 丑小鸭：起初不起眼后来出众者
senses.definition: in the phrase ugly duckling, a person or thing neglected at first but admired later
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 ugly duckling，指起初受冷落、后来令人赞叹的人或事物
senses.example: The old dockyard became the city's prettiest park — a real ugly duckling story.
senses.exampleCN: 旧船坞变成了全城最美的公园——一个真正的丑小鸭故事。
senses.why: From Andersen's tale: the rejected young bird grows into a swan.
senses.whyCN: 典出安徒生童话：被嫌弃的雏鸟长成了天鹅。

intro.en: Ugly comes from Old Norse, a compound of fear and a word for dread.
intro.cn: ugly 来自古诺斯语，由表示「恐惧」的词加表示「畏惧」的词根复合而成。

items.en: *aghas- is generally reconstructed as 'horror, guilt'; the deeper trail is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *aghas- 意为「恐怖、罪愆」；更早的脉络不确定。

items.en: Old Norse uggligr meant 'dreadful, fearful', from ugga 'to fear, dread'.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 uggligr 意为「可怕的」，出自动词 ugga「畏惧」。

items.en: The word entered English through Norse settlement in the Danelaw, as ugligr or usslig.
items.cn: 该词经诺斯人在丹麦区的定居进入英语，作 ugligr 或 usslig。

items.en: Middle English used it chiefly for dreadful or terrifying things, not merely plain looks.
items.cn: 中古英语中它主要指可怕的、令人恐惧之物，并不只指相貌平平。

items.en: The sense narrowed to visual unattractiveness and then spread to sounds, weather and morals.
items.cn: 词义收窄为「外观不美」，继而扩展到声音、天气与道德。

items.en: Modern use keeps all the strands: looks, sounds, threats, morals and the ugly duckling of the fairy tale.
items.cn: 现代用法保留了各条脉络：外貌、声音、威胁、道德，以及童话里的丑小鸭。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers Norse-family words and sound-alikes; the near-meaning group gathers unattractive and threatening words.
note.cn: 形近组收诺斯语词族与音近词；近义组收不美观与有威胁性的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of being ugly, in looks or in conduct.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「丑陋；丑恶」，指外貌或品行上的丑。

entries.definition: A playful misspelling of ugly seen online; not a separate word.
entries.definitionCN: 网络上对 ugly 的戏谑拼法，并非独立的词。

entries.definition: To stare at someone flirtatiously; sounds close to ugly but comes from Low German oogen, to eye.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抛媚眼地盯着看」，发音与 ugly 相近，但出自低地德语 oogen「用眼盯」。

entries.definition: Vulgar slang for extremely ugly; a blend not suitable for formal use.
entries.definitionCN: 粗俗俚语，指「极其丑陋」，为混合词，不宜正式使用。

entries.definition: The night bird; only the spelling resembles ugly, and the word is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「猫头鹰」，仅拼写与 ugly 相似，词源无关。

entries.definition: Extremely ugly or shocking; stronger and more literary than ugly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「极其丑陋的；骇人的」，比 ugly 更强烈、更书面。

entries.definition: Distorted and unnatural in appearance; adds strangeness to plain unattractiveness.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「怪诞的；丑怪离奇的」，在不美观之上叠加怪异。

entries.definition: Threatening evil; overlaps with ugly in the threatening sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不祥的；阴险的」，与 ugly 的「威胁」义重叠。

entries.definition: Causing strong dislike or disgust; emphasizes pushing away.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人厌恶的」，强调将人推开。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Norse fear root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的诺斯语「恐惧」词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Old Norse ugga is to dread: ugly began as dreadful, not merely plain.
normal.cn: 古诺斯语 ugga 是「畏惧」：ugly 起初指可怕，不只是不好看。

normal.en: An ugly mood in a crowd means trouble is coming.
normal.cn: 人群情绪 ugly 意味着麻烦将至。

normal.en: Ugly weather means dark clouds and hard winds.
normal.cn: ugly weather 指乌云密布、大风恶劣的天气。

normal.en: Get ugly describes a negotiation collapsing into shouting.
normal.cn: get ugly 形容谈判崩坏、变成争吵。

normal.en: The ugly duckling grows into a swan in Andersen's tale.
normal.cn: 安徒生童话里，丑小鸭最终长成天鹅。

abstract.en: Picture an eye sliding away from what it cannot bear to rest on.
abstract.cn: 想象一只目光从无法停留之物上滑开。

abstract.en: A face, a sky and a deed can all wear the same repelling look.
abstract.cn: 面孔、天空与行为可以戴上同一种令人回避的神色。

abstract.en: Ugliness of the inside shows through the surface sooner or later.
abstract.cn: 内在的丑陋迟早会透出表面。

examples.en: The argument got ugly and both families stopped speaking.
examples.cn: 争吵变得难堪，两家人从此不再来往。

examples.en: Concrete towers were once dismissed as ugly, then praised as honest.
examples.cn: 混凝土高楼曾被斥为丑陋，后来又被赞为质朴。

examples.en: The report did not hide the ugly truth about the factory's waste.
examples.cn: 报告没有隐瞒工厂排污的丑恶真相。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿哥李」——阿哥李那张脸实在不敢看：丑陋的

root: 古诺斯语 uggligr「可怕的」出自动词 ugga「畏惧」，一般认为可溯至原始印欧语 *aghas-「恐怖、罪愆」（重构形式）；该词经丹麦区的诺斯定居进入英语，词义由「可怕」收窄为「难看」，再扩展至声音、天气与道德。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of ugly all begin with the eye turning away: ugly looks, harsh sounds, menacing crowds, shameful deeds, awkward scenes, dark weather, the category of the ugly, and the duckling that outgrows the word.
sensesIntro.cn: ugly 的八个义项都始于目光的躲开：难看的外表、刺耳的声音、危险的 crowd、可耻的行为、难堪的局面、阴沉的天气、与好坏并列的「丑」，以及长成天鹅的丑小鸭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the eye turns away from what it cannot bear to look at.
core.cn: 核心意象：目光从无法直视之物上移开。

branches.en: THE SENSES: ugly faces and ugly sounds both repel.
branches.cn: 感官线：难看的脸与难听的声音都令人回避。

branches.en: THE DANGER: menacing crowds and breaking skies wear the warning look.
branches.cn: 危险线：躁动的人群与欲雨的天空挂着警告的神色。

branches.en: THE MORAL AND THE MESS: shameful deeds and awkward scenes inherit the word.
branches.cn: 道德与乱局线：可耻的行为与难堪的局面承袭了这个词。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY: the ugly takes a seat beside the good and the bad.
branches.cn: 范畴线：丑在好与坏之侧就座。

branches.en: THE EXCEPTION: the ugly duckling outgrows the look it was given.
branches.cn: 例外线：丑小鸭超越了人们给它定的外表。

intro.en: Ugly is a compact Norse compound; English adds ordinary suffixes and one famous fairy-tale phrase.
intro.cn: ugly 是一个紧凑的诺斯语复合词；英语为其加上普通后缀和一个著名的童话短语。

latinIntro.en: The word is Norse, not Latin, so there are no Latin cognates to list; the Indo-European root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属诺斯语源而非拉丁语源，故没有拉丁同族词可列；印欧词根属重构形式。

items.example: The verb is the core of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是复合词的核心。
它们构成 uglier 与 ugliest。

items.example: The reconstructed root lies beneath ugga.
items.exampleCN: 这个重构词根是 ugga 的底层。
它只是发音与 ugly 相近。

items.example: It carries the strongest grade of visual offense.
items.exampleCN: 它承载视觉反感的最强级。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「丑陋；丑恶；恶劣（的局势）」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「弄丑；丑化」（罕用）

definition_zh: 最终的；最后的；根本的；极致的；最好的
definition_en: last in a series or process, or greatest, most extreme and most basic of its kind
core_image: 长队排到尽头的那一位，也是压轴出场的最强者
scene: 十年施工的隧道终于全线贯通，剪彩仪式定在最末一日举行。The bridge opening was the ultimate event of the decade-long project.
sceneCN: 这里 ultimate 是形容词「最终的、最后的」（第 1 个义项：序列或过程的末位）；句意为通车典礼是这个长达十年工程的收官大事。

pos.zh: 形容词：最终的；最后的；根本的；极致的
名词：终极；顶点（常用于 the ultimate in ...）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「最终；根本上」
同族拉丁词经借入，义为「最后通牒」
加表示「几乎」的前缀构成，义为「倒数第二的」

senses.title: Last in a series or process
senses.definition: happening or coming at the end of a long series or process
senses.definitionCN: 发生在漫长序列或过程的末尾
senses.example: The merger was the ultimate step in a decade of cooperation.
senses.exampleCN: 这次合并是十年合作的最后一步。
senses.why: The Latin source meant simply the last one; the queue's final member is the ultimate.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原义就是「最后一个」；队列尽头的那位即是 ultimate。

senses.title: Most extreme or greatest of its kind
senses.definition: the greatest, best or most extreme example of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 同类中最好、最强或最极端的例子
senses.example: This car is the ultimate driving machine of its era.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车是那个时代的终极座驾。
senses.why: If nothing comes after the last, the last is also the peak; the end of the line doubles as the top.
senses.whyCN: 既然「最后」之后不再有，末位同时也就是顶点。

senses.title: Fundamental or basic
senses.definition: most basic or fundamental, as of causes, principles or realities
senses.definitionCN: 就原因、原则或现实而言，最为根本
senses.example: Physicists still search for the ultimate nature of matter.
senses.exampleCN: 物理学家仍在探寻物质的根本性质。
senses.why: Dig beneath the layers and the deepest layer is the last one; fundamental equals final.
senses.whyCN: 层层剥开，最深层就是最后一层；「根本」与「最终」在此重合。

senses.title: Supreme in authority
senses.definition: holding the highest or final authority, as of responsibility or power
senses.definitionCN: 就责任或权力而言，拥有最高或最终决定权
senses.example: The board bears ultimate responsibility for the fund.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会为该基金承担最终责任。
senses.why: Authority also forms a chain; where it stops is where it is ultimate.
senses.whyCN: 权力也构成链条；链条终止之处即为最高。

senses.title: The ultimate sacrifice
senses.definition: in the phrase the ultimate sacrifice, the giving of one's life for a cause
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 the ultimate sacrifice，指为事业献出生命
senses.example: The memorial honours those who paid the ultimate sacrifice.
senses.exampleCN: 纪念碑缅怀那些献出生命的人。
senses.why: Life is the last thing a person can give; nothing stands behind it.
senses.whyCN: 生命是一个人所能给出的最后之物；它背后再无可给。

senses.title: The ultimate in something
senses.definition: as a noun, the finest or most extreme degree of a quality, as in the ultimate in luxury
senses.definitionCN: 名词用法，指某种品质的最高或极端程度，如 the ultimate in luxury
senses.example: The spa claims to be the ultimate in relaxation.
senses.exampleCN: 这家水疗中心自称是放松的极致。
senses.why: The adjective is nominalized: the peak itself becomes the thing named.
senses.whyCN: 形容词名词化：顶点本身成为被命名之物。

senses.title: Ultimate cause versus proximate cause
senses.definition: in philosophy and biology, the deepest cause behind an immediate one
senses.definitionCN: 哲学与生物学中，位于直接原因背后的最深层原因
senses.example: Biologists separate the proximate mechanism from the ultimate cause of a behavior.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家把行为的直接机制与其终极原因分开。
senses.why: Causes stack in layers; the question behind the last question is ultimate.
senses.whyCN: 原因层层叠加；最后一个问题背后的问题即终极问题。

senses.title: Ultimatum: the last word in negotiation
senses.definition: in the related noun ultimatum, a final proposal whose rejection ends negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 同族名词 ultimatum 中，指拒绝即终结谈判的最后提案
senses.example: The union issued an ultimatum before striking.
senses.exampleCN: 工会罢工前发出了最后通牒。
senses.why: The family word keeps the Latin sense of the last: nothing comes after it.
senses.whyCN: 同族词保留了拉丁语「最后」之义：其后不再有别的话。

intro.en: Ultimate is the superlative of the Latin word for last, adopted as a learned borrowing.
intro.cn: ultimate 是拉丁语「最后」一词的最高级形式，作为学术借词进入英语。

items.en: *al- is generally reconstructed as 'to grow, nourish'; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *al- 意为「生长、滋养」；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Latin ultimus meant 'farthest, last', the superlative of ulter or the base of ultra 'beyond'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ultimus 意为「最远的、最后的」，是 ulter 的最高级，与 ultra「越过」同基。

items.en: Medieval Latin ultimatus meant 'reduced to the last, final', formed on ultimus.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 ultimatus 意为「至于最后、终结的」，由 ultimus 构成。

items.en: Ecclesiastical Latin used ultimatus for final states, keeping the superlative force.
items.cn: 教会拉丁语用 ultimatus 表示终结状态，保留最高级力度。

items.en: English adopted ultimate in the seventeenth century in learned and legal contexts for the last or furthest.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 ultimate，用于学术与法律语境，指最后、最远。

items.en: Advertising later stretched the word to mean the best of its kind, adding the modern peak sense.
items.cn: 后来的广告用语把它拉伸为「同类最佳」，添出现代的顶点义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin ultimus family; the near-meaning group gathers last, final and supreme words.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语 ultimus 词族；近义组收最后、最终与最高级词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning finally or fundamentally.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「最终；根本上」，由本词派生。

entries.definition: A final proposal whose rejection ends talks; neuter form of the Latin superlative.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「最后通牒」，是该拉丁最高级的中性形式。

entries.definition: Second to last; built with a prefix meaning almost.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「倒数第二的」，加表示「几乎」的前缀构成。

entries.definition: A prefix and word meaning beyond; shares the Latin base with ultimate.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀兼单词，义为「超越」，与本词同出拉丁语词基。

entries.definition: An extreme opinion or practice, from the same Latin base; rare but real.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「极端主义做法」，出自同一拉丁词基，罕见但真实存在。

entries.definition: Coming at the end; neutral and everyday where ultimate sounds learned or grand.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最后的」，日常中性，而 ultimate 听起来更书面、更宏大。

entries.definition: After all others in order; the plainest member of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最后的」，是该义场中最朴素的成员。

entries.definition: Highest in rank or degree; overlaps with the peak sense of ultimate.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最高的」，与 ultimate 的顶点义重叠。

entries.definition: Happening at last, after delay; stresses the outcome after time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最终的（经过一段时间后）」，强调时间之后的结果。

entries.definition: Forming the end point, often of a process or journey; technical flavor.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「终点的；晚期的」，带技术色彩。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin superlative and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁最高级词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Latin ultimus is the superlative of last: nothing comes after it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 ultimus 是「最后」的最高级：它后面不再有东西。

normal.en: Ultra and ultimate share one base: beyond, then the farthest point.
normal.cn: ultra 与 ultimate 同基：先「越过」，再到最远点。

normal.en: Ultimate responsibility is the duty that cannot be passed on.
normal.cn: ultimate responsibility 是无法转嫁的责任。

normal.en: The ultimate sacrifice means giving one's life.
normal.cn: the ultimate sacrifice 指献出生命。

normal.en: Penultimate is one step before the ultimate.
normal.cn: penultimate 比 ultimate 前一位，即倒数第二。

abstract.en: Picture a queue so long you walk all day, and one person at its far end.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长到你走一整天的队，尽头站着一个人。

abstract.en: The last of the line is also the strongest of the line.
abstract.cn: 队尾之人也是队列中的最强者。

abstract.en: Dig through every layer of soil; the bedrock at the bottom is ultimate.
abstract.cn: 把土层挖穿，最底下的基岩就是 ultimate。

examples.en: Reducing waste is the ultimate goal of the new packaging design.
examples.cn: 减少浪费是新包装设计的最终目标。

examples.en: Many call this city the ultimate food destination.
examples.cn: 许多人称这座城市为美食的终极目的地。

examples.en: The captain holds ultimate authority over the ship.
examples.cn: 船长对这艘船拥有最高权威。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥缇默特」——奥秘到提到最后才默然揭晓：最终的

root: 拉丁语 ultimus「最远的、最后的」为 ulter 的最高级，与 ultra「越过」同基；经中世纪拉丁语 ultimatus 与教会用法进入英语；一般认为词基可溯至原始印欧语 *al-「生长、滋养」（重构形式），同族词有 ultimatum、penultimate、ultra 等。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of ultimate all stand at the end of a line: the last step, the peak, the bedrock cause, the top authority, the final gift, the nominalized peak, the deep cause in science, and the family's last word in negotiation.
sensesIntro.cn: ultimate 的八个义项都立于队伍之末：最后一步、顶点、基岩之因、最高权威、最后的给予、名词化的极点、科学中的深层原因，以及谈判桌上词族的最后通牒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a queue stretches to its farthest end, where the last one stands.
core.cn: 核心意象：队伍伸向最远处，尽头站着最后一位。

branches.en: THE ORDER: the final step and the family's final word in negotiation.
branches.cn: 次序线：最后一步与词族在谈判中的最后一言。

branches.en: THE PEAK: the last doubles as the best, as adjective and as noun.
branches.cn: 顶点线：末位即最佳，形容词与名词两用。

branches.en: THE FOUNDATION: bedrock causes behind every surface layer.
branches.cn: 根基线：一切表层之下的基岩原因。

branches.en: THE AUTHORITY: the chain of power stops where it is ultimate.
branches.cn: 权威线：权力链条终止于最高处。

branches.en: THE GIFT: life is the last thing one can give.
branches.cn: 给予线：生命是人所能给出的最后之物。

intro.en: Ultimate carries the Latin superlative ending -imus, and English adds the ordinary -ly.
intro.cn: ultimate 带有拉丁最高级词尾 -imus，英语再为其加上普通的 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin ultimus, ultimatus and ultra are all recorded; only the Indo-European base is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ultimus、ultimatus 与 ultra 均有文献记录；只有印欧词基属重构形式。

items.example: It is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语该词的直接来源。

items.example: It marks the superlative in ultimus.
items.exampleCN: 它标出 ultimus 的最高级形式。
它构成中世纪拉丁语 ultimatus。

items.example: It belongs to the same last-things field.

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「最终；根本上」
同族拉丁词经借入，义为「最后通牒」
加表示「几乎」的前缀构成，义为「倒数第二的」

definition_zh: 最终；最后；根本上；归根结底
definition_en: in the end, after everything has been considered, or at the most basic level
core_image: 绕了很大一圈之后落定的那一下
scene: 搬家的事商量了三个月，看过八处房子，最后还是定了最初那套。Ultimately, they chose the small flat near the park.
sceneCN: 这里 ultimately 是副词「最终」（第 1 个义项：经过一切考虑之后）；句意为最终他们选定了公园附近那套小公寓。

pos.zh: 副词：最终；根本上；归根结底

derivatives.zh: 本词的形容词形式，义为「最终的；根本的」
同族名词，义为「最后通牒」

senses.title: In the end, after everything
senses.definition: after a long process or after all has been considered, as the final result
senses.definitionCN: 在漫长过程之后或一切考虑之后，作为最终结果
senses.example: The negotiations failed, and the deal ultimately collapsed.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判破裂，交易最终告吹。
senses.why: The adverb points to the end of the queue of events: whatever stands last is what truly happened.
senses.whyCN: 副词指向事件队列的末尾：站在最后的就是真正发生的。

senses.title: Fundamentally, at bottom
senses.definition: at the most basic level of causes or reasons
senses.definitionCN: 在原因或理由的最基本层面上
senses.example: The dispute was ultimately about water rights, not wages.
senses.exampleCN: 争端归根结底是关于水权，而非工资。
senses.why: Strip the surface layers and the deepest layer is what the sentence is really about.
senses.whyCN: 剥开表层，最深一层才是句子的真正所指。

senses.title: Tracing origins back to the source
senses.definition: used to say where something originally came from, through intermediate stages
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明某物经由中间阶段最初来自何处
senses.example: The word ultimately comes from a Greek verb for striking.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词最初源自一个表示「击打」的希腊语动词。
senses.why: The chain of borrowing runs backward until it stops; the stopping point is the ultimate source.
senses.whyCN: 借词链条一路回溯直至停下；停下的那点即终极来源。

senses.title: Ultimately responsible
senses.definition: in phrases about accountability, bearing the final responsibility that cannot be passed on
senses.definitionCN: 用于责任表述，指无法转嫁的最后责任
senses.example: The minister is ultimately responsible for the department's failures.
senses.exampleCN: 部长须为该部门的失误负最终责任。
senses.why: Responsibility climbs the hierarchy until someone at the top holds what remains.
senses.whyCN: 责任沿层级上行，直到顶层的人握住剩余的部分。

senses.title: What ultimately matters
senses.definition: in discussions of value, what counts most when everything else is set aside
senses.definitionCN: 在价值讨论中，撇开其余之后最重要的东西
senses.example: Rank and titles fade; what ultimately matters is trust.
senses.exampleCN: 头衔与级别都会褪色；最终要紧的是信任。
senses.why: Values too stand in a queue; the one at the end outlasts the rest.
senses.whyCN: 价值同样排成队列；站到最后的那个最长久。

senses.title: Eventually successful or settled
senses.definition: describing an outcome reached at last, often after setbacks
senses.definitionCN: 描述历经波折后终于达成的结果
senses.example: The rescue plan was ultimately successful, though costly.
senses.exampleCN: 救援计划终获成功，尽管代价高昂。
senses.why: The winding path is admitted, but its end is what the adverb seals.
senses.whyCN: 迂回之路被承认，但副词盖印的正是它的终点。

senses.title: The deciding turn in an argument
senses.titleCN: （论证中的）归根结底一锤定音
senses.definition: marking the final step of reasoning on which the conclusion rests
senses.definitionCN: 标出推理的最后一步，结论系于其上
senses.example: The data are suggestive, but ultimately only the trial can decide.
senses.exampleCN: 数据有启发意义，但归根结底只有试验才有决定权。
senses.why: Arguments are chains too; the adverb names the link that bears the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 论证同样成链；副词所名的正是承受结论的那一环。

senses.title: Ultimately in historical narrative
senses.definition: in historical writing, the outcome toward which events moved
senses.definitionCN: 历史书写中，事件所趋向的终局
senses.example: The republic ultimately gave way to empire.
senses.exampleCN: 共和国最终让位于帝制。
senses.why: History is read backward from its end, so the narrative adverb naturally marks it.
senses.whyCN: 历史从其终点回读，叙事副词自然落在终局上。

intro.en: Ultimately is the ordinary English adverb of ultimate, with the Latin superlative underneath.
intro.cn: ultimately 是 ultimate 的普通英语副词形式，其下埋着拉丁最高级。

items.en: Latin ultimus meant 'farthest, last', the superlative shared by the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ultimus 意为「最远的、最后的」，是整个词族共享的最高级。

items.en: Medieval Latin ultimatus carried the sense of being brought to the last.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 ultimatus 带有「至于最后」之义。

items.en: The adjective ultimate entered English first, in learned and legal use.
items.cn: 形容词 ultimate 先进入英语，用于学术与法律语境。

items.en: The adverb ultimately followed, first meaning finally in a series, later also fundamentally.
items.cn: 副词 ultimately 随之出现，先表序列中的最终，后亦表根本上。

items.en: Science and philosophy extended it to ultimate causes and ultimate sources.
items.cn: 科学与哲学把它扩展到终极原因与终极来源。

items.en: Today it is a common connector in argument and narrative, marking the decisive end.
items.cn: 如今它是论证与叙事中常见的连接词，标出决定性的终点。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the ultimus family; the near-meaning group gathers finally, basically and at-last words.
note.cn: 形近组收 ultimus 词族；近义组收 finally、basically 等「终了、根本」类词。

entries.definition: The adjective from which this adverb is built.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，是构成本副词的基础。

entries.definition: A final proposal in negotiation; the family's last word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「最后通牒」，词族的最后一言。

entries.definition: Second to last; one step before the ultimate.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「倒数第二的」，比 ultimate 前一位。

entries.definition: Hidden and further in purpose, as in ulterior motive; another Latin comparative of the same base.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「别有用心的； further 的」，如 ulterior motive，是同一词基的拉丁比较级。

entries.definition: Beyond; prefix and word sharing the Latin base.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀兼单词，义为「超越」，与本词同出拉丁语词基。

entries.definition: In the end, after delay; stresses the time it took.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「终于」，强调所费的时间。

entries.definition: At the end, or to introduce a last point; lighter and more everyday.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「最后」，更轻快、更日常。

entries.definition: After waiting or effort; carries relief or impatience.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「终于」，带着如释重负或不耐烦。

entries.definition: At the basic level; overlaps with the root sense of ultimately.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「根本上」，与 ultimately 的根基义重叠。

entries.definition: When everything is finished; the plain phrase counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「到头来」，是本义最平实的对应说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real superlative root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的最高级词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Ultimately is ultimate plus -ly: the adverb of the last thing.
normal.cn: ultimately 就是 ultimate 加 -ly：「最后之事」的副词。

normal.en: Ultimately responsible is the duty that stops with you.
normal.cn: ultimately responsible 是止于你身的责任。

normal.en: Word histories use ultimately from for the first source.
normal.cn: 词源叙述用 ultimately from 指出最初来源。

normal.en: But ultimately marks the point that outweighs the rest of the argument.
normal.cn: but ultimately 标出胜过其余论证的那一点。

normal.en: Ulterior motive is its Latin cousin: the purpose further behind.
normal.cn: ulterior motive 是它的拉丁近亲：藏在更深处的目的。

abstract.en: Watch a long discussion close: one sentence settles it, and that sentence is ultimately.
abstract.cn: 看一场长谈收尾：一句话定局，那句话就是 ultimately。

abstract.en: Every winding road has one final straight stretch.
abstract.cn: 每条迂回的路都有一段最后的直道。

abstract.en: Peel an onion fully and the small core is what remained ultimately.
abstract.cn: 把洋葱剥尽，最终剩下的就是那小小的芯。

examples.en: The project was delayed repeatedly but ultimately finished on budget.
examples.cn: 项目一再延期，但最终在预算内完成。

examples.en: Ultimately, the choice depends on what you value most.
examples.cn: 归根结底，选择取决于你最看重什么。

examples.en: The custom ultimately derives from an ancient harvest rite.
examples.cn: 这一习俗最终源自古代的收获仪式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥缇默特利」——奥秘提到最后，默然特然利落定案：最终

root: 由 ultimate 加副词词尾 -ly 构成；ultimate 源自拉丁语 ultimus「最远的、最后的」（ulter 的最高级，与 ultra 同基），一般认为词基可溯至原始印欧语 *al-「生长、滋养」（重构形式）；同族词有 ultimatum、ulterior、penultimate 等。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of ultimately all name the last point of a line: the end of events, the bottom of causes, the first source, the top of responsibility, the last value, the sealed outcome, the decisive step of an argument, and the end of a history.
sensesIntro.cn: ultimately 的八个义项都指一条线的最后一点：事件的终点、原因的底层、最初的来源、责任的顶端、最后的价值、盖印的结果、论证的决定一步，以及历史的终局。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: after a long winding path, one final point settles everything.
core.cn: 核心意象：长长的迂回之后，最后一个点定夺一切。

branches.en: THE END: outcomes reached, deals sealed, histories closed.
branches.cn: 终点线：结果达成、交易落定、历史收束。

branches.en: THE BOTTOM: basic causes and the decisive link of an argument.
branches.cn: 底层线：根本原因与论证的决定一环。

branches.en: THE SOURCE: tracing a chain back to its first link.
branches.cn: 溯源线：把链条一路回溯到最初一环。

branches.en: THE TOP: responsibility that can climb no further.
branches.cn: 顶端线：无法再上推的责任。

branches.en: THE VALUE: what remains when all else is set aside.
branches.cn: 价值线：撇开其余之后所剩的要紧之物。

intro.en: Ultimately joins the Latin superlative family with the plain English adverb ending.
intro.cn: ultimately 把拉丁最高级词族与朴素的英语副词词尾连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin ultimus and ultimatus are recorded; only the Indo-European base is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ultimus 与 ultimatus 均有记录；只有印欧词基属重构形式。

definition_zh: 不能的；不会的；无能力的
definition_en: lacking the skill, means or opportunity to do something
core_image: 想伸手去做，手却够不着那件东西
scene: 电话铃响到第四声，她刚做完手术的手还打着绷带，怎么也接不起来。She was unable to lift the receiver after the operation.
sceneCN: 这里 unable 是形容词「不能的」（第 1 个义项：缺乏能力或条件去做某事）；句意为手术后她无法拿起听筒。

pos.zh: 形容词：不能的；不会的；无能力的（只作表语，不用于名词前）

collocations.zh: 遗憾地无法（委婉拒绝用语）

derivatives.zh: 同族名词，义为「能力」，unable 即其否定形态的形容词
由 able 加副词后缀构成，义为「能干地」，与本词构成正反对照

senses.title: Lacking the power or skill to do something
senses.definition: not having the physical or mental power, or the skill, needed to do something
senses.definitionCN: 不具备做某事所需的体力、脑力或技能
senses.example: He was unable to walk without support after the injury.
senses.exampleCN: 受伤后他无法独自行走。
senses.why: The core image is the missing arm of the scale: able carries a weight, unable cannot lift it.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是天平上缺失的一端：able 拿得起，unable 拿不起。

senses.title: Lacking the means or opportunity
senses.definition: not having the money, time, tools or circumstances required
senses.definitionCN: 不具备所需的钱、时间、工具或环境条件
senses.example: The family were unable to afford the school fees.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人负担不起学费。
senses.why: The hand that cannot reach is not always weak; sometimes the ladder itself is missing.
senses.whyCN: 够不着的手未必无力；有时缺的是梯子本身。

senses.title: Unable to attend: polite refusal
senses.definition: in invitations and replies, a polite formula for declining
senses.definitionCN: 在邀请与回复中，用于婉拒的礼貌套语
senses.example: I am sorry to say I shall be unable to attend the dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 很遗憾，我将无法出席晚宴。
senses.why: Inability is the politest form of no: the refusal is blamed on circumstances, not on will.
senses.whyCN: 「无法」是最体面的拒绝：把推辞归因于境况而非意愿。

senses.title: Unable to cope: overwhelmed
senses.definition: not having the resources or strength to manage a situation
senses.definitionCN: 没有足够的资源或力量去应对某个局面
senses.example: New parents often feel unable to cope at first.
senses.exampleCN: 新手父母起初常觉得应付不过来。
senses.why: The load exceeds the lifter; the same missing weight returns at the scale of life.
senses.whyCN: 负载超过承力者；天平上缺失的那端在生活的秤上重现。

senses.title: Unable to say or find words
senses.definition: not able to express something in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 无法用言语或文字表达某事
senses.example: She was unable to find the words for her grief.
senses.exampleCN: 她无法用语言形容自己的悲恸。
senses.why: Even expression is an act: what cannot be lifted into words stays heavy inside.
senses.whyCN: 表达也是一种「举」：举不进言辞之物沉重地留在心里。

senses.title: Unable to believe or accept
senses.definition: not able to accept a fact or idea as true
senses.definitionCN: 无法把某个事实或观念当作真实来接受
senses.example: They were unable to believe the news at first.
senses.exampleCN: 起初他们无法相信这个消息。
senses.why: Belief is a grip of the mind; what the mind cannot hold, it cannot accept.
senses.whyCN: 相信是心智的抓握；心智握不住的，便无法接受。

senses.title: Legally or officially unable
senses.definition: prevented by law, rule or contract from doing something
senses.definitionCN: 因法律、规则或合同限制而不能做某事
senses.example: The bank was unable by law to release the records.
senses.exampleCN: 依法银行不能公开这些档案。
senses.why: The ladder can be removed by rules as well as by weakness; prohibition is another missing rung.
senses.whyCN: 梯子既可因无力而缺，也可因规则而被抽走；禁令就是缺失的那一级。

senses.title: Unable to see or hear
senses.definition: lacking the sight or hearing needed to perceive something
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏看见或听见所需的感官能力
senses.example: From the back row they were unable to see the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 从后排他们看不见舞台。
senses.why: Perception is the reach of the senses; beyond that reach, the thing might as well not exist.
senses.whyCN: 感知是感官的「够」；超出够及之处，那东西形同不存在。

intro.en: Unable is the native prefix un- laid on the Old English adjective able.
intro.cn: unable 是在本族前缀 un- 加于古英语形容词 able 之上构成的。

items.en: *h2ebhlus is generally reconstructed as the source of the able family; the deeper trail is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为 able 词族可溯至重构形式 *h2ebhlus；更早的脉络不确定。

items.en: Old English had related forms such as ēaðel and habyl, meaning easy to be held or fit.
items.cn: 古英语有 ēaðel、habyl 等相关形式，意为「易于保有；合适的」。

items.en: The modern adjective came through Old French able, habilé, from Latin habilis 'easy to hold, fit'.
items.cn: 现代形容词经古法语 able、habilé 传入，源自拉丁语 habilis「易握的；合适的」。

items.en: Able was settled in Middle English with the sense of competent or capable.
items.cn: 十四世纪 able 在中古英语中定型，意为「有能力的」。

items.en: The negative unable appears early, building the opposite directly on the word.
items.cn: 否定式 unable 很早出现，直接在 able 之上构成反义。

items.en: Today unable is used only after a verb, chiefly as be unable to.
items.cn: 如今 unable 只用于动词之后，主要作 be unable to。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the un- family and the able family; the near-meaning group gathers cannot, incapable and lacking words.
note.cn: 形近组收 un- 词族与 able 词族；近义组收 cannot、incapable 及表缺乏的词。

entries.definition: Having the skill, power or means; the positive word beneath the negative prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「能够的」，是本词去掉否定前缀后的正面词。

entries.definition: Not lessening; the un-a-b spelling pattern resembles unable without sharing its root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不减弱的」，拼写模式与 unable 相似但词根不同。

entries.definition: Capably; the adverb of able, the positive mirror of unable.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「能干地」，able 的副词形式，与本词互为正反镜像。

entries.definition: Not normal; shares the letter a-b with able but comes from Latin ab- plus norma.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「异常的」，与 able 同含 a-b 字母组合，但源自拉丁语 ab- 加 norma。

entries.definition: Not able to be used or obtained; a longer sibling on the same able stem.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不可用的；无法获得的」，是同一 able 词干上的较长同族词。

entries.definition: Not capable; more permanent in tone, often of persons or qualities.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无能力的」，语气上更显持久，常指人或品质。

entries.definition: The direct verb form of being unable; shorter and plainer.
entries.definitionCN: 情态动词否定式，义为「不能」，比 unable 更直接朴素。

entries.definition: Without power to act or change things; emphasizes strength and authority.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无能为力的」，强调力量与权柄的缺失。

entries.definition: Unable to act for oneself; adds the sense of needing help.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无助的；束手无策的」，兼具需要帮助之义。

entries.definition: Not suitable or qualified for a role; stresses fitness rather than momentary ability.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不胜任的；不合适的」，强调资格与适应，而非一时的能力。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real prefix structure and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的构词结构，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Unable is un- plus able: put not in front of capable.
normal.cn: unable 就是 un- 加 able：在「能够」前面放一个「不」。

normal.en: Be unable to is the fixed frame: it never stands before a noun.
normal.cn: be unable to 是固定句型：它从不放在名词前。

normal.en: Unable to attend is the polite way to say no to an invitation.
normal.cn: unable to attend 是婉拒邀请的礼貌说法。

normal.en: Unable to cope means the load has grown past your strength.
normal.cn: unable to cope 意为负荷已超出你的承受力。

normal.en: Regrettably unable softens a refusal on paper.
normal.cn: regrettably unable 让书面回绝显得委婉。

abstract.en: Picture a hand stretched toward a shelf just beyond its reach.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向差一寸才够得着的书架。

abstract.en: Sometimes the hand is strong and the ladder is missing.
abstract.cn: 有时手很有力，缺的是那架梯子。

abstract.en: Some weights cannot be lifted; some words cannot be said.
abstract.cn: 有些重物举不起；有些话说不出。

examples.en: The airline was unable to confirm the connecting flight.
examples.cn: 航空公司无法确认转接航班。

examples.en: She was unable to hide her disappointment at the result.
examples.cn: 她无法掩饰对结果的失望。

examples.en: We regret we are unable to accept late submissions.
examples.cn: 很遗憾，我们不能接受逾期提交。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安恩博」——安恩博举不动这块石头：不能

root: unable 由本族否定前缀 un- 加 able 构成；able 经古法语 able、habilé 来自拉丁语 habilis「易握的；合适的」；able 词族一般认为可溯至原始印欧语重构形式 *h2ebhlus；反义词为 able。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of unable all measure a gap between wish and reach: strength missing, means missing, polite refusal, overwhelm, silence, disbelief, prohibition, and the senses' own limits.
sensesIntro.cn: unable 的八个义项都在丈量愿望与够及之间的距离：缺力、缺条件、婉拒、应付不来、说不出、难以置信、依法不能，以及感官自身的限度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaches for what it cannot grasp.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸向它握不住的东西。

branches.en: THE BODY: strength and the senses fall short of the task.
branches.cn: 身体线：力量与感官不足以完成任务。

branches.en: THE CONDITIONS: means and rules remove the ladder.
branches.cn: 条件线：手段与规则抽走了梯子。

branches.en: THE COURTESY: inability as the polite form of refusal.
branches.cn: 礼节线：以「无法」为体的婉拒。

branches.en: THE LOAD: when coping fails, the load has outgrown the lifter.
branches.cn: 负荷线：当应对失灵，负载已超过承受者。

branches.en: THE MIND: unspoken grief and disbelief are weights the mind cannot lift.
branches.cn: 心智线：说不出的悲恸与难以置信，都是心智举不起的重量。

intro.en: Unable is a clean two-part word: the negative prefix un- on the able stem.
intro.cn: unable 是个干净的两段式词：否定前缀 un- 加 able 词干。

latinIntro.en: The stem comes from Latin habilis through Old French; the prefix un- is native Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 词干经古法语源自拉丁语 habilis；前缀 un- 则是本族日耳曼语成分。

items.example: It is the Latin stem of able.
items.exampleCN: 它是 able 的拉丁词干。
它把 able 变为 unable。

items.example: It appears in comfortable, unbreakable and kin words.
items.exampleCN: 它见于 comfortable、unbreakable 等同族词。

items.example: It forms abnormal, a mere look-alike.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abnormal，与 unable 只是形近。

items.example: It forms incapable, the near synonym.

items.exampleCN: 它构成 powerless 与 helpless。

items.example: Cannot is the plain verb counterpart.
items.exampleCN: cannot 是其平实的动词对应形式。

derivatives.zh: 同族名词，义为「能力」
本词去掉否定前缀的正面形式，义为「能够的」

definition_zh: 难以置信的；不可信的；惊人的；好得离谱的
definition_en: too unlikely or surprising to be believed, or extremely good or extreme
core_image: 听到消息时猛地停住脚步的那一瞬
scene: 球赛最后一秒，替补队员在半场外把球投了出去，全场屏息。The final shot was simply unbelievable.
sceneCN: 这里 unbelievable 是形容词「难以置信的」（第 2 个义项：因出乎意料而令人惊叹）；句意为最后那一投简直不可思议。

pos.zh: 形容词：难以置信的；不可信的；惊人的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「难以置信地；极其」
同前缀族名词，义为「不信；无信仰」
去掉否定前缀的正面形式，义为「可信的」

senses.title: Too improbable to be believed
senses.definition: so unlikely or inconsistent with fact that it cannot be accepted as true
senses.definitionCN: 因可能性太低或与事实不符而无法被当作真实接受
senses.example: His excuse for missing the exam sounded unbelievable.
senses.exampleCN: 他缺考的理由听起来难以置信。
senses.why: The core image is the mind refusing its grip: the story is offered, the mind will not close around it.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是心智拒绝「握住」：故事递来，心智却不肯合拢。

senses.title: Surprising beyond expectation
senses.definition: so unexpected or extreme that it amazes, as in an unbelievable result
senses.definitionCN: 因出乎意料或极端程度而令人惊叹，如 an unbelievable result
senses.example: The team made an unbelievable comeback in the final minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 球队在最后几分钟上演了不可思议的逆转。
senses.why: The same refusal flips tone: what the mind cannot close around delights instead of offending.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「握不住」换了色调：令人合不拢的不再是谎言，而是惊喜。

senses.title: Extremely good or impressive
senses.definition: very good, often used loosely in speech for emphasis
senses.definitionCN: 非常好，口语中泛用于强调
senses.example: The view from the summit was unbelievable.
senses.exampleCN: 山顶的景色美得让人难以置信。
senses.why: Amazement becomes praise: the word stretches from doubt to delight.
senses.whyCN: 惊叹化为赞美：这个词从怀疑拉伸到欢喜。

senses.title: A price or deal too good or too bad to be real
senses.titleCN: 离谱的价格；可疑的交易
senses.definition: of offers or bargains, so extreme that trust itself is questioned
senses.definitionCN: 就报价或交易而言，极端到令人怀疑其真实性
senses.example: They offered an unbelievable discount on the last day.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一天他们给出了低得离谱的折扣。
senses.why: When an offer outruns belief, the buyer hesitates: is it real, or is it a hook?
senses.whyCN: 当报价超出可信范围，买家便迟疑：是真便宜，还是鱼钩？

senses.title: Unbelievable behaviour
senses.definition: of conduct, so rude, bold or extreme that onlookers are startled
senses.definitionCN: 就行为而言，粗鲁、大胆或极端到令旁观者咋舌
senses.example: His unbelievable rudeness to the waiter shocked the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他对服务生难以置信的无礼震惊了全桌。
senses.why: Social norms are what the mind expects; conduct beyond them will not be taken in.
senses.whyCN: 社会常规是心智的预期；超出预期的举止让人无法「收下」。

senses.title: Unbelievable odds or statistics
senses.definition: of numbers, chances or figures, so far from the normal range that they seem wrong
senses.definitionCN: 就数字、概率或数据而言，偏离正常范围到看似有误
senses.example: She beat odds of a million to one — almost unbelievable.
senses.exampleCN: 她战胜了百万分之一的赔率——几乎令人无法相信。
senses.why: Numbers are checked against expectation; the figure that breaks the scale is unbelievable.
senses.whyCN: 数字要拿预期来校验；打破量程的那个数字便「不可信」。

senses.title: Unbelievable as a stretched exclamation
senses.definition: used alone or in the frame simply unbelievable as an exclamation of amazement
senses.definitionCN: 单独使用或用于 simply unbelievable 框架，作惊叹语
senses.example: They won again? Simply unbelievable!
senses.exampleCN: 他们又赢了？简直难以置信！
senses.why: The adjective hardens into an interjection: the refused belief becomes a cry.
senses.whyCN: 形容词凝固成感叹：被拒绝的「信」化作一声惊呼。

senses.title: Unbelievable weather or conditions
senses.definition: of conditions, so unusual for the place or season that people remark on them
senses.definitionCN: 就天气或境况而言，异于该地该季的常态而引人议论
senses.example: Snow in April here is almost unbelievable.
senses.exampleCN: 这里四月下雪几乎是不可思议的事。
senses.why: Seasons are the world's habit; weather that breaks the habit reads like a tall tale.
senses.whyCN: 季节是世界的习惯；打破习惯的天气读起来像天方夜谭。

intro.en: Unbelievable is un- laid on believable, which itself is believe plus the Latin-derived -able.
intro.cn: unbelievable 是 un- 加 believable，后者本身又是 believe 加源自拉丁语的 -able。

items.en: *leubh- is generally reconstructed as 'to care, desire, love'; the deeper trail is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *leubh- 意为「关爱、渴望、爱」；更早的脉络不确定。

items.en: Proto-Germanic gave *leubon, the ancestor of believe and of love.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语给出 *leubon，即 believe 与 love 的共同祖先。

items.en: Old English belēavian meant to hold dear, and by extension to hold a thing true.
items.cn: 古英语 belēavian 意为「珍爱」，引申为「把某事当作真实来持有」。

items.en: Believable was formed in the sixteenth century on believe with the suffix -able.
items.cn: 十六世纪在 believe 之上加后缀 -able 构成 believable。

items.en: The negative unbelievable followed, first of tales that could not be credited.
items.cn: 否定式 unbelievable 随之出现，最初指无法取信的故事。

items.en: In the twentieth century the sense stretched to amazed praise, its most common modern use.
items.cn: 二十世纪词义拉伸为惊叹式的赞美，成为现代最常见的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the believe family; the near-meaning group gathers improbable, incredible and amazing words.
note.cn: 形近组收 believe 词族；近义组收 improbable、incredible 及表惊人的词。

entries.definition: Able to be believed; the positive base of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可信的」，是本词去掉否定前缀的正面形式。

entries.definition: To accept as true; the verb on which the whole family stands.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「相信」，是整个词族的动词基础。

entries.definition: The noun of believing; a thing held true.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「信念；所信之事」。

entries.definition: The lack of belief, especially religious; older sibling of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不信；无信仰」（尤指宗教），是本词的同前缀前辈。

entries.definition: Loved dearly; shares the deep root with believe, since to believe was once to hold dear.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「深爱的」，与 believe 同出深词根，因为「相信」古义即「珍视」。

entries.definition: Impossible or amazing to believe; Latin-built twin of unbelievable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「难以置信的」，是 unbelievable 的拉丁构词孪生词。

entries.definition: Unlikely to happen or be true; stresses low probability rather than refusal to believe.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不大可能的」，强调概率之低，而非拒绝相信。

entries.definition: Not seeming reasonable or probable; formal, often of stories and excuses.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「难以取信的」，语气正式，多指故事与托辞。

entries.definition: Held in doubt; the doubting stays open rather than refusing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可疑的；半信半疑的」，怀疑保持开放而非拒绝。

entries.definition: Very surprising; pure amazement without the doubting undertone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人震惊的」，纯表惊叹，不含怀疑底色。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real believe root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 believe 词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Un + believable: build the negative on the believe family.
normal.cn: un + believable：在 believe 词族上加否定。

normal.en: Incredible is the Latin twin; unbelievable is the native twin.
normal.cn: incredible 是拉丁构词的孪生词，unbelievable 是本族构词的孪生词。

normal.en: An unbelievable story fails the test of belief.
normal.cn: an unbelievable story 通不过「相信」的检验。

normal.en: Unbelievable luck means luck so good it staggers you.
normal.cn: unbelievable luck 指好到令人瞠目的运气。

normal.en: The root means hold dear: belief is holding a thing dear as true.
normal.cn: 词根本义是「珍视」：相信就是把一件事当真来珍视。

abstract.en: Picture a story offered with open hands; the mind folds its arms and will not take it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个故事被双手奉上，心智却抱臂不接。

abstract.en: Some surprises are refused because the world never promised them.
abstract.cn: 有些惊喜被拒绝，只因世界从未许诺过它们。

abstract.en: When refusal softens, it turns into applause.
abstract.cn: 当拒绝软化，它就变成了喝彩。

examples.en: The ticket cost almost nothing — an unbelievable bargain.
examples.cn: 这张票几乎不要钱——便宜得难以置信。

examples.en: Her recovery after the accident was unbelievable to the doctors.
examples.cn: 她事故后的康复让医生们觉得不可思议。

examples.en: That is simply unbelievable; we closed the deal an hour ago.
examples.cn: 这简直难以置信；我们一小时前才完成交易。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安必离佛」——安必离佛十万八千里，信不得：难以置信

root: unbelievable 由本族否定前缀 un- 加 believable 构成，believable 又由 believe 加拉丁源后缀 -able 构成；believe 经古英语 belēavian 可溯至原始日耳曼语 *leubon 与原始印欧语重构词根 *leubh-「关爱、爱」，与 love 同族。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of unbelievable all circle one refused grip: tales that cannot be credited, results that amaze, prices that outbid trust, behaviour that startles, odds that break the scale, the hardened exclamation, and weather that breaks the season's habit.
sensesIntro.cn: unbelievable 的八个义项都围绕同一次被拒绝的「握住」：无法取信的故事、令人惊叹的结果、超出信任的报价、令人咋舌的行为、打破量程的赔率、凝固的惊叹语，以及打破季节习惯的天气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the mind's hands are offered something and fold shut instead of closing around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：心智之手被递来一物，却抱臂合拢，不肯握住。

branches.en: THE DOUBT: the story fails the test of belief.
branches.cn: 怀疑线：故事通不过相信的检验。

branches.en: THE AMAZEMENT: the refusal flips into delighted praise.
branches.cn: 惊叹线：拒绝翻转为欣喜的赞美。

branches.en: THE EXCESS: prices, conduct and odds that outrun what the mind can take in.
branches.cn: 超限线：价格、行为与赔率超出心智所能收下。

branches.en: THE CRY: the adjective hardens into an exclamation.
branches.cn: 惊呼线：形容词凝固成一声惊叹。

branches.en: THE SEASON: weather that breaks the world's habit reads like a tale.
branches.cn: 季节线：打破世界习惯的天气读来如同传说。

intro.en: Unbelievable stacks three layers: the native un-, the believe root, and the Latin -able.
intro.cn: unbelievable 叠了三层：本族前缀 un-、believe 词根，以及拉丁源后缀 -able。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic and the suffix Latin; only the Indo-European base is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 词根属日耳曼语源，后缀属拉丁语源；只有印欧词基属重构形式。

items.meaning: to hold dear; to hold true
items.example: It is the oldest recorded English step.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语中可考的最早环节。

items.example: It underlies both love and believe.
items.exampleCN: 它同时是 love 与 believe 的底层。
它把 believable 变为 unbelievable。

items.example: It appears in belief, where v becomes f.
items.exampleCN: 它见于 belief，词中 v 变为 f。

items.example: It forms incredible, the Latin twin.
items.exampleCN: 它构成拉丁孪生词 incredible。

items.example: It is the root inside incredible.
items.exampleCN: 它是 incredible 内部的词根。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「难以置信地；极其」
去掉否定前缀的正面形式，义为「可信的」
同前缀族名词，义为「不信；无信仰」

definition_zh: 叔叔；伯父；舅舅；姑父；姨父；叔伯般亲切的长辈
definition_en: the brother of a parent, or the husband of an aunt, or a friendly older man
core_image: 家里带来礼物与故事的那位长辈
scene: 每年春节他都从港口城市回来，口袋里装着糖和船上的故事。The children ran to greet their uncle at the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 uncle 是名词「叔伯」（第 1 个义项：父母的兄弟）；句意为孩子们跑到门口迎接他们的叔叔。

pos.zh: 名词：叔叔；伯父；舅舅；姑父；姨父；（对年长男性的）尊称

collocations.zh: 山姆大叔（美国政府的拟人形象）
汤姆叔叔（含贬义：逆来顺受者）
这就成了；万事大吉（英式俚语）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「叔叔身份；为叔之道」（罕用）
同族拉丁派生形容词，义为「叔伯般慈爱的」

senses.title: The brother of a parent
senses.definition: the brother of one's father or mother
senses.definitionCN: 父亲或母亲的兄弟
senses.example: My uncle on my mother's side is a fisherman.
senses.exampleCN: 我舅舅是渔民。
senses.why: The core image is the family circle one ring wider than the parents' own.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是比父母之环再外扩一圈的家庭圈。

senses.title: The husband of an aunt
senses.definition: the man married to one's aunt
senses.definitionCN: 与自己的姑母或姨母结婚的男性
senses.example: Uncle Wang, my aunt's husband, taught me to swim.
senses.exampleCN: 姨父王叔叔教我游泳。
senses.why: Marriage extends the kinship ring sideways: the aunt's ring pulls in her husband.
senses.whyCN: 婚姻把亲属圈向侧面扩展：姑姨之环把她的丈夫也拉了进来。

senses.title: A friendly older man, not related
senses.definition: a family friend or any older man addressed warmly, especially by children
senses.definitionCN: 受孩子或晚辈亲热称呼的年长男性，可无亲属关系
senses.example: The shopkeeper is called Uncle Ali by all the neighbourhood children.
senses.exampleCN: 街坊的孩子们都管店主叫阿里大叔。
senses.why: Kinship terms radiate outward: warmth turns a neighbour into family by name.
senses.whyCN: 亲属称谓向外辐射：亲昵的称呼把邻居变成「家人」。

senses.title: Cry uncle: to admit defeat
senses.definition: in the American phrase cry uncle, to surrender or admit you are beaten
senses.definitionCN: 美式短语 cry uncle，指认输或承认被打败
senses.example: He would not cry uncle even after three rounds.
senses.exampleCN: 即使三个回合之后他也不肯认输。
senses.why: The child being wrestled must beg the elder to stop; calling uncle is calling the older power.
senses.whyCN: 被摔跤的孩子须求长辈住手；喊 uncle 就是唤那位年长的强者。

senses.title: Uncle Sam: the United States personified
senses.definition: in the phrase Uncle Sam, a personification of the United States government
senses.definitionCN: 短语 Uncle Sam 中，指美国政府的拟人化形象
senses.example: Uncle Sam wants every form filled in triplicate.
senses.exampleCN: 山姆大叔要每张表格一式三份。
senses.why: The state becomes a stern but familiar elder who makes demands.
senses.whyCN: 国家变成一位严厉却熟稔的长辈，提出种种要求。

senses.title: Bob's your uncle: and there you are
senses.definition: in the British phrase Bob's your uncle, it is as easy as that, the task is done
senses.definitionCN: 英式短语 Bob's your uncle，指事情就这么简单、办妥了
senses.example: Press the button and Bob's your uncle.
senses.exampleCN: 按下按钮，一切搞定。
senses.why: A benevolent uncle in the phrase stands for things falling easily into place.
senses.whyCN: 短语中那位好心的叔叔，象征事情轻松顺遂。

senses.title: The uncle in family stories and literature
senses.titleCN: 文学与故事中的叔伯角色
senses.definition: in fiction and family talk, the role of the older relative who brings gifts, freedom or mischief
senses.definitionCN: 小说与家庭话语中，那位带来礼物、自由或恶作剧的长辈亲属角色
senses.example: Every family story has an uncle who spoils the children a little.
senses.exampleCN: 每个家庭故事里都有个会把孩子惯坏一点的叔叔。
senses.why: The role is the parent's brother: authority softened by distance.
senses.whyCN: 这个角色就是父母的兄弟：因隔着距离而温和的权威。

senses.title: Uncle as a term of respect for elders
senses.definition: in many cultures, an honorific for older men of the community, as in uncle and aunt forms
senses.definitionCN: 多种文化中对社区年长男性的敬称，与 aunt 等称谓对举
senses.example: In the village, elders are addressed as uncle regardless of kinship.
senses.exampleCN: 在村里，长辈无论有无亲缘都被称为叔叔。
senses.why: The kinship map stretches to cover the whole community; respect borrows the family word.
senses.whyCN: 亲属地图扩展到整个社区；敬意借用了家庭之词。

intro.en: Uncle travelled from Latin through French, from a diminutive of the word for grandfather.
intro.cn: uncle 从拉丁语经法语传入英语，其源头是「祖父」一词的指小形式。

items.en: *awo- is generally reconstructed as a kinship term for a maternal or adult relative; the deeper trail is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *awo- 是指称母系或成年亲属的亲属词；更早的脉络不确定。

items.en: Latin avunculus meant 'little grandfather', a diminutive of avus 'grandfather', specifically the mother's brother.
items.cn: 拉丁语 avunculus 意为「小祖父」，是 avus「祖父」的指小词，特指母亲的兄弟。

items.en: Old French oncle borrowed the Latin word and widened it to both mother's and father's brother.
items.cn: 古法语 oncle 借入该拉丁词，并把词义扩展到母系与父系的兄弟。

items.en: English took the word in the thirteenth century through Anglo-Norman uncle, oncle.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪经盎格鲁-诺曼语的 uncle、oncle 借入该词。

items.en: The kinship sense settled, and the friendly-extension senses for non-relatives grew.
items.cn: 亲属义定型，而对非亲属的亲昵扩展义随之生长。

items.en: The word now names kin, warm neighbours, national symbols and surrender in a schoolyard game.
items.cn: 如今这个词既指亲属与热络的邻里，也指国家象征与游戏中的认输。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin kinship family; the near-meaning group gathers family words of the same ring.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁亲属词族；近义组收同圈的亲属称谓词。

entries.definition: The female counterpart; from Latin amita, a parallel kinship borrowing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「姑姨」，是其女性对应词，源自拉丁语 amita，属同一批亲属借词。

entries.definition: Kindly and helpful like an uncle; the direct Latin-derived adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「叔伯般慈爱的」，是直接由拉丁语派生的形容词。

entries.definition: Not clean; begins with the same un- sound but is a wholly different formation.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不洁的」，起音与 uncle 相同，但构词完全不同。

entries.definition: Dense forest; rhymes and nearly rhymes with uncle but has a Hindi source.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「丛林」，与 uncle 韵近，源自印地语。

entries.definition: The Latin grandfather root itself; recorded in Latin, reconstructed further back.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，即拉丁语「祖父」词根本身；见于拉丁语文献，更早为重构形式。

entries.definition: The sister of a parent or wife of an uncle; the paired kinship term.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「姑姨」，父母的姐妹或舅母，是 uncle 的对偶称谓。

entries.definition: A child of an uncle or aunt; the next ring of the same family map.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「堂表亲」，是叔伯姑姨的子女，同一家庭地图的下一圈。

entries.definition: The child viewed from the other side; the uncle's counterpart word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「侄子；外甥」，是 uncle 关系的另一端称谓。

entries.definition: The parent's parent; the very word from which avunculus was made.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「祖父」，正是 avunculus 所由派生的词。

entries.definition: An older member of a community; overlaps with the honorific use of uncle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「长者」，与 uncle 的敬称用法重叠。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real little-grandfather root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的「小祖父」词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Latin avunculus is a little grandfather: the uncle as a young grandpa.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 avunculus 是「小祖父」：叔叔就是一位年轻的祖父。

normal.en: Avuncular keeps the Latin face: a kindly, uncle-like manner.
normal.cn: avuncular 保留了拉丁面孔：叔伯般慈和的态度。

normal.en: Cry uncle is what you shout when the big one has you pinned.
normal.cn: cry uncle 是被大块头压住时的喊话。

normal.en: Uncle Sam is the government wearing a family face.
normal.cn: Uncle Sam 是戴上家庭面孔的政府。

normal.en: Bob's your uncle ends a recipe: and there it is, done.
normal.cn: Bob's your uncle 收尾一份说明：就这么成了。

abstract.en: Picture the family circle drawn in rings: parents at the centre, the uncle one ring out.
abstract.cn: 想象画成一圈圈的家庭环：父母居中，叔叔在外一圈。

abstract.en: A good uncle is a parent with the pressure taken off.
abstract.cn: 好叔叔就是卸掉了压力的父母。

abstract.en: Names can make family of strangers.
abstract.cn: 称呼能把陌生人变成家人。

examples.en: My uncle drove eight hours to be at my graduation.
examples.cn: 我叔叔开了八小时车来参加我的毕业典礼。

examples.en: The twins were brought up partly by an uncle in the port town.
examples.cn: 这对双胞胎部分是由港口城的一位叔父抚养的。

examples.en: All right, all right, I cry uncle — you win this round.
examples.cn: 好好好，我认输——这回合你赢了。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the family circle drawn one ring wider than the parents' own.
core.cn: 核心意象：比父母之环再外扩一圈的家庭环。

branches.en: THE KIN: the parent's brother and the aunt's husband.
branches.cn: 亲属线：父母的兄弟与姑姨的丈夫。

branches.en: THE WARMTH: neighbours and elders brought inside the family word.
branches.cn: 亲昵线：邻里与长辈被家庭之词接纳进来。

branches.en: THE PLAY: calling for the older power when pinned in a game.
branches.cn: 游戏线：被压住时呼唤那位年长的强者。

branches.en: THE SYMBOL: state and recipe alike borrow a friendly uncle face.
branches.cn: 象征线：国家与说明文字同样借用友善的叔叔面孔。

branches.en: THE STORY: the uncle role, authority softened by distance.

intro.en: Uncle is a Latin kinship borrowing; its family shows the little-grandfather suffix at work.
intro.cn: uncle 是拉丁亲属借词；其词族展示了「小祖父」指小后缀的运作。

latinIntro.en: Latin avus and avunculus are recorded; only the Indo-European base is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 avus 与 avunculus 均有记录；只有印欧词基属重构形式。

items.example: It is the base of the family.
It carries the sense into formal English.
items.exampleCN: 它把该义带进正式英语。

items.example: It gives aunt by way of French.
It came through French like uncle.
items.exampleCN: 它与 uncle 一样经法语借入。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「叔叔身份；为叔之道」（罕用）
同族拉丁派生形容词，义为「叔伯般慈爱的」

definition_zh: 在……下面；少于；在……之下（状态、管辖）；控制中；根据（条款）
definition_en: below or lower than something, less than a number, or controlled by or covered by something
core_image: 桌面下藏着的书包，桥下流过的河水
scene: 暴雨倾盆，桥洞下挤满了躲雨的自行车和行人。The cyclists waited under the bridge until the rain stopped.
sceneCN: 这里 under 是介词「在……下面」（第 1 个义项：下方位置）；句意为骑行者在桥下避雨直到雨停。

pos.zh: 介词：在……下面；少于；在……管辖下；根据
副词：在下面；低于；在水下

derivatives.zh: 由本词与 neath 复合，义为「在……底下」，语气更强调覆盖
由本词加动名词及形容词后缀构成，义为「潜在的；在下面的」
由本词与 age 合成，义为「未成年的；未到法定年龄的」

senses.title: Below something
senses.definition: in or to a position directly below something or covered by it
senses.definitionCN: 位于某物的正下方或被其覆盖
senses.example: The cat hid under the sofa all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 那只猫整个下午都躲在沙发底下。
senses.why: The core image is the space beneath a shelter: the covering above, the hidden below.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是掩体之下的空间：上有覆盖，下有藏身。

senses.title: Less than a number or amount
senses.definition: below a figure, age or standard in measurement
senses.definitionCN: 在数字、年龄或标准之下
senses.example: Children under twelve travel free on the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 十二岁以下儿童免费乘坐公交车。
senses.why: Position turns into quantity: the number line is a ladder, and under is below a rung.
senses.whyCN: 位置转为数量：数轴是一架梯子，under 就在某一梯级之下。

senses.title: Controlled by or subjected to
senses.definition: governed, commanded or affected by a person, force or condition
senses.definitionCN: 受某人、某种力量或状况的管辖、指挥或影响
senses.example: The team worked under great pressure before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 截止日期前，团队在巨大压力下工作。
senses.why: Authority presses downward like a cover; to be under it is to live beneath the weight.
senses.whyCN: 权威像覆盖物一样自上而下施压；身处其下即承受其重。

senses.title: In the process or state of
senses.definition: undergoing or in the middle of a process, as under repair or under discussion
senses.definitionCN: 正在经历或处于某一过程之中，如 under repair、under discussion
senses.example: The bridge is under repair until March.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥维修至三月。
senses.why: The process is a roof over the thing: while it lasts, the thing stands beneath it.
senses.whyCN: 过程像罩在事物之上的顶棚：过程持续期间，事物就立于其下。

senses.title: According to a rule or agreement
senses.definition: as provided or required by a law, rule or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 依照某法律、规则或协议的规定
senses.example: Under the new regulations, all shops close by nine.
senses.exampleCN: 根据新条例，所有商店九点前关门。
senses.why: A written rule hangs over conduct like a beam; actions pass beneath it.
senses.whyCN: 成文规则如横梁悬于行为之上；一切举动自其下经过。

senses.title: Beneath a surface in name or appearance
senses.definition: hidden by or beneath an outward appearance or name
senses.definitionCN: 隐藏于外表或名义之下
senses.example: Under his calm manner, he was furious.
senses.exampleCN: 在他平静的态度之下，是满腔怒火。
senses.why: The visible surface covers the true thing; what you see on top conceals what lies under.
senses.whyCN: 可见的表面遮住真实之物；你看到的「上面」掩盖着底下的东西。

senses.title: Below water
senses.definition: below the surface of water, as an adverb or in compounds like underwater
senses.definitionCN: 在水面之下，作副词或构成 underwater 等复合词
senses.example: The divers stayed under for nearly an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员在水下待了将近一小时。
senses.why: The surface itself becomes the shelter: the world below the line of the sea.
senses.whyCN: 水面本身成了掩体：海平面之下是另一个世界。

senses.title: Lower in rank or importance
senses.definition: lower than someone in rank, chain of command or importance
senses.definitionCN: 在级别、指挥链或重要性上低于某人
senses.example: No one in the office is under more strain than the manager's assistant.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室里没有人比经理助理承受更大的压力。
senses.why: Hierarchy is drawn as layers; to be under is to sit on a lower layer.
senses.whyCN: 层级被画成一层层；处于 under 就是坐在较低一层。

senses.title: Under one's breath: quietly
senses.definition: in the phrase under one's breath, in a whisper so others barely hear
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 under one's breath，指压低嗓音低语，别人几乎听不见
senses.example: He muttered a complaint under his breath.
senses.exampleCN: 他压低声音抱怨了一句。
senses.why: The voice too can be pushed under a surface, below the level of hearing.
senses.whyCN: 声音同样可以被压到「表面」之下，低于可闻之线。

senses.title: Go under: to sink or fail
senses.definition: in the phrase go under, to sink below the surface, or of a business, to fail
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 go under，指沉入水下，或指企业倒闭
senses.example: Two old shipping firms went under last year.
senses.exampleCN: 两家老航运公司去年倒闭了。
senses.why: The ship below the waves and the firm below the line share one downward image.
senses.whyCN: 沉入浪下之船与跌破底线之公司共享同一幅下坠画面。

intro.en: Under is one of English's oldest native words, unchanged in sense since Old English.
intro.cn: under 是英语最古老的本族词之一，自古英语以来词义几乎未变。

items.en: *n̥dher- is generally reconstructed as 'below'; the deeper trail is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *n̥dher- 意为「在下」；更早的脉络不确定。

items.en: Proto-Germanic *under, *undar kept the meaning below, between or among.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 *under、*undar 保留了「在下、介于、其间」之义。

items.en: Old English under already carried position, subordination and subjection senses.
items.cn: 古英语 under 已具备位置、从属与臣服诸义。

items.en: German unter and Dutch onder are close cousins; Latin inferus and infra share the deeper root family.
items.cn: 德语 unter、荷兰语 onder 是近亲；拉丁语 inferus 与 infra 属更深的同根家族。

items.en: The word multiplied into phrases and compounds: understand, undergo, undertake.
items.cn: 该词繁衍出大量短语与复合词：understand、undergo、undertake。

items.en: Modern English keeps every old sense and adds technical ones, from undersea to underclass.
items.cn: 现代英语保留全部古义并新增技术义项，如 undersea、underclass。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the under- compound family; the near-meaning group gathers below, beneath and subordinate words.
note.cn: 形近组收 under- 复合词族；近义组收 below、beneath 及表从属的词。

entries.definition: To grasp meaning; a compound of under plus stand with a shifted sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「理解」，由 under 与 stand 构成的复合词，词义已偏移。

entries.definition: To experience or endure something; under plus go.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「经历；承受」，由 under 加 go 构成。

entries.definition: Directly below, with stress on being covered; under plus neath.
entries.definitionCN: 介词兼副词，义为「在……底下」，由 under 加 neath 构成，强调被覆盖。

entries.definition: Dutch cousin of under, meaning below; same Germanic family.
entries.definitionCN: 荷兰语同族词，义为「在下」，与 under 同属日耳曼语族。

entries.definition: Excessive or improper; looks close to under but comes from un- plus due.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「过度的；不当的」，形近 under，但由 un- 加 due 构成。

entries.definition: At a lower position, without implying covering; looser than under.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在下方」，不含覆盖义，比 under 宽松。

entries.definition: Under, in a slightly literary tone; also used for dignity, as beneath one.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在……之下」，略带书面语色彩，亦用于 beneath one「有失身份」。

entries.definition: Secret or deceitful, or done with the palm turned up; another under- compound.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「阴险的；秘密的」，或指「手心向上的（动作）」，为另一 under- 复合词。

entries.definition: Lower in rank; the formal adjective for the hierarchy sense of under.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「下级的」，是本词层级义的正式对应词。

entries.definition: Lower in position or quality; built on the same deep root family as under.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「较低的；较差的」，与 under 同出更深的词根家族。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Germanic root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的日耳曼词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: German unter is the twin: un-ter, under.
normal.cn: 德语 unter 是孪生词：un-ter，under。

normal.en: Under age, under pressure, under control: a weight pressing from above.
normal.cn: under age、under pressure、under control：都是自上而下的压重。

normal.en: Go under is the ship slipping below the waves.
normal.cn: go under 是船滑到浪面之下。

normal.en: Under the new law means the law hangs over every action.
normal.cn: under the new law 意为法律悬于一切举动之上。

normal.en: Under one's breath pushes the voice below the hearing line.
normal.cn: under one's breath 把声音压到可闻线之下。

abstract.en: Picture a table: the legs and the floor hold the top, and the shadow hides below.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子：桌腿与地板撑起桌面，阴影藏在下面。

abstract.en: Every covering creates an underneath, and every underneath longs for air.
abstract.cn: 每个覆盖物都造出一个「底下」，每个「底下」都渴望空气。

abstract.en: Rank is a staircase; standing lower is standing under.
abstract.cn: 级别是一段楼梯；站得低就是站于其下。

examples.en: The letters lay under the pile of newspapers.
examples.cn: 信件压在报纸堆底下。

examples.en: The firm survived the crisis while others went under.
examples.cn: 这家公司熬过了危机，而其他公司纷纷倒闭。

examples.en: Under the terms of the lease, repairs are the landlord's duty.
examples.cn: 依照租约条款，维修是房东的义务。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安得」——安安稳稳藏在得下面：在下面

root: 古英语 under「在下」，一般认为可溯至原始日耳曼语 *under/*undar 与原始印欧语重构词根 *n̥dher-「在下」；与德语 unter、荷兰语 onder 同族，与拉丁语 infra、inferus 属更深同根家族；英语保留其全部古义并繁衍出大量复合词。

sensesIntro.en: The ten senses of under all live beneath something: shelters and tables, numbers and lines, authority and process, rules and names, water and rank, whispers and sinking ships.
sensesIntro.cn: under 的十个义项都活在某物之下：掩体与桌子、数字与底线、权威与过程、规则与名义、水面与层级、压低的耳语与下沉的船。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something above covers, and something below hides or bears it.
core.cn: 核心意象：上有覆盖，下有藏匿或承托。

branches.en: THE SPACE: beneath tables, bridges and the sea's surface.
branches.cn: 空间线：桌子、桥洞与海面之下。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: the number line as a ladder, under one rung.
branches.cn: 度量线：数轴如梯，居于某级之下。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: authority and rank pressing down the chain.
branches.cn: 压重线：权威与级别沿指挥链向下施压。

branches.en: THE ROOF: processes and rules that hang over conduct.
branches.cn: 顶棚线：悬于行为之上的过程与规则。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN AND THE DOWNFALL: names, whispers and ships that slip below.
branches.cn: 隐匿与倾覆线：名义、耳语与滑入水下的船。

intro.en: Under is a bare native root, but English has built a whole city of compounds on it.
intro.cn: under 是个裸的本族词根，但英语在其上建起了一整座复合词之城。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, not Latin, so there are no direct Latin cognates; infra and inferior belong to the same deep family by reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语源而非拉丁语源，故无直接拉丁同族词；infra 与 inferior 经重构属更深的同根家族。

items.example: The root form is unchanged in shape.
items.exampleCN: 词根形式历经千年基本未变。

items.example: It forms subway, subordinate and kin words.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 subway、subordinate 等同族词。
