definition_zh: 在……底下；在……下面；底部；下面；在底层
definition_en: directly below something, or the part or place below a surface
core_image: 掀开地毯看地板的那一下
scene: 老屋翻新，工人掀开积灰的地毯，露出一层拼花木地板。The floor underneath the carpet was oak, still firm.
sceneCN: 这里 underneath 是介词「在……底下」（第 1 个义项：直接位于覆盖物之下）；句意为地毯下的地板是橡木的，依然坚实。

pos.zh: 介词：在……底下；在……下面
副词：在下面；在底下；在底层
名词：底部；底面

collocations.zh: 阳光底下依然寒冷（引申用法）

derivatives.zh: 构成成分，义为「在下」
由 beneath 缩略而成的成分，义为「在下」，多用于诗歌

senses.title: Directly below and covered
senses.definition: in or to a position directly below something that covers or rests on it
senses.definitionCN: 位于覆盖或压着某物的正下方
senses.example: The key was hidden underneath the flowerpot.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙藏在花盆底下。
senses.why: The core image is the surface that conceals: lift it and the hidden place opens.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是遮蔽的表面：掀开它，藏身之处便现形。

senses.title: The underside of a thing
senses.definition: the part of a thing that faces downward or rests on the ground
senses.definitionCN: 物体朝下或贴地的那一面
senses.example: Check the underneath of the car for rust.
senses.exampleCN: 检查一下汽车底盘有没有生锈。
senses.why: The hidden face is the one you never see until you stoop or lift.
senses.whyCN: 那是你俯身或抬起之前永远看不见的一面。

senses.title: Lower in a written page
senses.definition: at a lower position on a page or screen, following what was written above
senses.definitionCN: 书页或屏幕上较低的位置，位于上文之下
senses.example: Sign the form and date it underneath.
senses.exampleCN: 在表格上签名并在下方注明日期。
senses.why: The page has a top and a bottom like any surface; underneath is the lower half.
senses.whyCN: 页面与任何表面一样有上下；underneath 就是下半部分。

senses.title: Beneath an outer layer of clothing
senses.definition: under an outer garment, next to the skin or covered by it
senses.definitionCN: 在外衣之下、贴身或被覆盖之处
senses.example: She wore a thin jumper underneath the raincoat.
senses.exampleCN: 她在雨衣里面穿了件薄套衫。
senses.why: Clothes are stacked surfaces; underneath names the layer closest to the body.
senses.whyCN: 衣物是层层叠叠的表面；underneath 指最贴近身体的那层。

senses.title: Hidden under an appearance
senses.definition: behind or concealed by an outward look or manner
senses.definitionCN: 藏于外表、态度或表象之后
senses.example: Underneath the politeness, she was furious.
senses.exampleCN: 在那番礼貌之下，她怒不可遏。
senses.why: Manners are surfaces too; the true feeling rests beneath them.
senses.whyCN: 态度也是表面；真实情绪就卧在其下。

senses.title: The underneath as a noun: the bottom part
senses.definition: as a noun, the lower surface or bottom part of something
senses.definitionCN: 名词用法，指物体的下表面或底部
senses.example: The table has a drawer in the underneath.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌子的底部有个抽屉。
senses.why: The preposition is lifted into a noun: the hidden place becomes a thing you can name.
senses.whyCN: 介词升为名词：那处藏匿之所成为可以指名之物。

senses.title: Underneath it all: at the deepest level
senses.definition: in the phrase underneath it all, at the deepest or most basic level
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 underneath it all，指在最深层、最根本处
senses.example: Underneath it all, the two quarrelling nations feared the same thing.
senses.exampleCN: 归根结底，这两个争吵的国家惧怕着同一件事。
senses.why: Layers are peeled one by one until the base remains; the phrase names the base.
senses.whyCN: 一层层剥开直至基座；这个短语命名的正是基座。

senses.title: Underneath in structures and machines
senses.definition: the lower supporting part of buildings, vehicles or machines
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、车辆或机器的底部承重部分
senses.example: Inspect the bridge underneath after every flood.
senses.exampleCN: 每次洪水过后都要检查桥底。
senses.why: What bears the weight is necessarily below; the support lives in the hidden place.
senses.whyCN: 承重者必居于下；支撑就住在那个看不见的地方。

intro.en: Underneath joins the native under with neath, a shortened form of beneath.
intro.cn: underneath 由本族词 under 与 beneath 的缩略形式 neath 复合而成。

items.en: *n̥dher- 'below' is generally reconstructed at the base; the deeper trail is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为词基是重构形式 *n̥dher-「在下」；更早的脉络不确定。

items.en: Old English under carried the below sense from the start.
items.cn: 古英语 under 自始即有「在下」之义。

items.en: Old English beneothan meant below, built on be- plus neothan, a form of nether.
items.cn: 古英语 beneothan 意为「在下」，由 be- 加 neothan（nether 的形式）构成。

items.en: Beneath was shortened to neath in verse, and underneath was formed for extra emphasis.
items.cn: 诗歌中 beneath 缩略为 neath，underneath 则为加强语气而构成。

items.en: The compound settled in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, stressing direct contact or covering.
items.cn: 该复合词于十五、十六世纪定型，强调直接接触或覆盖。

items.en: Today it covers space, layers, pages and hidden feelings alike.
items.cn: 如今它兼指空间、层次、页面与隐秘的情感。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the neath family and compounds; the near-meaning group gathers below, beneath and bottom words.
note.cn: 形近组收 neath 词族与复合词；近义组收 below、beneath 与 bottom 类词。

entries.definition: Under, in a slightly literary tone; the parent of the neath element.
entries.definitionCN: 介词兼副词，义为「在……之下」，语气稍书面，是 neath 成分的母体。

entries.definition: Poetic short form of beneath, almost only in verse.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，beneath 的诗体缩略形式，几乎只见于诗歌。

entries.definition: The first element of the compound; the plain everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 介词兼副词，复合词的第一个成分，也是最日常的用词。

entries.definition: To insure or guarantee; a different under- compound with a shifted sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承保；担保」，是另一个词义偏移的 under- 复合词。

entries.definition: Lower, as in netherworld; the surviving adjective of the neath family.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「下方的」，如 netherworld（阴间），是 neath 词族残存的形容词。

entries.definition: Below something; looser than underneath, which stresses contact and covering.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……下面」，比 underneath 宽松，后者强调接触与覆盖。

entries.definition: The lowest part of something; the plain noun counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「底部」，是最朴素的名词对应词。

entries.definition: The face of a thing that looks down; technical counterpart of the underneath.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「下表面」，是 underneath 名词义的技术对应词。

entries.definition: Under, often with the figurative dignity sense.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……之下」，常带 beneath one 的地位比喻义。

entries.definition: At a lower position without contact; looser still than under.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在下方」，不含接触义，比 under 更宽松。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real compound parts and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的复合成分，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Underneath = under + neath: two below-words stacked for emphasis.
normal.cn: underneath = under + neath：两个「在下」叠用以示强调。

normal.en: Beneath shortened to neath lives mostly in poems.
normal.cn: beneath 缩略成的 neath 主要活在诗行里。

normal.en: The underneath of a car is the floor you never see.
normal.cn: the underneath of a car 是你从不看见的那层底。

normal.en: Underneath it all digs to the deepest layer of a matter.
normal.cn: underneath it all 一路挖到事情的最深层。

normal.en: Underneath the raincoat: the layer next to the skin.
normal.cn: underneath the raincoat：贴身的那一层。

abstract.en: Picture lifting a doormat: the house reveals a face it never shows.
abstract.cn: 想象掀开门垫：房子露出一副从不示人的面孔。

abstract.en: Every surface has two faces; only one faces the world.
abstract.cn: 每个表面都有两面；只有一面朝向世界。

abstract.en: The deepest feeling lives underneath the easiest smile.
abstract.cn: 最深的情感就住在最轻易的微笑之下。

examples.en: A note was tucked underneath the door mat.
examples.cn: 门垫底下塞着一张字条。

examples.en: The bridge underneath was scoured by the flood.
examples.cn: 桥的底部被洪水掏刷了。

examples.en: He is calm on the surface, but underneath he is anxious.
examples.cn: 他表面平静，内里却很焦虑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安德尼思」——安得把尼龙毯掀开，思量底下藏何物：在底下

root: underneath 由 under「在下」加 neath（beneath 的缩略）复合而成；beneath 出自古英语 beneothan，由 be- 加 nether 词根构成；词基一般认为可溯至原始印欧语重构词根 *n̥dher-「在下」，与 under、nether 同族。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of underneath all peel a surface: covered spaces, undersides, lower pages, inner layers of clothing, hidden feelings, the noun of the bottom, the deepest level, and the load-bearing base.
sensesIntro.cn: underneath 的八个义项都在掀开一层表面：被覆盖的空间、底面、页面下方、衣物的里层、藏起的情绪、底部的名词、最深处，以及承重的基座。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface is lifted and the concealed face appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：掀开一层表面，被遮的面孔现形。

branches.en: THE SPACE: covered spots and the underside of things.
branches.cn: 空间线：被覆盖之处与物体的底面。

branches.en: THE LAYERS: pages and clothing, each with a lower level.
branches.cn: 层次线：页面与衣物，各有其下一层。

branches.en: THE HEART: appearances conceal, and underneath it all is the truth.
branches.cn: 内心线：表象遮掩，underneath it all 即真相。

branches.en: THE BASE: the named bottom and the load-bearing underside.
branches.cn: 基座线：被命名的底部与承重的底面。

branches.en: THE HIDE: the cover that sits over and hides what lies beneath.
branches.cn: 遮掩线：盖在上面、藏住下方之物的覆盖层。

intro.en: Underneath stacks two below-words: the plain under and the poetic neath.
intro.cn: underneath 叠用了两个「在下」之词：朴素的 under 与诗意的 neath。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, not Latin, so there are no Latin cognates to list; the deep root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语源而非拉丁语源，故没有拉丁同族词可列；深层词根属重构形式。

definition_zh: 理解；懂得；明白；了解；获悉；推断
definition_en: to grasp the meaning of something, to know how something works, or to learn or infer information
core_image: 站到事物下面把它接住、扛在肩上
scene: 老师画了一张图，水管从高处弯到低处，水压的道理一下就清楚了。Now I understand how the water pressure works.
sceneCN: 这里 understand 是动词「明白、理解」（第 1 个义项：掌握意义）；句意为现在我明白水压是怎么回事了。

pos.zh: 动词：理解；懂得；了解；获悉

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「理解；谅解；理解力」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「可以理解的」
加否定前缀 mis- 构成，义为「误解」

senses.title: To grasp the meaning of something
senses.definition: to know what something means, in speech, writing or signs
senses.definitionCN: 知道言语、文字或符号的含义
senses.example: She did not understand the joke until it was explained.
senses.exampleCN: 解释之后她才明白那个笑话。
senses.why: The core image is standing under and taking the weight of meaning onto one's own shoulders.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是站到下面，把意义的重量接到自己肩上。

senses.title: To know how something works
senses.definition: to know the working, cause or system behind something
senses.definitionCN: 知道事物背后的运作、成因或体系
senses.example: He understands engines better than anyone in the workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 他比车间里任何人都更懂发动机。
senses.why: Understanding a machine is bearing its whole structure in mind, not just its surface.
senses.whyCN: 懂机器就是在心中扛起它的整体结构，而不只是表面。

senses.title: To know how someone feels
senses.definition: to be sympathetic to or aware of someone's feelings and situation
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的感受与处境抱有同情或体察
senses.example: A good teacher understands why a child misbehaves.
senses.exampleCN: 好老师懂得孩子为何调皮。
senses.why: To carry a person's situation is to stand beneath them for a moment, sharing the load.
senses.whyCN: 体察一个人的处境，就是暂时站到其下，分担那份重量。

senses.title: To believe or be told indirectly
senses.definition: to learn or infer information, often second-hand, as in I understand that ...
senses.definitionCN: 获知或推断出信息，常为间接来源，如 I understand that ...
senses.example: I understand that the shop will close next month.
senses.exampleCN: 据悉这家店下个月就要关门。
senses.why: What stands under your notice is taken in without proof; hearing is a kind of receiving.
senses.whyCN: 站到你注意力之下的东西无需证明便被接收；听闻也是一种承接。

senses.title: To treat as implicitly agreed
senses.definition: to take something as agreed or settled without saying it, as it is understood that ...
senses.definitionCN: 把某事当作无需言明的共识，如 it is understood that ...
senses.example: It is understood that everyone arrives on time.
senses.exampleCN: 不言而喻，人人都得准时到场。
senses.why: The agreement needs no words: it stands beneath the conversation, holding it up.
senses.whyCN: 共识无需言明：它立于对话之下，撑着整场对话。

senses.title: To interpret a language
senses.definition: to follow speech or text in a language
senses.definitionCN: 能听懂或读懂某种语言的话语或文本
senses.example: The children understand Cantonese but speak only a little.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们听得懂粤语，但只会说一点。
senses.why: A language is a weight of sound and habit; to understand it is to bear it willingly.
senses.whyCN: 语言是声音与习惯的重量；听懂就是甘愿把它扛起来。

senses.title: To realize the seriousness of something
senses.definition: to be fully aware of the importance, danger or consequence of something
senses.definitionCN: 充分意识到某事的重要性、危险性或后果
senses.example: By the second storm, they understood the danger of the coast road.
senses.exampleCN: 到第二场风暴时，他们才真正认识到沿海公路的危险。
senses.why: Awareness lands with weight; when the meaning finally presses down, you understand.
senses.whyCN: 认识是带着重量落地的；当意义终于压下来，你便懂了。

senses.title: To make yourself understood
senses.definition: in the phrase make yourself understood, to express yourself so others follow
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 make yourself understood，指表达清楚使他人听懂
senses.example: He speaks little Spanish but can make himself understood.
senses.exampleCN: 他西班牙语说得不多，但能让人听懂他的意思。
senses.why: The weight is passed across: your meaning must stand under the listener's mind before it is carried.
senses.whyCN: 重量完成交接：你的意思须先立于听者心智之下，才谈得上被扛走。

intro.en: Understand is under plus stand, an Old English compound whose literal sense has shifted.
intro.cn: understand 是 under 加 stand 的古英语复合词，其字面义已发生偏移。

items.en: *n̥dher- 'below' and *stā- 'to stand' are generally reconstructed at the base; the deeper trail is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为词基是重构形式 *n̥dher-「在下」与 *stā-「站立」；更早脉络不确定。

items.en: Old English understandan meant to stand under, stand in the midst of, or to take on oneself.
items.cn: 古英语 understandan 意为「立于其下；置身其间；承当于己」。

items.en: The exact old image is debated: standing under, standing between, or standing firm beneath a thing.
items.cn: 古老的字面意象存在争议：是立于其下、立于其间，还是坚定地承于其下。

items.en: The mental sense had already taken over by Middle English, and the literal sense was lost.
items.cn: 到中古英语时期，「心智」义已完全接管，字面义消亡。

items.en: Greek epistamai, to know, also once meant to stand upon or before; standing and knowing rhyme across languages.
items.cn: 希腊语 epistamai（知晓）也曾意为「立于其上或其前」；「站立」与「知晓」在各语言间彼此押韵。

items.en: The verb now covers meaning, machines, feelings, hearsay and tacit agreement alike.
items.cn: 如今这个动词涵盖意义、机器、情感、传闻与默契。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the under- compound family; the near-meaning group gathers knowing, grasping and sympathy words.
note.cn: 形近组收 under- 复合词族；近义组收知晓、领会与体谅类词。

entries.definition: The noun of comprehension, sympathy or agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「理解；谅解；理解力」。

entries.definition: To endure or experience; a sibling compound on the same under-.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「经历；承受」，同一 under- 上的姊妹复合词。

entries.definition: To take on a task; another sibling compound.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承担；着手做」，另一姊妹复合词。

entries.definition: Under one's feet; an adverb compound of the same family.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在脚下」，同族的副词性复合词。

entries.definition: To take in fully; formal, stresses grasping the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「完全理解」，语气正式，强调把握整体。

entries.definition: To seize mentally; vivid, stresses the act of taking hold.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「领会」，形象生动，强调抓住的动作。

entries.definition: To become fully aware; stresses the moment it lands.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「意识到」，强调顿悟的那一刻。

entries.definition: To understand the worth or feeling of something; adds valuation.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「体察；赏识」，在理解之外叠加价值判断。

entries.definition: To feel with someone; the feeling half of understanding a person.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同情；共鸣」，是「理解一个人」的情感半边。

normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的复合成分，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Under + stand: put yourself beneath a thing and carry it.
normal.cn: under + stand：把自己放到事物之下，把它扛起来。

normal.en: Old English understandan also meant stand between or take on oneself.
normal.cn: 古英语 understandan 也有「立于其间、承当于己」之义。

normal.en: Understood is the old strong past: stand, stood; understand, understood.
normal.cn: understood 是古老的强变化过去式：stand→stood，understand→understood。

normal.en: It is understood that ... names the agreement nobody needs to say aloud.
normal.cn: it is understood that ... 指无需明说的默契。

normal.en: Misunderstand simply puts a bad step in front: miss the stand.
normal.cn: misunderstand 只是在前面错踏一步：没站到该站的位置。

abstract.en: Picture walking under a heavy beam and letting it rest on your shoulders.
abstract.cn: 想象走到一根重梁之下，让它稳稳落在肩头。

abstract.en: To understand is to stand in the middle of a thing until it holds you up.
abstract.cn: 理解就是站到事物中央，直到它把你托住。

abstract.en: A misunderstanding is a beam dropped on the wrong shoulders.
abstract.cn: 误解就是把梁落错了肩膀。

examples.en: I don't understand why the meeting was cancelled.
examples.cn: 我不明白会议为何被取消。

examples.en: After the tour, we finally understood the city's layout.
examples.cn: 参观之后，我们终于弄清了这座城市的布局。

examples.en: She understood at once that the letter was bad news.
examples.cn: 她立刻明白那封信是坏消息。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of understand all bear a weight on the mind's shoulders: meanings, machines, feelings, hearsay, tacit agreements, languages, dangers, and the task of being followed.
sensesIntro.cn: understand 的八个义项都在心智肩头承重：意义、机器、情感、传闻、默契、语言、危险，以及让人听懂自己的任务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: walk beneath the thing and let it rest on your shoulders.
core.cn: 核心意象：走到事物之下，让它稳落在肩头。

branches.en: THE MATTER: meanings, mechanisms and languages taken on board.
branches.cn: 事物线：意义、机制与语言被扛上肩。

branches.en: THE PERSON: standing beneath another's situation for a moment.
branches.cn: 他人线：暂时站到他人的处境之下。

branches.en: THE AWARENESS: hearsay received and dangers finally pressing down.
branches.cn: 觉察线：传闻被接收，危险终于压下来。

branches.en: THE SILENCE: the agreement that stands beneath the talk and holds it up.
branches.cn: 沉默线：立于对话之下、撑起整场对话的默契。

branches.en: THE HANDOVER: passing your meaning beneath another mind.
branches.cn: 交接线：把你的意思递到他人心智之下。

definition_zh: 承担；着手做；从事；承诺；答应负责
definition_en: to take on a task or responsibility and start doing it, or to promise formally that you will do something
core_image: 伸手把一件大事从架子上接下来，扛到自己肩上
scene: 新桥动工前，工程师在图纸上签下了自己的名字。The chief engineer agreed to undertake the design of the new bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 undertake 是动词「承担、着手做」（第 1 个义项：接下任务并开始做）；句意为总工程师同意承担新桥的设计工作。

pos.zh: 承担；着手做；承诺负责
承接任务；从事某项工作

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「事业；任务；（正式）承诺」
由本词加施动者后缀构成，义为「殡葬承办人」，为词义偏移的特殊用法

senses.title: To take on and start a task
senses.definition: to accept a task or duty and begin working on it
senses.definitionCN: 接受任务或职责并着手开始做
senses.example: The lab will undertake a three-year study of sleep patterns.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室将开展一项为期三年的睡眠模式研究。
senses.why: Under plus stand puts you beneath the work: once you take it on, the weight rests on your shoulders and you must stand up under it.
senses.whyCN: under 加 stand 把你置于工作之下：一旦接下，重量便落在肩头，你必须扛着它站起来。

senses.title: To promise formally
senses.definition: to state formally that you will do something, often in writing or speech
senses.definitionCN: 正式表示将做某事，常以书面或口头形式作出
senses.example: The company undertook to refund every customer within thirty days.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司承诺在三十天内向每位客户退款。
senses.why: Taking on a duty in words is like taking on the work itself: the promise puts the load on you before any real work starts.
senses.whyCN: 用言语接下职责如同接下工作本身：承诺在任何实际工作开始之前就把担子压在你身上。

senses.title: To accept responsibility or obligation
senses.definition: to accept that you are responsible for something, such as a duty, debt, or duty of care
senses.definitionCN: 接受对某事的负责，如职责、债务或注意义务
senses.example: By signing the lease, she undertook responsibility for repairs to the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 签下租约后，她承担起修缮屋顶的责任。
senses.why: Standing under a beam means accepting everything that falls on it; accepting responsibility is agreeing to be that beam.
senses.whyCN: 立于梁下意味着承受一切落在梁上的东西；接受责任就是同意成为那根梁。

senses.title: To engage in an activity
senses.definition: to carry out an activity or course of action, especially a formal or planned one
senses.definitionCN: 进行某项活动或行动方案，尤指正式或有计划的工作
senses.example: The army undertook a review of its training procedures.
senses.exampleCN: 军方对其训练流程进行了一次审查。
senses.why: The compound treats the activity as a standing position: you are under it, and doing it is simply holding that position until it is done.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把活动当作一种站立的姿态：你在它之下，做它就是保持那个姿态直到完成。

senses.title: To accept a risk or burden
senses.definition: to accept the risks, costs, or burdens that come with an action
senses.definitionCN: 接受某一行动所带来的风险、成本或负担
senses.example: Every climber who signs up undertakes the risks of high altitude.
senses.exampleCN: 每位报名的登山者都接受高海拔带来的风险。
senses.why: To be under something is to be exposed to its weight; undertaking a risk is letting that weight stand over you by choice.
senses.whyCN: 在某种东西之下就是暴露于它的重量之中；接受风险就是自愿让那重量悬在自己上方。

senses.title: A journey or venture begun
senses.titleCN: 启程 undertaking：一项已启程的事业
senses.definition: in older or literary use, to set out on a journey or an enterprise
senses.definitionCN: 旧式或文学用法，指开始一段旅程或一项事业
senses.example: They undertook the crossing of the desert at first light.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在天刚亮时踏上穿越沙漠的旅程。
senses.why: A journey undertaken is a burden lifted and carried forward; the word keeps this older image of setting out with a load.
senses.whyCN: 被承担的旅程是被举起并向前背负的担子；这个词保留了「负重启程」的旧意象。

senses.title: To pledge in law or contract
senses.titleCN: 在法律或合同中作出承诺
senses.definition: to give a formal, often binding, assurance, as in an undertaking given to a court
senses.definitionCN: 作出正式且有约束力的保证，如向法院出具的承诺
senses.example: Counsel undertook to hand over the documents by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 律师承诺在周五前移交文件。
senses.why: A legal undertaking is the promise sense fixed in place: standing under the words means they can be enforced against you.
senses.whyCN: 法律上的承诺把「承诺」义项固定下来：立于言辞之下，意味着这些言辞可以对你产生强制力。

senses.title: To take on the management of something
senses.definition: to take charge of arranging or managing something, such as an event or funeral
senses.definitionCN: 负责安排或操办某事，如一场活动或葬礼
senses.example: The school undertook the organization of the whole festival.
senses.exampleCN: 学校承担了整个节日活动的组织工作。
senses.why: Managing is standing beneath the moving parts so they do not fall; the one who holds things up is the one who has undertaken.
senses.whyCN: 管理就是站在各运转部件之下托住它们不让其坠落；托住一切的人正是承担了它的人。

intro.en: Undertake is a pure Old English compound: under plus take, a hand reaching beneath a load to lift it onto the back.
intro.cn: undertake 是纯粹的古英语复合词：under 加 take，像一只手伸到重物之下把它举上背。

items.en: *n̥dher- is reconstructed as 'below, under'; *deh₃- is generally reconstructed as 'to give', the source of take's Germanic ancestor. The deeper origins remain source uncertain.
items.cn: 原始印欧语重构形式 *n̥dher- 表示「在下」；*deh₃- 一般认为表示「给予」，是 take 日耳曼语祖先的来源；更深的来源不确定。

items.en: Old English undertacan meant to take on oneself, to receive, or to catch hold from beneath.
items.cn: 古英语 undertacan 意为「承当于己；接受；从下方抓住」。

items.en: By the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries the verb meant to take upon oneself a duty, a journey, or a venture.
items.cn: 十三至十四世纪时，该动词已表示承担职责、旅程或事业于己身。

items.en: The sense narrowed toward beginning a task and promising to do it; Shakespeare uses undertake for taking charge of an enterprise.
items.cn: 词义逐渐收窄为「着手做某事」与「承诺去做」；莎士比亚即用 undertake 表示接手一项事业。

items.en: One who undertakes any task came, by euphemism in the seventeenth to eighteenth centuries, to name the one who undertakes the dead: the undertaker.
items.cn: 十七至十八世纪间，通过委婉用法，「承接任何事务的人」转而专指「承办丧事的人」：undertaker。

items.en: Today the verb lives in formal registers: projects are undertaken, promises are undertaken, obligations are undertaken.
items.cn: 如今该动词多用于正式语域：项目被承担，承诺被作出，义务被肩负。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the under- compound family; the near-meaning group gathers words for taking on duties and beginning work.
note.cn: 形近组收 under- 复合词族；近义组收承担职责与着手工作类词。

entries.definition: The noun for a task, venture, or formal promise.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事业；任务；（正式）承诺」。

entries.definition: Under plus stand; a sibling compound, but about the mind rather than the hand.
entries.definitionCN: under 加 stand 的姊妹复合词，义为「理解」，关乎心智而非双手。

entries.definition: To experience or endure; the sibling that receives rather than takes.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「经历；承受」，是承接而非主动去拿的姊妹词。

entries.definition: Under one's feet; an adverb compound of the same under- family.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在脚下」，同一 under- 词族的副词性复合词。

entries.definition: A quiet or hidden tone beneath the surface of a voice or colour.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「低调；底色」，指声音或色彩表面之下的暗层。

entries.definition: To take on a duty or role, often without being asked.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承担；就任」，多指主动承接职责或角色。

entries.definition: To bear a burden on your shoulders; vivid and physical.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「肩负」，形象化地表达负重。

entries.definition: To begin a long or important venture; stresses the start.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「着手；开始」，强调重大事业的起点。

entries.definition: To bind yourself to a course of action; stresses firmness.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「承诺投入」，强调坚定不移。

entries.definition: To accept work or responsibility; the everyday, lighter counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「承担；接手」，是更日常的说法。

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the word's own structure and family.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自词形结构与词族的记忆锚点。

normal.en: Under plus take: reach beneath the load and take it onto your back.
normal.cn: under 加 take：伸手到重物之下，把它接到背上。

normal.en: Undertook, undertaken follow the irregular pattern of take, took, taken.
normal.cn: undertook、undertaken 遵循 take→took→taken 的不规则变化模式。

normal.en: An undertaking is both the work you take on and the promise you make.
normal.cn: undertaking 既指你接下的工作，也指你许下的承诺。

normal.en: Understand and undergo are siblings: stand under, go under, take under.
normal.cn: understand 与 undergo 是同族：立于其下、行于其下、接于其下。

normal.en: The undertaker is the one who undertakes the last task of all.
normal.cn: undertaker 是承接最后一项事务的人——殡葬承办人。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge beam resting on your shoulders as you sign your name beneath it.
abstract.cn: 想象桥的横梁压在肩上，你在梁下签下自己的名字。

abstract.en: Signing is undertaking: the ink dries and the weight is yours.
abstract.cn: 签名即承担：墨迹一干，重量便归你所有。

abstract.en: To undertake is to become the beam that others can build on.
abstract.cn: 承担就是成为一根可供他人搭建的梁。

examples.en: The charity undertook to rebuild every damaged school within two years.
examples.cn: 该慈善机构承诺在两年内重建所有受损的学校。

examples.en: She undertook a careful revision of the entire manuscript.
examples.cn: 她对整部手稿进行了一次细致的修订。

examples.en: Who will undertake the responsibility if the project fails?
examples.cn: 如果项目失败，谁来承担责任？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安德忒克」——安（安德）在下面（under）特意（忒）接着（take）：在下面接住重物，即承担

root: 古英语 undertacan「承当于己；从下方抓住」，由 under「在下」加 tacan「抓住、拿取」复合而成；under 溯至原始印欧语重构形式 *n̥dher-「在下」，take 的日耳曼语祖先一般溯至 *deh₃-「给予」（经北欧语传入英语，来源细节存疑）；字面意象「在下接取」一直支撑着「承担」义。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of undertake all begin with one gesture: reaching beneath a load to take it up — a task, a promise, a risk, a responsibility, or a whole venture.
sensesIntro.cn: undertake 的八个义项都始于同一个动作：伸手到重物之下把它接起来——可以是任务、承诺、风险、职责，或整项事业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching under a load and taking it onto the back
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸到重物之下，把它接到背上

branches.en: THE WORK: tasks and activities taken up and carried through.
branches.cn: 工作线：被接起并完成到底的任务与活动。

branches.en: THE WORD: promises and legal pledges that fix the load in place.
branches.cn: 言辞线：把担子固定下来的承诺与法律保证。

branches.en: THE DUTY: responsibility accepted like a beam across the shoulders.
branches.cn: 职责线：如横梁压肩般被接受的责任。

branches.en: THE ROAD: risks accepted and journeys begun under one's own weight.
branches.cn: 道路线：被接受的风险与自行背负启程的旅程。

branches.en: THE HANDOVER: taking charge so nothing falls while it is being arranged.
branches.cn: 操办线：接手管理，让一切在安排过程中不致坠落。

intro.en: Undertake is built from two native Old English words, each still living in English.
intro.cn: undertake 由两个古英语本族词构成，二者至今仍在英语中使用。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, not Latin, so there are no Latin cognates to list; the deep roots are reconstructions.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语源而非拉丁语源，故没有拉丁同族词可列；深层词根属重构形式。

它与 take 构成 mistake。

items.example: It forms forsake with take's root.
items.exampleCN: 它与 take 词根构成 forsake。

items.example: It forms attendance with related verbs.
items.exampleCN: 它与相关动词构成 attendance。

由本词加施动者后缀构成，义为「殡葬承办人」，为词义偏移的特殊用法

definition_zh: 失业的；未被雇用的；未被利用的
definition_en: not having a paid job, or not being used
core_image: 工牌摘下后空着的手，和一张没排上日程的椅子
scene: 工厂大门贴出了歇业通知，人们攥着最后一个月的工资条站在门口。Thousands of workers were left unemployed when the factory closed.
sceneCN: 这里 unemployed 是形容词「失业的」（第 1 个义项：失去有薪工作）；句意为工厂关闭后数千名工人失业。

pos.zh: 失业的；未被雇用的；未被利用的
（the unemployed）失业者（总称）

derivatives.zh: 由本词变 -ed 为 -ment 构成，义为「失业；失业率；失业状态」
去掉否定前缀后的词基，义为「雇用；使用」
由词基加施动者后缀构成，义为「雇主」
由词基加后缀构成，义为「雇员」

senses.title: Without a paid job
senses.definition: not having a job that pays wages or a salary, though able and often willing to work
senses.definitionCN: 没有领取工资或薪金的工作，但有工作能力且通常愿意工作
senses.example: He was unemployed for six months before finding a new post.
senses.exampleCN: 他失业了六个月才找到新职位。
senses.why: The prefix un- turns employ into its opposite: the hand that once held the tool now holds nothing.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 把 employ 翻转为反面：曾经握着工具的手如今空无一物。

senses.title: Temporarily out of work
senses.definition: out of work between jobs, often for a limited period
senses.definitionCN: 处于两份工作之间的待业状态，常为有限时段
senses.example: After graduation she was unemployed for only a few weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业后她只待业了几个星期。
senses.why: Being unemployed is a state, not a character trait: the un- marks a temporary vacancy, not a permanent lack.
senses.whyCN: 失业是一种状态而非本性：un- 标记的是暂时的空缺，而非永久的匮乏。

senses.title: Not being used
senses.definition: not currently being put to use, said of machines, capital, or resources
senses.definitionCN: 未被投入使用，用于机器、资金或资源
senses.example: A large part of the fund sat unemployed in a low-interest account.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔资金的大部分闲置在一个低息账户里。
senses.why: Employ once meant simply to use; anything can be employed, so anything can be unemployed — hands, money, machines.
senses.whyCN: employ 本义只是「使用」；任何东西都可被使用，因此任何东西都可能未被使用——手、资金、机器皆然。

senses.title: Skill or effort left idle
senses.titleCN: 才能或精力未被施展的
senses.definition: not given an outlet or occupation, said of abilities or energy
senses.definitionCN: 才能或精力没有得到施展的用武之地
senses.example: His talent sat unemployed in the small branch office.
senses.exampleCN: 他的才华在小小的分部里无处施展。
senses.why: A skill unexercised is like a tool unemployed: both wait for the hand that will put them back to work.
senses.whyCN: 未被施展的才能如同闲置的工具：二者都在等待那只把它们重新用起来的手。

senses.title: Registered as job-seeking
senses.definition: officially recorded as out of work and seeking employment, as in labour statistics
senses.definitionCN: 在劳动统计中被正式记录为无工作且正在求职
senses.example: She registered as unemployed at the local job centre.
senses.exampleCN: 她在当地就业服务中心登记为失业。
senses.why: The state needs the word to draw a line: not employed, not retired, but actively looking.
senses.whyCN: 统计制度需要这个词划出一条界线：既非在职、也非退休，而是正在积极求职。

senses.title: The unemployed as a group
senses.definition: the unemployed, as a collective noun for all people without work
senses.definitionCN: the unemployed 作集合名词，指所有没有工作的人
senses.example: The marchers included many of the long-term unemployed.
senses.exampleCN: 游行队伍中有许多长期失业者。
senses.why: The adjective stiffens into a noun: the whole class of people defined by the absence of employment.
senses.whyCN: 形容词凝固成名词：整个群体被「没有工作」这一缺席所定义。

senses.title: Seasonal or cyclical idleness
senses.titleCN: 季节性或周期性失业的
senses.definition: out of work because of the season or a business cycle, as in seasonal trades
senses.definitionCN: 因季节或经济周期而无工作，见于季节性行业
senses.example: Dockworkers were seasonally unemployed each winter.
senses.exampleCN: 码头工人每年冬天都会季节性失业。
senses.why: The tide of work goes out and comes back; un-employed names the low water of employment.
senses.whyCN: 工作的潮水会退去也会回来；un-employed 命名的正是雇用潮的低水位。

senses.title: Idle hours or facilities
senses.definition: of time, rooms, or equipment lying unused, as in unemployed hours
senses.definitionCN: 指时间、房间或设备处于闲置状态，如 unemployed hours
senses.example: The unemployed evenings of that winter were filled with chess.
senses.exampleCN: 那年冬天闲置的夜晚都用来下棋。
senses.why: Even time can be employed or unemployed: hours with no occupation stretch like empty factory halls.
senses.whyCN: 连时间也可被「使用」或「闲置」：无所事事的钟点像空置的厂房一样漫长。

intro.en: Unemployed is employ wrapped in the Old English negative un-, with a French body and a Germanic shell.
intro.cn: unemployed 是 employ 加上古英语否定前缀 un-：法语的身躯，日耳曼的外壳。

items.en: Latin implicare meant to enfold or entangle; its participle implicitus and variant implicatus fed the sense of being held or busy.
items.cn: 拉丁语 implicare 意为「包住；缠住」，其分词 implicitus 与变体 implicatus 衍生出「被占用；忙碌」之义。

items.en: Old French employer meant to use, apply, or engage; the Latin root had shifted from entangling to making use of.
items.cn: 古法语 employer 意为「使用；应用；聘用」，拉丁词根由「缠绕」转为「利用」。

items.en: The verb is recorded from the fifteenth century, first for using things and then for hiring people.
items.cn: 动词约自十五世纪有记录，先用于「使用物」，后用于「雇用人」。

items.en: The prefix un-, from Old English un-, attaches negatives to adjectives and participles; it is cognate with Latin in- and Greek a(n)-.
items.cn: 前缀 un- 来自古英语，加在形容词与分词前构成否定；它与拉丁语 in-、希腊语 a(n)- 同源。

items.en: The participle unemployed is recorded from the late sixteenth century, at first also for unused things.
items.cn: 分词 unemployed 约自十六世纪末有记录，最初也可指「未被使用之物」。

items.en: Unemployment followed as the abstract noun, and the pair now anchors the vocabulary of labour statistics.
items.cn: 抽象名词 unemployment 随之出现，这对词如今是劳动统计词汇的基石。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the employ family and un- counterparts; the near-meaning group gathers words for being without work.
note.cn: 形近组收 employ 词族与 un- 对应词；近义组收「没有工作」类词。

entries.definition: The abstract noun for the state of being unemployed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「失业；失业率；失业状态」。

entries.definition: The positive participle: having a job.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「受雇的；有工作的」，为本词的正面形式。

entries.definition: The person hired; the ee- receives the action.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「雇员」，后缀 -ee 表示动作的接受方。

entries.definition: The person or company that hires; the er- gives the action.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「雇主」，后缀 -er 表示动作的发出方。

entries.definition: To put into position; shares the Old French ending but not the Latin root, only similar in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「部署；调配」，与 employ 词根不同只是拼写相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: Without a job; more informal and direct.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无工作的」，语气更口语、更直接。

entries.definition: A phrase with the same meaning, common in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「失业的」，日常口语常用。

entries.definition: Not working or in use; broader, covering machines and time as well.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「闲置的；空闲的」，适用面更广，也指机器与时间。

entries.definition: Losing a job because the post itself is no longer needed, chiefly British.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「（因岗位撤销而）被裁员的」，多用于英式英语。

entries.definition: The verb for ending someone's employment for economic reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「裁员；暂时解雇」，强调因经济原因终止雇用。

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the prefix, the root, and the family.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自前缀、词根与词族的记忆锚点。

normal.en: Un- plus employed: the employed hand is full, the unemployed hand is empty.
normal.cn: un- 加 employed：受雇的手是满的，失业的手是空的。

normal.en: Employ is French-faced but means simply to use: hands, people, money.
normal.cn: employ 面孔像法语词，但本义只是「使用」：用手、用人、用钱。

normal.en: Employee receives the job (-ee), employer gives it (-er).
normal.cn: employee 接收工作（-ee），employer 发出工作（-er）。

normal.en: Unemployment is the state; unemployed is the person in that state.
normal.cn: unemployment 是状态，unemployed 是处于该状态的人。

normal.en: Deploy looks like employ but only deploys, it does not hire.
normal.cn: deploy 拼写像 employ，但只「部署」，不「雇用」。

abstract.en: Picture an empty badge hook beside a full one on the factory wall.
abstract.cn: 想象工厂墙上，一个空着的工牌挂钩旁边是一个满着的挂钩。

abstract.en: Un- is a hand that unclenches: what was held falls away.
abstract.cn: un- 是一只松开的手：原本握住的东西就此脱落。

abstract.en: Being unemployed is a pause between two beats of work, not the end of the song.
abstract.cn: 失业是两个工作节拍之间的休止，而非乐曲的终结。

examples.en: The closure left nearly two hundred workers unemployed.
examples.cn: 工厂关闭使近两百名工人失业。

examples.en: Long-term unemployed people often need more than training to return to work.
examples.cn: 长期失业者重返职场往往需要的不仅是培训。

examples.en: The report measured unemployment among graduates for the first time.
examples.cn: 该报告首次统计了毕业生的失业情况。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安·因普洛伊德」——安（un 不）因普洛伊（employ 雇用）不成，德（ed）没人雇：失业

root: employ 经由古法语 employer「使用；聘用」溯至拉丁语 implicare「包住；缠住」（其分词形式衍生出「被占用」之义）；否定前缀 un- 来自古英语，与拉丁语 in- 同源，加于分词前构成否定；unemployed 即「未被雇用的」，词义随 employ 从「使用」收窄到「雇用」。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of unemployed fan out from one empty space: hands without a job, machines without a task, money without a purpose, hours without an occupation.
sensesIntro.cn: unemployed 的八个义项从同一片空白展开：没有工作的手、没有任务的机器、没有用途的资金、没有事做的钟点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty badge hook where a working hand used to hang its card
core.cn: 核心意象：原本挂着工牌的挂钩如今空着

branches.en: THE PERSON: jobless, between jobs, and registered as seeking.
branches.cn: 个人线：没有工作、待业在两职之间、登记求职。

branches.en: THE THINGS: machines, money and hours left idle.
branches.cn: 器物线：闲置的机器、资金与时间。

branches.en: THE TALENT: skills with no outlet to work through.
branches.cn: 才能线：无处施展的技能。

branches.en: THE GROUP: a class of people defined by absence of work.
branches.cn: 群体线：被「无工作」定义的一类人。

branches.en: THE TIDE: seasonal and cyclical lows in employment.
branches.cn: 潮汐线：季节性与周期性的雇用低谷。

intro.en: Unemployed shows a Germanic prefix clipped onto a French verb, a very common English pattern.
intro.cn: unemployed 展示了日耳曼前缀接在法语动词上的组合，这是英语中极常见的模式。

latinIntro.en: The deep root is Latin implicare; cognates show the fold-and-use shift.
latinIntro.cn: 深层词根是拉丁语 implicare；同族词展示了「缠绕→使用」的语义转移。

items.example: It forms implicate with the Latin root.
items.exampleCN: 它与拉丁词根构成 implicate。

latinEntries.example: The ancestor of employ and imply.
latinEntries.exampleCN: employ 与 imply 的祖先。

latinEntries.example: It forms apply via Old French aplier.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 经由古法语 aplier 构成 apply。

由词基加施动者后缀构成，义为「雇主」
由词基加后缀构成，义为「雇员」

definition_zh: 失业；失业状态；失业率；失业人数
definition_en: the state of not having a paid job, or the number or rate of people in that state
core_image: 就业大门前一条越排越长的队伍
scene: 经济下行时，就业中心门口的队伍从街角排到了邮局。Unemployment rose sharply in the region last winter.
sceneCN: 这里 unemployment 是名词「失业；失业率」（第 1 个义项：无工作的状态）；句意为去年冬天该地区失业率急剧上升。

pos.zh: 失业；失业状态
失业率；失业人数（统计义）

derivatives.zh: 由名词 -ment 换为形容词分词 -ed 构成，义为「失业的」
去掉否定前缀后的词基名词，义为「就业；雇用」
词基动词，义为「雇用；使用」

senses.title: The state of having no job
senses.definition: the condition of not having a paid job while being available for work
senses.definitionCN: 没有有薪工作但可参加工作的一种状态
senses.example: Two years of unemployment taught him to budget carefully.
senses.exampleCN: 两年的失业生活教会了他精打细算。
senses.why: The suffix -ment turns the negative participle into a thing: the absence of employment becomes a state you can be inside.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 把否定分词变成一件「东西」：雇用的缺席成了一种人可以身处其中的状态。

senses.title: The number of people without work
senses.definition: the total count of people who are without work, as a statistic
senses.definitionCN: 没有工作的人的总数，作为一项统计数字
senses.example: Unemployment fell by ten thousand this quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 本季度失业人数减少了一万。
senses.why: A state can be counted by counting the people in it; the word slides from condition to headcount.
senses.whyCN: 状态可以通过清点其中的人数来计量；这个词便从「状况」滑向「人数」。

senses.title: The unemployment rate
senses.definition: the percentage of the labour force without work, as in the unemployment rate
senses.definitionCN: 劳动力中无工作者的百分比，如失业率
senses.example: The unemployment rate inched up to six point two percent.
senses.exampleCN: 失业率微升至百分之六点二。
senses.why: Economists prefer ratios to headcounts; the same word now names the measure as well as the state.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家偏好比率而非绝对人数；同一个词于是又承担了「度量」之义。

senses.title: Idleness of resources
senses.definition: the state of land, capital, or machines not being used
senses.definitionCN: 土地、资金或机器未被使用的状态
senses.example: The report also measured unemployment of farmland in the district.
senses.exampleCN: 该报告还统计了区内农田的闲置情况。
senses.why: Since employ means to use, unemployment can name any unused thing, not only unused people.
senses.whyCN: 既然 employ 本义是「使用」，unemployment 就可指任何未被使用之物，而不只是未被雇用的人。

senses.title: Long-term joblessness
senses.definition: prolonged joblessness lasting months or years, as in long-term unemployment
senses.definitionCN: 持续数月或数年的长期无工作状态，如长期失业
senses.example: Long-term unemployment erodes both skills and confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 长期失业会消磨技能，也会消磨信心。
senses.why: A temporary gap hardens into a condition; the noun carries the weight of time spent outside work.
senses.whyCN: 暂时的空缺会硬化为一种处境；这个名词承载着工作之外流逝的时间之重。

senses.title: Seasonal joblessness
senses.definition: joblessness caused by the seasons of a trade, as in seasonal unemployment
senses.definitionCN: 由行业季节引起的失业，如季节性失业
senses.example: Seasonal unemployment peaks in the quiet winter months.
senses.exampleCN: 季节性失业在淡季的冬季达到高峰。
senses.why: Work has tides; the word marks the low water that returns with the calendar.
senses.whyCN: 工作有潮汐；这个词标记着随日历周期性回落的低水位。

senses.title: Structural joblessness
senses.definition: joblessness caused by changes in an economy rather than a downturn, as in structural unemployment
senses.definitionCN: 由经济结构变化而非经济衰退引起的失业，如结构性失业
senses.example: Automation created structural unemployment in the coalfields.
senses.exampleCN: 自动化在煤田地区造成了结构性失业。
senses.why: When the jobs themselves vanish rather than the demand, the absence is built into the structure of work.
senses.whyCN: 当消失的是岗位本身而非需求时，「缺席」便被建造进了工作结构之中。

senses.title: A social and political problem
senses.definition: joblessness treated as a public issue to be fought or reduced, as in fighting unemployment
senses.definitionCN: 被视为需治理或降低的公共问题的失业，如「治理失业」
senses.example: The government promised to fight unemployment with new training schemes.
senses.exampleCN: 政府承诺以新的培训计划来治理失业。
senses.why: Once counted, a state becomes an enemy: societies name the problem so they can act on it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦被计量，状态便成了敌人：社会给问题命名，是为了能够对它采取行动。

intro.en: Unemployment stacks three layers: a Latin root, a French verb, and an Old English negative prefix.
intro.cn: unemployment 叠了三层：拉丁词根、法语动词、古英语否定前缀。

items.en: Latin implicare meant to enfold or entangle; its participle gave the sense of being held or busy.
items.cn: 拉丁语 implicare 意为「包住；缠住」，其分词形式衍生出「被占用；忙碌」之义。

items.en: Old French employer meant to use, apply, or engage.
items.cn: 古法语 employer 意为「使用；应用；聘用」。

items.en: The verb entered English in the fifteenth century; employment followed as its noun.
items.cn: 动词于十五世纪进入英语，其名词 employment 随之出现。

items.en: The negative prefix un- is native Old English, cognate with Latin in- and Greek a(n)-.
items.cn: 否定前缀 un- 是古英语本族成分，与拉丁语 in-、希腊语 a(n)- 同源。

items.en: The noun unemployment is recorded from the late nineteenth century, when labour statistics demanded an abstract term.
items.cn: 名词 unemployment 约自十九世纪末有记录，当时劳动统计需要这样一个抽象名词。

items.en: Today unemployment is an economic indicator as much as a personal condition.
items.cn: 如今 unemployment 既是个人处境，也是一项经济指标。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the employ family and un- counterparts; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for joblessness and idleness.
note.cn: 形近组收 employ 词族与 un- 对应词；近义组收失业与闲置类名词。

entries.definition: The adjective for a person in this state.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指处于失业状态的人。

entries.definition: The positive noun: having work or hiring people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「就业；雇用」，为本词的正面形式。

entries.definition: The base verb: to use or to hire.
entries.definitionCN: 词基动词，义为「使用；雇用」。

entries.definition: The American term for payments to the jobless.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，美式说法，指付给失业者的救济金。

entries.definition: Putting forces or systems into position; shares the -ment ending but not the Latin root, only similar in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部署」，与 unemployment 词根无关只是拼写相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: The state of having no job; plainer and more direct.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「无工作状态」，措辞更朴素直接。

entries.definition: The state of not working; broader, covering machines and time.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「闲置；空闲」，适用面更广，也指机器与时间。

entries.definition: The British term for losing a job because the post is cut.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式用语，指因岗位撤销而被裁员。

entries.definition: The act of ending employment for economic reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「裁员；暂时解雇」，强调经济原因。

entries.definition: Periods when machines or systems are not working.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「停机时间」，指机器或系统停止运转的时段。

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the layered structure of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自词语分层结构的记忆锚点。

normal.en: Un- + employ + -ment: not + use/hire + state.
normal.cn: un- 加 employ 加 -ment：不 + 使用/雇用 + 状态。

normal.en: Employment is the door; unemployment is standing outside it.
normal.cn: employment 是那扇门，unemployment 是站在门外。

normal.en: Unemployed describes the person; unemployment describes the state or the number.
normal.cn: unemployed 形容人，unemployment 形容状态或数字。

normal.en: Employ is one syllable shorter than employee and employer.
normal.cn: employ 比 employee、employer 都短一个音节，是词族的根。

normal.en: The -ment family: employment, unemployment, entertainment, government.
normal.cn: -ment 词族：employment、unemployment、entertainment、government。

abstract.en: Picture a queue outside an employment office growing longer each winter.
abstract.cn: 想象就业中心门外的队伍，每个冬天都在变长。

abstract.en: Un- flips the sign on the board: hiring becomes not hiring.
abstract.cn: un- 翻转了公告牌上的符号：「招聘」变成了「不招聘」。

abstract.en: A rate is the queue made into a number on a chart.
abstract.cn: 「率」就是那条队伍变成图表上的一个数字。

examples.en: Unemployment among young workers has doubled in five years.
examples.cn: 五年来青年工人的失业人数翻了一番。

examples.en: She received unemployment benefits while retraining as a nurse.
examples.cn: 她在接受护士再培训期间领取失业救济金。

examples.en: The scheme aims to cut unemployment in the former mining towns.
examples.cn: 该计划旨在降低前矿业城镇的失业率。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安·因普洛伊门特」——安（un 不）因普洛伊（employ 雇用）的门（ment）关上了：失业这道门

root: unemployment 由古英语否定前缀 un- 加 employment 构成；employment 经古法语 employer「使用；聘用」溯至拉丁语 implicare「包住；缠住」（分词形式衍生「被占用」之义）；un- 与拉丁语 in-、希腊语 a(n)- 同源；名词形式在十九世纪末随劳动统计制度兴起而定型。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of unemployment move from a personal condition outward: one person's empty hands become a headcount, a rate, a tide, a structure, and finally a problem a whole society must fight.
sensesIntro.cn: unemployment 的八个义项由个人处境向外扩展：一个人空着的双手，变成人数、比率、潮汐、结构，最终成为全社会必须应对的问题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a queue outside the employment office door
core.cn: 核心意象：就业中心门外排起的队伍

branches.en: THE STATE: joblessness as a condition, short or long.
branches.cn: 状态线：作为处境的失业，或短或长。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: headcounts and rates on the economist's chart.
branches.cn: 数字线：经济学家图表上的人数与比率。

branches.en: THE THINGS: land, capital and machines left unused.
branches.cn: 器物线：未被使用的土地、资金与机器。

branches.en: THE TIDES: seasonal lows and structural shifts in work.
branches.cn: 潮汐线：工作的季节性低谷与结构性变动。

branches.en: THE FIGHT: joblessness named as a problem societies act on.
branches.cn: 治理线：被命名为公共问题的失业。

intro.en: Unemployment is a three-layer construction: native prefix, French verb, Latin root.
intro.cn: unemployment 是三层结构：本族前缀、法语动词、拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: The deep root is Latin implicare; its family shows the fold-and-use shift.
latinIntro.cn: 深层词根是拉丁语 implicare；其词族展示了「缠绕→使用」的语义转移。

items.example: It forms implicate with the Latin root.
items.exampleCN: 它与拉丁词根构成 implicate。

latinEntries.example: The ancestor of employ and imply.
latinEntries.exampleCN: employ 与 imply 的祖先。

latinEntries.example: It forms apply via Old French aplier.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 经由古法语 aplier 构成 apply。

去掉否定前缀后的词基名词，义为「就业；雇用」
词基动词，义为「雇用；使用」

definition_zh: 不公平的；不公正的；偏袒的；违反规则的
definition_en: not fair, not based on equal treatment or on what is right or just
core_image: 一架秤，一边被悄悄压上了看不见的砝码
scene: 两条跑道一湿一干，起跑线前孩子们皱起了眉头。It seemed unfair that one lane was dry and the other was soaked.
sceneCN: 这里 unfair 是形容词「不公平的」（第 1 个义项：待遇不平等）；句意为一条跑道干一条湿，这看起来不公平。

pos.zh: 不公平的；不公正的；偏袒的
违反规则或道德的；不正当的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「不公平地；不公正地」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「不公平；不公正」
去掉否定前缀后的词基，义为「公平的；公正的」

senses.title: Not equal in treatment
senses.definition: treating people unequally when they should be treated the same
senses.definitionCN: 本应一视同仁时却区别对待
senses.example: It is unfair to judge two applicants by different standards.
senses.exampleCN: 用不同标准评判两位申请者是不公平的。
senses.why: Fair once meant beautiful and then levelled into even-handed; un- simply lifts the level out from under the scale.
senses.whyCN: fair 由「美丽」演化为「持平均匀」；un- 只是把秤下的水平面抽走。

senses.title: Not just or right
senses.definition: contrary to justice or to what is morally right
senses.definitionCN: 与正义或道德上正当之事相悖
senses.example: Punishing the whole class for one pupil's mistake was unfair.
senses.exampleCN: 因一名学生的过错惩罚全班是不公正的。
senses.why: A fair judgement weighs blame against deed; when the weights are wrong, the sentence itself tilts.
senses.whyCN: 公正的判决让过错与惩罚相称；砝码一旦放错，判决本身便倾斜了。

senses.title: Showing favouritism
senses.definition: favouring one side or person without good reason
senses.definitionCN: 没有正当理由地偏袒一方或某人
senses.example: The referee's unfair favouritism spoiled the whole match.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判不公的偏袒毁了整场比赛。
senses.why: A level field lets skill decide; favouritism is a hidden thumb on the scale.
senses.whyCN: 平整的场地让技艺决定胜负；偏袒是压在秤上的隐形拇指。

senses.title: Breaking the rules of a game
senses.definition: not allowed by the rules of a game or contest
senses.definitionCN: 为比赛或竞赛规则所不允许的
senses.example: It is unfair to start before the whistle blows.
senses.exampleCN: 哨声未响就抢先起跑是不合规则的。
senses.why: Games are fairness made visible: the rules are the level ground, and unfair play digs a hole in it.
senses.whyCN: 游戏是把公平变得可见的形式：规则就是平地，违规行为就是在平地上挖坑。

senses.title: Taking undue advantage
senses.definition: gaining an advantage by methods that equal rivals do not have
senses.definitionCN: 用对手无法享有的手段获取优势
senses.example: Using the leaked answers gave the team an unfair advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 使用泄露的答案让该队占了不公平的便宜。
senses.why: Advantage is fair when every runner starts at the same line; a head start no one else has is unfairness in inches.
senses.whyCN: 当每位跑者都站在同一条起跑线上时优势才是公平的；他人没有的先手就是以寸计的不公。

senses.title: Commercially improper
senses.definition: breaching accepted standards of business conduct, as in unfair competition
senses.definitionCN: 违背公认商业行为准则，如不正当竞争
senses.example: The court found the firm guilty of unfair competition.
senses.exampleCN: 法院判定该公司存在不正当竞争行为。
senses.why: Markets promise a fair ring: no tricks, no rigged weights; unfair practice is a weight palmed in the open square.
senses.whyCN: 市场承诺公平的交易：不耍花招、不压秤；不正当行为就是众目睽睽之下掌心藏着的砝码。

senses.title: Unjust criticism or blame
senses.definition: criticism or blame that does not match what was actually done
senses.definitionCN: 与实际所为不相称的批评或指责
senses.example: The paper later admitted its unfair attack on the young author.
senses.exampleCN: 该报后来承认对那位年轻作者的攻击有失公允。
senses.why: Blame should weigh the deed, not the mood; an unfair accusation loads the scale with what never happened.
senses.whyCN: 指责应当衡量行为而非情绪；不公正的指控是往秤上放从未发生之事的砝码。

senses.title: In law: procedurally wrong
senses.definition: failing the required standards of a legal process, as in unfair dismissal or unfair trial
senses.definitionCN: 未达到法律程序要求的正当标准，如不公平解雇、审判不公
senses.example: The tribunal ruled the dismissal unfair and ordered compensation.
senses.exampleCN: 裁定机构认定解雇不公，判令给予补偿。
senses.why: Law formalises the scale: procedures are the pivot, and unfair procedure moves the pivot itself.
senses.whyCN: 法律把秤制度化：程序是支点，程序不公移动的正是支点本身。

intro.en: Unfair is the Old English pair fair plus un-, both layers native to English.
intro.cn: unfair 由 fair 加古英语前缀 un- 构成，两个层次都是英语本族成分。

items.en: *peh₂- is generally reconstructed as a root meaning the same in Old English and Old Saxon; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语重构词根 *peh₂- 在古英语与古撒克逊语中同义；更深的来源不确定。

items.en: Old English fæge meant beautiful, pleasant, or fated to die; the modern senses of beautiful and fair-haired descend from it.
items.cn: 古英语 fæge 意为「美丽的；宜人的；注定一死的」，现代「美丽」「金发白皙」诸义皆源于此。

items.en: By the thirteenth century fair had widened to clean, unblemished, lawful, and then even-handed in judgement.
items.cn: 十三世纪时 fair 已扩展为「洁净的；无瑕的；合法的」，进而表示「评判持中的」。

items.en: The prefix un- is native Old English, cognate with Latin in- and Greek a(n)-, and attaches freely to adjectives.
items.cn: 前缀 un- 是古英语本族成分，与拉丁语 in-、希腊语 a(n)- 同源，可自由加于形容词前。

items.en: Unfair is recorded from Old English times in the sense not beautiful, and from Middle English in the modern sense not just.
items.cn: unfair 早在古英语时期已有记录，义为「不美的」；现代「不公」义自中古英语时期确立。

items.en: The word now anchors the vocabulary of justice: unfair treatment, unfair dismissal, unfair competition.
items.cn: 如今该词是正义词汇的基石：不公平对待、不公平解雇、不正当竞争。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the fair family and un- counterparts; the near-meaning group gathers words for injustice and bias.
note.cn: 形近组收 fair 词族与 un- 对应词；近义组收不义与偏颇类词。

entries.definition: The positive base: just, even-handed, or blonde.
entries.definitionCN: 正面词基，义为「公平的；公正的；（发色）浅淡的」。

entries.definition: The adverb: justly, or simply quite.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「公正地」，也可弱化为「相当」。

entries.definition: The adverb of this entry: in an unjust way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「不公平地」。

entries.definition: To get on, or a transport charge; same sound but a different word and origin, only similar in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「进展；车费」，与 fair 同音但来源不同，只是音同形近。

entries.definition: Not suitable; built with the same un- prefix on a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不合适的」，用同一 un- 前缀加于另一词根。

entries.definition: Contrary to justice; more formal and legal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不公正的」，语气更正式、更书面。

entries.definition: Leaning to one side in judgement; stresses the tilt itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有偏见的」，强调倾斜本身。

entries.definition: Favouring one side; the opposite of impartial.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「偏袒的」，与 impartial 相对。

entries.definition: Not equitable; formal, used of distributions and arrangements.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不公平的」，正式用语，多指分配与安排。

entries.definition: Favouring only one view or party; everyday and vivid.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「片面的；一边倒的」，日常且形象。

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the prefix, the base, and the sound-alikes.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自前缀、词基与同音词的记忆锚点。

normal.en: Un- + fair: fair is the level scale, unfair is the loaded one.
normal.cn: un- 加 fair：fair 是持平的秤，unfair 是被压了的秤。

normal.en: Fair itself meant beautiful first, then clean, then just.
normal.cn: fair 本义先是「美丽」，再是「洁净」，后是「公正」。

normal.en: Fair and fare sound the same but fare only travels and pays.
normal.cn: fair 与 fare 同音，但 fare 只管出行与车费。

normal.en: The un- family: unhappy, unfair, unfit, unable.
normal.cn: un- 词族：unhappy、unfair、unfit、unable。

normal.en: Unfairly tells how, unfairness names the thing.
normal.cn: unfairly 说明方式，unfairness 给不公命名。

abstract.en: Picture a balance scale with one pan secretly heavier.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，其中一侧托盘被悄悄加重了。

abstract.en: Un- tilts the level field until the ball rolls to one side.
abstract.cn: un- 把平整的场地一端抬起，球便滚向一侧。

abstract.en: Fairness is everyone's shoes on the same starting line.
abstract.cn: 公平就是所有人的鞋都落在同一条起跑线上。

examples.en: Changing the rules halfway through is unfair to every player.
examples.cn: 比赛进行到一半改规则，对每位选手都不公平。

examples.en: She complained of unfair treatment at work and won her case.
examples.cn: 她投诉在工作中受到不公平对待并胜诉。

examples.en: Critics called the tax unfair to small businesses.
examples.cn: 批评者称这项税对小企业不公平。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安·费尔」——安（un 不）费尔（fair 公平）：不安逸的公平，即不公

root: unfair 由古英语否定前缀 un- 加 fair 构成；fair 溯自古英语 fæge「美丽的；注定一死的」，一般上溯至原始印欧语重构词根 *peh₂-（更早来源不确定）；词义由「美丽」经「洁净、合法」演化为「持中、公正」；un- 与拉丁语 in-、希腊语 a(n)- 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of unfair all break one image: the level scale. Unequal treatment, favouritism, rule-breaking, undue advantage, bad procedure — each is a thumb pressed on one pan.
sensesIntro.cn: unfair 的八个义项都在破坏同一意象：那架持平的秤。不平等对待、偏袒、违规、不当优势、程序失当——每一条都是压在秤盘上的拇指。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance scale with a hidden weight on one pan
core.cn: 核心意象：一架秤，一侧托盘藏着看不见的砝码

branches.en: THE SCALE: unequal treatment, wrong weights, and favouritism.
branches.cn: 天平线：不平等对待、放错的砝码与偏袒。

branches.en: THE GAME: broken rules and advantages no rival shares.
branches.cn: 赛场线：被打破的规则与对手没有的优势。

branches.en: THE MARKET: improper conduct in the fair ring of trade.
branches.cn: 市场线：公平交易圈中的不正当行为。

branches.en: THE WORDS: blame that outweighs the deed.
branches.cn: 言辞线：重过行为本身的指责。

branches.en: THE COURT: procedures whose pivot itself has moved.
branches.cn: 法庭线：支点本身已移动的程序。

intro.en: Unfair shows the most productive negative pattern in English: un- on a native adjective.
intro.cn: unfair 展示了英语中最能产的否定模式：un- 加于本族形容词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Germanic, not Latin, so there are no Latin cognates to list; the deep root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 词基属日耳曼语源而非拉丁语源，故没有拉丁同族词可列；深层词根属重构形式。

items.exampleCN: 它与 partial 构成 impartial。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「不公平地；不公正地」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「不公平；不公正」
去掉否定前缀后的词基，义为「公平的；公正的」
